Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 13, verse 1

We have already spoken at length, in our reflections (khawatir), about the letters with which some surahs of the Noble Qur'an begin, such as His words, the Truth: ﴿Alif Lam Mim﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah), and His words: ﴿Alif Lam Mim Ra﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd), and such as His words: ﴿Alif Lam Mim Sad﴾ (Surat al-A'raf), and other tawqifi letters (letters whose meaning is fixed by revelation, tawqif) that came at the beginning of some of the opening letters of the surahs. But what I wish to emphasize here is that the verses of the Qur'an are all built on wasl (continuous joining), not on waqf (pausing). That is why you find them vocalized (mashkul), because they are joined to what follows them.

Had we applied this rule, we would have read "Mim Ra" (المر) by pronouncing it: "alif", "lam", "mim", "ra". But it pleased the Truth, glorified is He, that these letters at the beginning of Surat al-Ra'd should come built on waqf, so we say: "alif", "lam", "mim", "ra". Thus Jibril (peace be upon him) recited them to Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah (ﷺ), and thus we recite them. He, glorified is He, continues:

﴿These are the verses of the Book.﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd)

That is: the surah that has come to you is among the verses of the Noble Book, the Qur'an, and it is in addition to what was sent down to you before. The Book as a whole includes everything from the beginning, ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾ (Surat al-Fatiha), to the beginning of the Qur'an, until the end of Surat al-Nas.

We know that the idafa (genitive construction, idafa) comes with three meanings. Sometimes the idafa carries the meaning of "min" (of/from), as in our saying "ardabb qamh" (an ardabb of wheat), meaning an ardabb of wheat. Sometimes the idafa carries the meaning of "fi" (in), as in our saying "madhakarat al-manzil" (studying at home), meaning studying in the house. A third time the idafa carries the meaning of "li" (for/belonging to), and it takes two forms.

It may be an expression of ownership, as in our saying "mal Zayd li-Zayd" (Zayd's wealth belongs to Zayd). The second form is that the lam is for exclusivity (ikhtisas), as in our saying "lijam al-faras" (the bridle of the horse), meaning that the bridle is specific to the horse, for it is not reasonable that a horse should own a bridle. So, the words of the Truth, glorified is He, here:

﴿These are the verses of the Book.﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd)

mean: these are verses from the Qur'an, because the word "al-Kitab" (the Book), when used without qualification, refers to the Noble Qur'an. And the mithl (exemplary usage) is the saying "Fulan al-rajul" (so-and-so is the man), meaning that he is truly a man, as though his conduct is the standard of manhood, and as though the qualities of manhood in others are not complete as they are in him. Or like your saying "Fulan al-sha'ir" (so-and-so is the poet), meaning that he is an outstanding poet.

Thus we know that when the word "al-Kitab" is used without qualification, in matters of creed it refers to the Noble Qur'an, and when the word "al-Kitab" is used without qualification in grammar, it refers to the book of Sibawayh, which contains the rules of grammar. He, glorified is He, continues describing the Noble Qur'an:

﴿And that which has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth, but most people do not believe.﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd)

We know that the intention of one who opposes the truth is to gain some splendor from that opposition. And He, glorified is He, said at the end of Surat Yusuf:

﴿And most of mankind, even if you should strive, will not be believers.﴾ (Surat Yusuf 12:103)

Then He described the Noble Qur'an, saying, exalted is He:

﴿It was not a narration invented, but a confirmation of what was before it and a detailed explanation of all things and a guidance and mercy for a people who believe.﴾ (Surat Yusuf 12:111)

Thus we see that the Truth, glorified is He, does not seek gain from you, but He willed to send down this Book so that you may gain: ﴿But most people do not believe﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd). That is: most of those whom you call to belief in this true Book do not believe that it was sent down to you from your Lord, because they did not properly reflect on what it contains, and they submitted to their desires. They wanted worldly authority, and did not turn to the fact that what has come in this Book is what gives them the good of this world and the Hereafter.

And the word "Allah" is a proper name for the Necessary Existent (wajib al-wujud), in which all the attributes of perfection are contained. The moment you say "Allah," it is as if you have said "the Able," "the Harmful," "the Beneficent," "the All-Hearing," "the All-Seeing," "the Giver," and so on through the rest of God's Most Beautiful Names.

For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Every work that does not begin with the name of Allah is abtar (deficient, cut off)."

This is because every work that does not begin with His name, glory be to Him, does not bring to mind that He has subjected all things to you, and that you did not subject things by your own power. Therefore the believer is the one who enters upon any work with the formula "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate," because He, glory be to Him, is the One who made everything submissive to man. Had He not made them submissive, they would not have responded to you, O man.

The True One, glory be to Him, has clarified this through simple examples. We see a small child take a rope and tie it around the neck of a camel, and command it to kneel and lower itself onto its four legs, and the camel obeys. We see the tiny flea that keeps a person awake all night when it creeps into his clothes, and that person exerts tremendous effort to catch it; he may succeed, and he may not.

Thus we know that no one has subjected anything by his own will or desire. Rather, the True One, glory be to Him, is the One who makes all creatures submissive for the service of man. The True One, glory be to Him, said:

﴿And We have subjected them to them; so some of them they ride, and some of them they eat.﴾ (Surah Ya-Sin, 72)

When you undertake any work that requires power, you say: "In the name of the Able who has given me some power." If you undertake a work that requires money, you say: "In the name of the Rich who has granted me some wealth with which to meet my need."

In every work you undertake, you need power, wisdom, wealth, and expansion (bast), and other attributes of the Truth by which He, glory be to Him, subjects everything to you. So His mercy, glory be to Him, willed to make it easy for us to begin any work with His name, which encompasses all attributes of beauty and perfection: "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate." For this reason they call it a proper name for the Necessary Existent. The rest of the Most Beautiful Names are attributes that exist in their absolute perfection only in Him, and so they have become like a proper name.

So "the Mighty" in its absolute sense is Allah. We say of a man, "the mighty of his people" ('aziz qawmihi), and we say "the Rich" in its absolute sense is Allah, but we say "so-and-so is rich" and "so-and-so is poor." Thus we see that these are attributes that have taken the rank of names; when they are used absolutely, they refer to Him, glory be to Him.

We have already learned that the names of Allah are either names of essence (dhat) or names of attributes (sifat). If a name has no counterpart, it is a name of essence, such as "the Mighty" ('Aziz). But if the name is an attribute of action, such as "the Bestower of Honor" (al-Mu'izz), then it must have a counterpart, which here is "the Humiliator" (al-Mudhill).

If He were able only to exalt and not able to humiliate, He would not be God. If He were able only to harm and did not benefit anyone, He could not be God. If He were able to extend (provision) but not able to restrict, He could not be God.

All of these are attributes that have counterparts, and their effect appears in others. So, glory be to Him, for example, He is Mighty in His essence, and He exalts others and humiliates others. The word "Allah" is the name that encompasses all attributes of perfection. There are other names that God taught to some of His creation, and there are third names that we will come to know, if God wills, when we meet Him:

﴿Faces that day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord.﴾ (Surah al-Qiyamah, 22–23)

We note that the True One, glory be to Him, began this verse by speaking of the upper world first and did not speak of the earth. He said:

﴿Allah is the One who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see.... ﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 2)

The word "raised" (rafa'a), when used in human usage, indicates that something was in a position and you lifted it from its place upward, as in the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him:

﴿And he raised his parents upon the throne....﴾ (Surah Yusuf, 100)

Yusuf's parents were in a lower place, and then Yusuf raised them to a higher place than where they had been. So was the sky placed in a lower position and then Allah raised it? No, rather Allah created it raised.

Our shaykh 'Abd al-Jalil 'Isa said: "If you say, 'Glory be to Allah who made the elephant large,' was the elephant small and then God made it large, or did He create it large? He created it large. And if you say, 'Glory be to Allah who made the gnat small,' was it large and then God made it small? No, rather Allah created it small." When He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Allah is the One who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see....﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 2)

this means that He created them raised. In human custom we know that what is raised must have pillars beneath it to hold it up. But the creation of Allah is different: we see the sky raised across the horizon, and it appears to us that the sky meets the earth, but in reality it does not meet it.

We have never found a person walking in any direction who collides with pillars, or with a single pillar that he thinks is one of the pillars holding up the sky, since it appears in this way. So are there invisible pillars, or are there no pillars at all?

This raising may have another matter behind it. We have said that when a thing is raised, that is because of something that holds it or carries it. He, glory be to Him, says regarding the raising of the sky:

﴿And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission. Indeed Allah is to people Kind and Merciful.﴾ (Surah al-Hajj, 65)

If it is held from above, it does not need pillars. His saying, "He holds" (yumsik), means that He, glory be to Him, has set for it its own laws, which we have not yet come to know.

Contemporary scientists have surveyed the earth and space by means of artificial satellites and other means, and they have not found pillars raising the heavens or holding them.

Engineers in our age compete to raise ceilings without pillars, but until now they still depend on load-bearing walls.

Thus we know that He, glory be to Him, either carried the sky on pillars more subtle and finer than our eyes can see, which is why we see it without pillars, or it is raised without pillars at all.

"'Umud" (pillars) is a collective noun (ism jam'), not a plural, and its singular is "'amud" or "'imad." This verse comes as an explanation of what was stated in summary in the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him, in Surah Yusuf:

﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth they pass by, while they turn away from it.﴾ (Surah Yusuf, 105)

He, glory be to Him, here gave the detail, and clarified that He:

﴿raised the heavens without pillars that you see....﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 2)

meaning, you do not see them, by the rule of your sight. Do not be surprised that there exists a creature you do not see, because the eye is one means of perception and has its own law: it sees some things and does not see others. The proof of this is that if you look at a person two meters tall who moves away from you, you find him getting smaller gradually until he disappears from your field of vision, yet he does not actually disappear.

This means that the law of your sight is governed by a law that has a specific range. There are other laws, such as the law of hearing, the law of gravity, and the law of electricity, all of which are phenomena whose effects we benefit from, yet we do not see them. So do not be surprised that there exists something you do not perceive, because the powers of your perception have their own laws.

The True One, glory be to Him, wills to demonstrate the truth of this by causing what scientists discover in the universe of things and forces that were not known before, though we were benefiting from them without realizing it. This shows that human perception is not capable of perceiving everything.

This clarifies for us that our seeing the sky raised without pillars that we see may mean that there are pillars made in a way unknown to us, or that it is raised without pillars at all. His saying, "without pillars that you see" (bi-ghayri 'amadin tarawnaha), is a declarative statement, and the example from our lives is when you say to your son, "I am going out to work, and you, study your lessons." In this way you have clarified to him, "Study your lessons," and this is a declarative statement, but what is intended by it is an imperative.

Presenting an imperative utterance in the form of a declarative one has a purpose, just as you say, "So-and-so has died, may God have mercy on him." Your saying "may God have mercy on him" is a declarative statement: you are informing that God has had mercy on him.

Even though you do not know whether God has had mercy on him or not, you said it out of optimism that mercy would fall upon him. You could have said, "So-and-so has died, O my Lord, have mercy on him," and by that you would be asking mercy for him. Likewise is the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him:

﴿without pillars that you see....﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 2)

meaning: look carefully and gaze deeply at it, and investigate what concerns you in this, if you are able. When the speaker draws your attention to something in order to stir the senses of your perception, that means he is confident of his workmanship.

The example from our lives, and to God belongs the highest example, and He, glory be to Him, is exalted above having any likeness: when you enter to buy wool, and the merchant offers you a cloth, you ask him, "Is this one hundred percent wool?" The merchant says to you, "Yes, it is one hundred percent wool, and bring a match so we can light a thread of it so you can see for yourself."

The True One, glory be to Him, clarifies here that the heavens are raised without pillars, and you should look for yourselves by extending your sight, and you will not find any pillars that are evident to you or to anyone else across the horizon of any one of you.

Each person has his own horizon according to the power of his sight. There are those for whom the sky meets the earth before their eyes, and we say to him: you need a medical prescription for glasses to treat this matter.

Horizons differ from person to person, and in common everyday speech it is said: "So-and-so has a narrow horizon; he sees only what is beneath his feet."

Someone might say: this happens to me and to those living now, and no one sees pillars raising the heavens; will this happen to those who come after us?

We say: artificial satellites from outer space have surveyed all areas of the earth, and no one has found any pillars raising the sky from the earth. This is the proof of the truth of the matter that the True One stated in this verse:

﴿Allah is the One who raised the heavens without pillars that you see....﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 2)

"Heavens" (samawat) is the plural of "sky" (sama'), which is everything that rises above you and shades you. The True One, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And He sent down from the sky water....﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 22)

We know that rain only falls from the clouds that rise above a person and appear suspended in the sky. When "the sky" is used without qualification, it refers to the highest sky that shades everything beneath it.

When people wanted to know the reality of the sky, whether it has a body or does not have a body, and whether it is an extension of atmosphere and air, the scientists did not agree on an answer. The True One, glory be to Him, has scattered the proofs of His existence, the proofs of His power, the proofs of His wisdom, and the proofs of His craftsmanship in the universe; then He gave you, O man, the proofs within yourselves as well, and He, glory be to Him, said:

﴿And in yourselves. Will you not see?﴾ (Surah al-Dhariyat, 21)

Look at yourself, and you will find scientists discovering every day something new and a wondrous secret, whether in anatomy or physiology. You will be amazed at your own self as you see those discoveries that earlier minds were unable to grasp, some of which are understood now and some of which will be understood later. The understanding of some unknown matters in the past indicates that you will understand new things in the future. If you look outside yourself, you will find the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him:

﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and in themselves, until it becomes clear to them that it is the Truth....﴾ (Surah Fussilat, 53)

The meaning of "We will show them" (sanurihim) in this verse is that the seeing does not end, because the "sin" (sa-) indicates the future. Those to whom the Qur'an was revealed read it this way, and we read it this way, and there will continually be new signs and new bounty from Allah, glory be to Him, until the Hour arrives.

And He, glory be to Him, said:

﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most people do not know.﴾ (Surah Ghafir, 57)

When you reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth, you will find it an utterly immense matter. It is enough for you to be perplexed about the matter of your own creation and formation, while you are merely an individual confined to a limited space, with a limited lifespan that has a beginning and an end. So how about the creation of the heavens and the earth, which existed before you and will continue after you until they split apart by the command of Allah, and the stars scatter at that moment?

It must be that the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of people, for the heavens and the

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 13, verse 3:

The Truth, glory be to Him, continues to recount His cosmic signs in this verse: ﴿And He it is who spread out the earth...﴾ [13:3]

That is, it is present before you and extended. Some people understand "madd" (extension) to mean "basṭ" (spreading out), and we say: spreading out follows from extension. For this reason some scholars stood up and said: "And who said the earth is spherical?"

Indeed, the Truth, glory be to Him, said: it is spread out, and He, glory be to Him, is the One who said: He has extended the earth.

I said to these scholars: let us first understand the word "madd," and let us also understand the word "al-arḍ" (the earth), which is that on which you and others stand, and on which creatures live, extending northward to the North Pole and southward to the South Pole. Wherever you are, in whatever position, it is extended eastward and westward. The meaning of ﴿He spread out the earth...﴾ [13:3] is that if you stand in a place and proceed from it, you find the earth extended before you, and there is no edge at which it ends. Had it been spread out, it would have had an end, and it would have been in the shape of a triangle, a square or a rectangle; it would have had an edge, and we would have found someone walking to that edge who would say: "I have reached the edge of the earth, and before me is emptiness." Not one of mankind has ever said that.

If a person walks along the equator, for example, he will remain walking on dry land, or riding a vessel that crosses the sea or ocean, until he reaches the same point from which he began his journey.

Thus we find the earth extended, unbounded, and this is not possible unless the earth is round, such that if you walk following any line of latitude or line of longitude, you will end at the point from which you began your journey.

This was the proof that scholars offered for the sphericity of the earth, before they invented the idea of photographing it from outside the atmosphere. And we take from the words of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿And He it is who spread out the earth...﴾ [13:3].

Another meaning is the necessity for a person to reflect on this extension; whoever finds life constricting in one place can migrate to another place, for the earth of God is spacious, and the Truth, glory be to Him, is the One who said:

﴿Was not the earth of God spacious so that you could emigrate therein?﴾ [4:97]

We know that the corruption of the world in our time has arisen from the corruption of policies and the increase of upheavals, and that is one of the consequences that hinder the extension of the earth: when a person tries to leave the borders of his homeland, he finds guards and obstacles at the borders of neighbouring countries, and everyone has forgotten the words of the Truth, glory be to Him:

﴿And the earth He set down for all creatures﴾ [55:10]. He, glory be to Him, has subjected the earth and made it subservient to all creatures, and if this Qur'anic principle is not realised, the world will remain in conflict; some countries will remain in need of people and some countries in narrowness of provision, due to the population increasing beyond the capacities of the earth on which they live. There will remain land without men, and men without land, as a result of the artificial barriers between countries. And until this issue is resolved, as we said at the United Nations, the Qur'anic principle must be applied: ﴿And the earth He set down for all creatures﴾ [55:10].

Whoever finds the land in which he grew up constricting should be permitted to emigrate. He, glory be to Him, continues in the same verse:

﴿And He placed in it firm mountains and rivers...﴾ [13:3]. The word "rawāsī" (firm, anchored things) is the plural of "rāsin," which means a fixed thing. He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And the mountains He anchored﴾ [79:32]. Thus the Truth has brought the ruling He willed for the mountains, and in another verse God gives us the reason for their being "rawāsī," saying:

﴿And We placed in the earth firm mountains lest it shake with them﴾ [21:31]. That is: lest the earth convulse with you. Had the earth been created in a state of stability, we would not have needed firm mountains to anchor it; but the earth was created in motion, and it is subject to agitation, and were it not for the firm mountains, the earth would have quaked.

Someone may say: but we now cut through mountains and take granite from one mountain to pave the floors of some areas, and cut marble from another mountain to make baths, basins and staircases, and extract some stones of certain kinds of mountains to extract uranium from them?

We say: consider the wisdom of the Truth, blessed and exalted, in His creation, and His wisdom in His governance. This earth has a circumference, a centre and diameters, and the closer you get to the centre of the earth, the smaller the diameter becomes. An example of this is the watermelon: if you extract its outer rind, you will have a sphere of green rind, and another sphere of the edible contents of the watermelon; and if you extract yet another sphere from the red fibres of which the watermelon consists, you will have yet another sphere, and the diameter of the new sphere will naturally be smaller than the green sphere.

Whenever you extract further spheres from the contents of the watermelon, the diameters become smaller, because you are approaching the centre of the circle. The green circumference that surrounds the watermelon, which is the rind, resembles the circumference found on the terrestrial globe; and this crust surrounding the earth is solid, whereas what lies within the earth and its interior consists of many different things and materials, some of which are liquid and some solid.

Whenever we approach the centre of the earth, we find an increase in temperature, and the masses of lava that gush out boiling from the craters of volcanoes indicate this; they are lava of extremely high temperature, and they are scorching lava.

The Truth, glory be to Him, willed to make the interior of the earth liquid, out of mercy towards us; for when we build houses, or cut stones from the mountains, or use the constituents of mountains for any purpose, we are in fact moving some of the constituents of the earth from one location to another.

When a weight moves from one place on the surface of the earth to another, the liquid within the earth's interior moves from the area upon which the weight has increased to the area from above which the weight has lightened, so that balance is achieved; and if that did not happen, the towering buildings that we see would collapse as the earth rotates.

An illustrative example: if you place a piece of dough on the surface of a watermelon or a ball, and set the watermelon or ball in rotation, the watermelon or ball will throw the piece of dough off its surface.

Scholars of "the science of motion" have explained this, saying: everything round that moves produces a process called self-ejection (al-ṭard al-dhātī), because a piece of dough, or anything we place on a rotating round object, has density and weight on the area where it is located, and this weight reaches the centre; and in order for the circular motion to continue in balance, the round object must eject the excess weight above it.

For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, willed that the two hemispheres of the earth, from whatever position you imagine, be equal in weight to the other hemisphere; and however much material you take and transfer from one location to another, the weight balances as a result of the movement of the liquids within the belly of the earth. This indicates the greatness of the Creator, who created with precise planning. And it suffices that we look at the greatness of the Truth, who did not make the mountains firm anchors to prevent the earth from shaking with us, but placed in the mountains and deserts that to which we turn for help when the earth constricts us; so we go to the mountains to extract raw materials, export them, and then buy wheat with their price. And we see around us the deserts, where those who dwelt in them formerly gasped from thirst and found no tree under which to shelter, and there God causes oil wells to gush forth.

Thus we see that every region of the earth contains good equal to any other region of the earth, and God has appointed for every matter a time in which mankind can benefit from that matter at that time. For this reason we find the Truth, glory be to Him, saying concerning the mountains:

﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in Him who created the earth in two days, and set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds. And He placed in it firm mountains above it, and blessed it, and measured therein its sustenance in four days, equal for those who ask.﴾ [41:9–10]

That is: He, glory be to Him, blessed the mountains, which are part of the earth, and willed that provisions be measured out in the mountains and the earth; and it suffices that we know that when rain falls from the sky upon the mountains, it carries with it some silt from the surfaces of those mountains, and thus the fertility of the earth is renewed.

Had the mountains been brittle, they would have melted away after a small number of rainfalls, and the fertile crust that nourishes the plants when we sow them in the earth would have melted away too.

But He, glory be to Him, willed that the atmospheric conditions pass in their variety and diversity in a sequence that provides heat and moisture sufficient to make the earth crack, so that the surface of the solid mountains becomes brittle to descend with the rain, and to nourish the earth with fertility, so that the sustaining of life may continue by producing the plants we need when cultivated.

We note His words, glory be to Him, in the same verse: ﴿And He placed in it firm mountains and rivers...﴾ [13:3].

Here the Truth combines the firm mountains, which are the fixed things, with the rivers, which carry flowing water, and this is a combination of opposites.

The term "nahr" (river) applies to what carries sweet waters, whereas "baḥr" (sea) is composed of salt water. If you survey all the rivers of the world, you will find that their courses flow into the seas, and this is evidence that the level of a river is always higher than the level of the sea; had the matter been the reverse, the water of the sea would have overwhelmed the water of the rivers, and we would not have been able to drink or cultivate.

For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, willed that sweet water be the higher, because it has a function to perform before it pours into the sea. I say this so that we may know the wisdom in the words of the Truth, glory be to Him:

﴿He has released the two seas, meeting side by side; between them is a barrier they do not transgress.﴾ [55:19–20]. And it is remarkable that the barrier which separates the river from the sea is gradual, such that the descent of the river's waters into the sea's waters proceeds by degrees, achieving ease in this transition; and it is also remarkable that if you dig on the seashore you may find sweet water.

For this reason, when we visit al-ʿArīsh we find a shore named the Shore of the Palms; and we know that palms need sweet water, as though the Truth, glory be to Him, had placed in these palms the property of extracting sweet water from this place that lies on the sea; and there may be sweet streams for it.

He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Have you not seen that God sends down water from the sky and then makes it flow as springs in the earth...﴾ [39:21].

In the countryside we find someone who digs a well and its water is sweet, and another who digs a well and its water is salty. This is evidence that the water in the belly of the earth is not mixed, but each water has channels that differ according to the type of water.

In the same verse, the Truth, glory be to Him, arranges the coming forth of fruits as a consequence of the presence of the firm mountains as a source of silt and fertility of the earth, and of the rivers which carry the water necessary for irrigation; thus the coming forth of fruits becomes a natural matter. And the fruit, as we know, is the goal of any planting. And in the same verse the Truth continues to mention His bounty, saying, glory be to Him:

﴿And from all fruits He made in it two mates, two...﴾ [13:3].

Some people use the word "zawj" (mate, pair) to mean two things, as when we say "a pair of shoes," although the precise expression requires us to say "two shoes" (zawjān min al-aḥdhiya), describing a right shoe and a left shoe; for the word "zawj" is a counterpart term, used for a thing that has a like; that is why we have the odd number and the even number; and the even number is one that has a counterpart. In humans, it is the male and the female. He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And of everything We created two mates...﴾ [51:49].

People also err in understanding the word "tawʾam" (twin); they think it means the two who are born together, but the precise meaning of "tawʾam" is the one born with another, and two together are called "the twins" (al-tawʾamān). Here the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And it is He who spread out the earth, and placed in it firm mountains and rivers, and from all fruits He made in it two mates, two...﴾ [13:3].

The Truth, glory be to Him, has not created anything except that He willed it to multiply, in confirmation of the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him:

{Glory be to He who created

This verse came with some detail to the words of the Truth, glory be to Him, at the end of Surah Yusuf: "And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by, while they turn away from it." (Surah al-Ra'd) [Note: the text here cites this as Surah al-Ra'd; translated as given.]

And this is a sign that joins His, exalted be He, saying: "He raised the heavens without pillars that you can see..." (Surah al-Ra'd, 2)

And it joins: "He arranges the affair, and details the signs..." (Surah al-Ra'd, 2)

And it joins the saying of the One, glory be to Him: "And it is He who spread out the earth and placed therein firm mountains and rivers, and of all fruits He placed therein two mates, covering the night with the day..." (Surah al-Ra'd, 3)

And when we reflect on the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: "And in the earth are neighbouring tracts..." (Surah al-Ra'd, 4)

we find that we cannot know it as the earth on which the likes of us live; that is the earth. If we wished to define it, we would render it vague, for it is too clear to need definition. The word "qit'a" (tracts/parts) first indicates a "whole" that is divided into parts, and this whole is a comprehensive genus; and within it is the particularity that distinguishes one tract from another. You hear the words of the scholars about the existence of zones of the earth called the wheat belt, and other zones called the banana belt; and hot zones, and other cold ones. The saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: "neighbouring tracts..." (Surah al-Ra'd, 4) is a statement that indicates the miraculous; for although they are neighbouring, each of them suits the climate in which it exists; the cultivation of maize requires a certain climate, and likewise the cultivation of bananas. Thus you find every region suited to what it produces; the earth is not one uniform dough, rather it is soil suited to the atmosphere in which it lies.

It is remarkable that in it are the secrets that man needs; this master whom all creatures serve. The earth is not uniform in its sameness; rather it differs according to what suits the conditions. There is a salty patch that does not grow, and another fertile one that grows.

Moreover, fertility differs from place to place and from one patch to another; the fruit of the guava from a certain tree in a certain region differs from the fruit of the guava from a tree in another region; and wheat in one region differs from wheat in another region, and it is said to you, "this is so-and-so's wheat." This happens although the earth is watered with one water.

The scholars far removed from the logic of heaven say: "The cause of the difference is the process of selection and choosing." As if they did not know that choosing requires a chooser, and that he should have a mind with which to think in order to choose; and likewise selection. Do seeds possess a mind with which they think and choose? Of course not.

They say: plants feed by capillary action, and we know that the capillary tubes we see in laboratories are made of thin glass; and when we place them in a basin of water, the water rises in them above the level of the vessel.

If we believe the scientists in that, how can we believe them that one tree takes water from another tree, and each produces the same fruits, yet the fruit of one tree differs from the other in taste?

We say: each tree takes from the earth what benefits it; and for that reason plants differ, and all of that happens by the power of the One who decreed and guided. Thus we see the earth as neighbouring tracts; some of which are suitable for a cultivation different from the cultivation of another land.

Some of the atheists may say: this difference is due to nature and environment. These ignore that nature as a whole is the sun that gives light, heat and radiation, the moon also reflects some of the light, the stars guide the one who travels in the wilderness, and air currents alternate, having their courses and their appointed times.

And despite all that, there is fertile land that produces, and salty land that produces nothing; red land, and black land, and sandy land, and all of them are neighbouring.

There must then be a chooser who acts, who commands this differently from that. The Truth, glory be to Him, continues in the same verse: "and gardens of vines, and crops, and palm trees, both single and clustered, watered with one water; yet We make some of them excel others in fruit..." (Surah al-Ra'd, 4)

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, brought the luxuries first; He spoke of fruit, then spoke of crops from which comes the staple food. We do this in our lives too: when you enter the table of one of the elders, you find fruit arranged on platters beside the main table on which food is served.

After the vines and the crops from which comes the necessary staple, the Truth, glory be to Him, brings the palm trees, which produce sustenance, and the dates they produce may be a luxury that a person consumes after the necessary food.

The saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: "single and clustered..." (Surah al-Ra'd, 4) requires us to know what "sinwan" (clustered) is.

We find the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, saying: "The paternal uncle is the sinw (counterpart) of your father," meaning that the sinw is the like.

Thus the meaning of "sinwan" is "two alike." We see this clearly in palm trees: we sometimes see one root from which two palm trees grow, or three palm trees; and sometimes four or five palm trees grow from one root.

The title "sinwan" is applied to a single root that branches into two or more palm trees; the word "sinwan" suits the dual and the plural, but in the dual it is treated in inflection like the dual: one says "two clustered (palms) bore fruit" and "I saw two clustered (palms)"; in the plural one says "I saw clustered (palms)" and "I passed by clustered (palms)." The singular, of course, is "sinw."

He, glory be to Him, says here in the verse about which we are reflecting: "and gardens of vines, and crops, and palm trees, single and clustered, watered with one water; yet We make some of them excel others in fruit..." (Surah al-Ra'd, 4).

It is remarkable that every tree takes through its roots a quantity of water and nutrients necessary to produce fruits of differing shape and taste.

This is what made us say before: the scientists' assumptions in plant sciences that plants feed by the capillary property is an inaccurate assumption.

For if that were so, the capillary tubes would take the same materials for one plant as those taken by the capillary tubes of another plant. But that is not the case: each plant takes from the earth only what is specific to it, and leaves the rest.

The fruits of each plant differ and are not alike; indeed the fruits of a single tree differ from one another.

An example of this: the mango tree or the fruitful palm tree. You can observe yourself, and you will see that you select from the mangoes coming from one tree what pleases you, and reject other fruits; and you will see that you select from the dates coming from one palm tree what delights you, and reject some of the fruits of that same palm.

When you go to buy fruit, you buy according to your attitude toward saving: if you love saving you will buy the second-grade fruit; and if you love to enjoy the good of that fruit, you will buy from the distinguished fruit.

I challenge anyone to stand before a fruit basket and select the fruits that are not beautiful in shape and sheen; rather every person tries to take the beautiful and good of that fruit, and when he pays the price of what he bought, you will find him paying with the old paper money in his pocket, and he will keep the new money for himself.

This attitude prevails over the attitude of any person; he is always inclined to reject taking the bad, and always afraid of losing the good. The Truth, glory be to Him, says: "Say: Even if you possessed the treasuries of the mercy of my Lord, you would then withhold, for fear of spending..." (Surah al-Ra'd, 100)

You find in fruits no similarity, but difference in taste from one kind to another; likewise you find difference in the manner of eating them. None of us eats the whole date; rather we eat the date fruit after removing the stone; we eat the fig whole, and we remove the hard seed from the heart of the apricot, then eat the apricot after that.

Each fruit has its own particular system; it is not a mechanical matter in God's giving of similar fruits; rather there is difference, and this difference extends to the finest details, to the extent that when you take a cluster of grapes you find some grapes differ from others.

We do not prefer some fruits over others in eating only; we prefer some of the fruits of a single kind over other of its fruits.

When you read: "We make some of them excel others in fruit..." (Surah al-Ra'd, 4)

know that there is no thing or matter that is preferred absolutely, and another matter that is absolutely preferred over it; since we prefer some of it over others, this means that each of them is preferred in one respect and preferred over in another respect.

The clear example before us all: when we sit at a table on which there is a turkey, your hand may move toward the dish of pickles before your hand extends to the turkey, because your "soul" desired it first; so do not say that there is always something preferred over, or something always preferred.

Likewise people: beware of thinking that there is a person absolutely virtuous, and another absolutely inferior; rather there is a person virtuous in one respect and inferior to another in another respect.

The example: the owner of a luxurious car whose tire bursts; he wishes that God would send him someone to pass by and change the tire; then there passes by this man in unclean clothes stained with grease, and this man is better than him in his ability to remove the burst tire and fit the spare, sound one.

Thus God spread bounty among people, so that some of them need others; and therefore I say: when you find yourself virtuous in some respect, beware of falling into conceit; ask yourself: what does someone else excel you in? And remember the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: "O you who believe, let not a people ridicule another people, perhaps they may be better than them, nor let women ridicule other women, perhaps they may be better than them..." (Surah al-Hujurat, 11)

Thus the Truth, glory be to Him, willed to distribute excellence among people, so that each needs the other, and so that society complements itself. Likewise He, glory be to Him, distributed excellence in foods, fruits and produce; and look at yourself at the moment when various kinds of fruit are presented to you: you may take a piece of sycamore fig before you take a piece of apple; for at the moment your soul desired the sycamore fig, it became, in the estimation of measures and exchange, the better, and every person can find that in what concerns him or what he loves.

And the Truth, glory be to Him, is the One who said: "And everything with Him is in measure" (Surah al-Ra'd, 8).

Therefore you find man coloring and ingeniously preparing food, and individuals' appetites for varied foods differ; you may find two people who both favor chicken meat, but one prefers the breast meat and the other prefers the thigh meat, and you find a third who prefers pigeon meat, and a fourth who prefers eating fish.

Indeed you find difference in the manner of eating among those who love fish: some love to eat the fish's head, and some love the fish's flesh itself; and no one has knowledge of the cause of the difference in temperaments in being drawn to different kinds of foods. When you contemplate this matter, there may come to your mind the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: "How can you disbelieve in God...?" (Surah al-Baqarah, 28)

The question here from God is for wonder; and wonder is usually at something whose cause is hidden, so is a cause hidden from God that He should wonder? Of course not; He, glory be to Him, is exalted above that, and He knows the cause of the disbelief of the disbelievers; but He denounces to them the causes of disbelief.

The example from our lives, and to God belongs the highest example: you find yourself, when saying "How can you insult your father?" to a person who directs cutting words at his parent, wondering in order to deny what this person did.

Likewise the saying: "How can you disbelieve in God?" because disbelief is something that cannot come from a rational person. We had a shaykh, the eminent scholar Ahmad al-Tawil; he used to tell us about a shaykh of his, who when reading the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him, "How can you disbelieve in God...?" (Surah al-Baqarah, 28), used to say: the address here is general to every person, because the Truth after it brings the general matter: "and you were dead..."

And it is a matter of wonder that you show astonishment at something whose cause you do not know. Such wonder cannot be attributed to God, because He knows everything. When wonder is attributed to God, as in His saying, ﴿How can you disbelieve in God, when you were dead and He gave you life?﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah), it means that He denies that a person should disbelieve when the proofs of faith are in place. Yet some people disbelieve in God regardless. God's saying, ﴿And if you are amazed, then amazing is their saying...﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd), is addressed to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him). The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was amazed that they used to call him "the Truthful, the Trustworthy" before God sent him as a messenger, and after the message came they said, "He is a sorcerer, a liar."

How can he be truthful and trustworthy in his humanity and personal character, and then when God supports him with the support of prophethood, you accuse him of lying? Would it not have been more fitting for you to say that he has become more truthful? Is it possible that he is truthful in your eyes, and then he lies about God?

There is also wonder in that they denied resurrection after death, although God has made the proofs for it clear. Yet only the believers received the matter of resurrection with acceptance, as soon as the Messenger of God conveyed it to them as one reporting from his Lord. We find that God, exalted is He, has respected the inquisitiveness of the human intellect. He clarified this and set up proofs for it, and He informed us that He was not incapable of the first creation, so He will not be incapable of resurrection.

He brought us into being from nothing, and in the resurrection He will bring us forth from existence. It is then foolishness that anyone should doubt the resurrection. The one who is wasteful toward himself denies the resurrection only because he cannot control himself, and he thinks that by denying resurrection he will not meet the dark fate that he will meet in the Hereafter.

That is why you find those who are wasteful toward themselves trying to cast doubt on the resurrection, and God brings up their doubt in His saying, ﴿And they say: "There is nothing but our life of this world. We die and we live, and only time destroys us."﴾ (Surat al-Jathiyah, 24).

If one of them had placed the matter of resurrection in his certainty, he would have turned away from his desires, whereas he wants to rush after his desires. That is why you find them saying, ﴿When we have been lost in the earth...﴾ (Surat al-Sajdah, 10).

By this they mean that after death they will become dust, returning to the earth as elements and dust scattered by the winds, so how will God bring them back for resurrection and produce them anew? God says: ﴿He says, "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?" Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is Knowing of all creation."﴾ (Surat Ya-Sin, 78–79).

Among the disbelievers is one who said: "We will become dust, then we will mix with the soil, and this soil will be cultivated, and our elements will mingle with what the earth produces of fruits, vegetables and trees. Then a child eats from the fruit that was nourished by our elements, so some of us becomes part of this child's constituents. Analogy shows that we will be scattered, so how will God bring us back?"

All of that is, naturally, from the whispering and inspiration of Satan: ﴿And indeed, the devils inspire their allies...﴾ (Surat al-An'am, 121).

I say: Let us suppose that a person became ill, grew emaciated, and lost thirty kilograms of his weight. What was lost of this weight must have gone into the earth as elements mixed with it. Then a doctor came, diagnosed the disease and prescribed the medicine, and God willed recovery for this patient, so he regained his weight and returned to his natural state. Are the thirty kilograms he regained the very same quantity, in its quality and particularity, that he had previously lost? Certainly not.

Thus we understand that formation is a relative formation of elements: so much of carbon, so much of sodium, so much of magnesium, and so on. Therefore, recompense on the Last Day is a necessary rational process. God says: ﴿How can you disbelieve in God, when you were dead and He gave you life, then He will cause you to die, then He will give you life again, then to Him you will be returned?﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah, 28).

As long as there is a command, and there is a prohibition, and there is a prohibition, and there is a clear method that explains everything. And if you are amazed, O Muhammad, at the disbelievers and at what they raise of disputes, then you may be amazed, for these are matters that deserve amazement. When God addresses creation, He addresses them either about a matter they doubt, or about a matter no one doubts.

The example from our own life, and to God belongs the highest example: when you address someone about a matter he doubts, you try to affirm it by every means. Thus we find some people denying resurrection and reckoning, and we find God, exalted is He, reminding them of it through His Messenger and affirming it for them.

Also, God addressed them about what they did not doubt, which is death, and said: ﴿Every soul will taste death...﴾ (Surat Ali 'Imran, 185).

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said: "I have never seen a certainty more like doubt than people's certainty about death."

So death is certain, yet no one tries to think that it is coming. God says: ﴿Then indeed, after that, you will surely die.﴾ (Surat al-Mu'minun, 15).

This is an affirmation of a matter on which people agree that it is occurring, but because of their heedlessness toward it, they appeared like those who deny it. Therefore He addressed them with the address used for deniers, then He said after that: ﴿Then indeed, on the Day of Resurrection you will be resurrected.﴾ (Surat al-Mu'minun, 16).

He did not say "wa-la-tub'athun" (with emphasis), because resurrection is a matter that does not need emphasis, and the absence of emphasis here is stronger than emphasis, because the matter of death is very clear despite heedlessness toward it, whereas resurrection is a reality without doubt, so it does not need emphasis.

The example from our own life, and to God belongs the highest example: a person goes to the doctor, and after examining him the doctor says, "Go, I will not write you a prescription." This statement means that this person is in perfect health, as if writing a prescription would carry a suggestion that there is an illness.

Likewise, God addresses creation about the thing they deny for which there is clear evidence, so His address to them comes without emphasis, and by that method He makes clear that they are wrong to deny it. As for the thing that they are certain of but are heedless of, He affirms it for them so that they do not become heedless of it.

Likewise with oaths. He swore by the fig and the olive, He swore by the wise Qur'an, and He swore by other things, and in other places we find Him saying: ﴿I swear by this city, and you are a resident of this city, and by the begetter and what he begets.﴾ (Surat al-Balad, 1–3).

﴿We have certainly created man in hardship.﴾ (Surat al-Balad, 4).

﴿I swear...﴾ (Surat al-Balad, 1).

Then He brings the answer to the oath? I say: He has come here with His saying: ﴿I swear...﴾ (Surat al-Balad, 1), as if He is making clear that you have no right to deny; therefore it would not be right for me to swear to you, and even if I were to swear, I would swear by such and such.

In the verse that is the subject of our reflections, He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And if you are amazed, then amazing is their saying, "When we are dust, will we indeed be in a new creation?"﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd, 5).

He, may He be exalted, reminds them of what they should not have forgotten: He created them from dust, and He created the dust from nothing, and He is the One who said: ﴿Were We then incapable of the first creation? Rather, they are in doubt about a new creation.﴾ (Surat Qaf, 15).

So, He, exalted is He, is amazed at the matter of these people, and what increases the wonder is that they denied Muhammad (peace be upon him) after they had tested his truthfulness and found his trustworthiness, and they said this about him before he was sent. Beyond that, they denied resurrection even though proof for it exists. The Almighty describes them: ﴿Those are the ones who disbelieved in their Lord...﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd, 5). That is: these who deny you, O Muhammad, and deny resurrection, have not only disbelieved in God, who imposed the worship of obligation, but they also disbelieve in the lordship that gives to the believer and the disbeliever, the obedient and the disobedient, and by whose command causes are set in motion to respond to any striver who follows the rules of striving, so he receives from the gifts of lordship, which are gifts of honor that guarantee provision, whereas the gifts of divinity are obligations to obey the devotional commands, represented in "fa'al" (do) and "la taf'al" (do not do).

God does not impose obligation on a human being until he reaches the degree of maturity that qualifies him to beget a like of himself. God has left every person to enjoy the good blessings that He has bestowed upon mankind, and it was incumbent on the human being to seek faith as soon as the call reaches him from the Messenger who conveys from God, the Messenger who is witnessed to be truthful and trustworthy. Therefore we find God, as He describes those who deny faith: ﴿Those are the ones who disbelieved in their Lord...﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd, 5).

He adds: ﴿Those will have shackles around their necks, and those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd, 5). The ghull (shackle) is an iron collar that has an end in each hand to restrain it, and an end hanging at the neck to reduce the range of movement of the hands, and for greater humiliation. And they are the companions of the Fire. The word "sahib" (companion) is applied to someone you know in a way that pleases your being and your essence. There is one you accompany, there is one you befriend, there is one you bond with, and there is one you know superficially and do not form a deep relationship with.

Knowledge has degrees, and companionship is a harmony and attraction between two. Whoever keeps company with the Fire is one whom the Fire loves, and each of them insists on the other's company, so that the Fire does not say to its Lord on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Is there any more?﴾ (Surat Qaf, 30). That is: the punishment itself is eager to reach the disobedient.

The seeking of haste is to ask for a thing before its time, and to fall short of the time needed for the goal. When you want some goal, you need a time that differs from one goal to another; and when you hurry toward a goal, you want to reach it before its time.

Every choice of hastening or delaying has its advantages and disadvantages. So is the haste here for the sake of something desired? They here hasten the evil before the good, and this is evidence of the disorder and corruption of their standards of thinking. They had already said: ﴿We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth, [90] Or [until] you have a garden of palms and grapes and cause rivers to gush forth within them in profusion, [91] Or you cause the heaven to fall upon us in fragments as you have claimed, [92]﴾ (Surah al-Isra'). 

Thus we find these disbelievers, while they hasten the evil before the good, just as they hastened that stones should rain down upon them, not knowing that every punishment has a term and a fixed appointed time. They did not consider saying: "O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then guide us to it." Rather, they said: ﴿O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment.﴾ (Surah al-Anfal, 32).

Thus the Exalted has clarified for us the disorder that has reached their souls and their corruption, for their standards ended in disbelief. Nothing shows the corruption of standards more than their hastening of evil before good, because the sensible person, when choosing between two matters, hastens toward the good because it benefits, and sets aside the evil.

As long as the souls of these disbelievers are corrupt, and as long as their standards are disordered, the cause of that must be disbelief.

So then: hastening evil before good, with respect to an individual or a group, is a proof of foolishness in choosing among alternatives. If they had truly desired what benefits them, they would have hastened the good and not hastened the evil. And here the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And they ask you to hasten the evil before the good, although there have passed before them exemplary punishments...﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 6).

Why, then, do they hasten punishment? Have they not considered what befell those who denied the messengers before them? When the Messenger says: "Beware lest a punishment befall you," or "Beware lest such-and-such," is there any lie in that? And why did they not take heed of the lessons that occurred throughout history to the peoples who denied the messengers before them?

"Al-mathulat" is the plural of "mathulah"; and in another view, "mathalah." The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished...﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 126).

And He also says: ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it...﴾ (Surah al-Shura, 40).

Thus "mathulat" is from "mithl" (likeness); that is, the punishment is made equal to the deed. And the saying of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿And there have already passed before them exemplary punishments...﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 6) means: He, glorified is He, had already sent down punishment upon the like of them among the earlier nations who denied the messengers; either by annihilation, if their faith was hopeless, or by subjugation and victory over them. He, glorified is He, continues in the same verse: ﴿And indeed your Lord is full of forgiveness for the people despite their wrongdoing...﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 6). That is: He, glorified is He, does not hasten punishment upon those who disbelieve, perhaps a righteous man will arise among them. He, glorified is He, was patient with Abu Jahl, and from him came Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, the righteous Companion; and He was patient with Khalid ibn al-Walid, so he became "the drawn sword of Allah," after he had been one of the fiercest fighters in the camp of disbelief.

The reports of the Companions convey to us how Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl fought until he was struck with a grievous wound, and he looked at Khalid ibn al-Walid saying: "Is this a death that would please the Messenger of Allah with me?"

The reports of the Companions also convey to us how one of the Muslim fighters grieved at the moment Khalid ibn al-Walid escaped him in the days when he was upon disbelief, while he did not know that the Truth, glorified is He, had reserved Khalid to be the drawn sword of Allah after his Islam.

Thus it was the will of the Truth that some of the chieftains of Quraysh escape death in the days when they were upon disbelief, so that they might become among the best of the people of Islam afterward. He, glorified is He, continues: ﴿And indeed your Lord is full of forgiveness for the people despite their wrongdoing...﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 6).

Although people are wrongdoers, He, glorified is He, forgives them; because He, glorified is He, is more pleased with His believing servant who repents than any of you who, having lost his camel with its provisions in a barren wilderness, then finds it. Therefore I hold that whoever reproaches a servant for a sin for which the servant has sought forgiveness from Allah is a sinful person; for the servant has sought Allah's forgiveness, so no one should poke his nose into this matter. We note here the saying of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿despite their wrongdoing...﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 6).

In this expression some scholars find that Allah has used one particle in place of another; so "ʿalā" (upon) has come in place of "maʿa" (with). We note that "ʿalā" consists of three letters, while "maʿa" consists of two letters; so why did the Truth, glorified is He, omit the lighter and use "ʿalā"? There must be a purpose behind that. I say: the Truth, glorified is He, used "ʿalā" in His saying: ﴿And indeed your Lord is full of forgiveness for the people despite their wrongdoing...﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 6), to confirm for us that the wrongdoing of people called for punishment; but His mercy, glorified is He, prevails over punishment. Thus the word "ʿalā" performed the meaning of "maʿa," and it added to us that the Truth, glorified is He, is the one who controls punishment, and that the mercy of Allah overwhelms the wrongdoing of the servants. Similarly His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And they give food, despite their love for it...﴾ (Surah al-Insan, 8); that is, they love food greatly; but the desire for generosity and hospitality overcomes the love of food. But people should not assume that the mercy of Allah always overcomes His punishment; for if some of the audacious were to assume this and imagine it a general rule, the cosmos would be corrupted. Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, concludes the noble verse with His saying:

﴿And indeed your Lord is severe in punishment﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 6); that is: He, glorified is He, is capable of severe punishment. Thus the verse combined hope and warning.

We know that when "lawla" (لولا) is followed by a nominal sentence, it is a particle of prohibition due to existence (حرف امتناع لوجود). An example is your saying, "Lawla Zayd 'indaka la-zurtuka" (لولا زيد عندك لزرتك), meaning: what prevents you from visiting so-and-so is the presence of Zayd. When "lawla" is followed by a verbal sentence, the speaker wants what follows it to happen. An example is your saying, "Lawla 'atafta 'ala fulan" (لولا عطفت على فلان) or "Lawla safahta 'an waladika" (لولا صفحت عن ولدك), meaning: in this there is encouragement for what follows to happen.

The apparent meaning of the words of the disbelievers in this verse, on which we are reflecting, is that they ask for a sign to confirm the truthfulness of the Messenger (ﷺ) in the clear statement of truth that he brings to them. It is as if, by this saying, they deny the miracle with which he (ﷺ) came, which is the Noble Qur'an, despite the fact that they were a people of eloquence, literature, clear expression and magnificent linguistic performance. They set up markets for literature, awarded prizes for literary brilliance, hung poems on the walls of the Ka'bah, and the tribes boasted of the poets and orators they had produced.

When the Qur'an came from the same kind of brilliance as yours, surpassing your eloquence, and you could not produce a verse like its verses, how did you not regard it as a miracle? Yet you demand another miracle, like the miracle of Musa (peace be upon him) or the miracle of 'Isa (peace be upon him)? You should have been proud of the complete miracle that carries the method until the Hour arrives.

But foolishness made them ask for a miracle other than the Qur'an. They did not pay attention to the other miracles that accompanied the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They did not notice that water gushed from between the fingers of the Prophet (ﷺ), that a little food satisfied the people and overflowed, that a cloud shaded him, and that the trunk of the palm tree moaned with an audible sound when the Messenger of Allah moved his pulpit, after he (ﷺ) had been delivering the sermon while leaning on the trunk. Perhaps they had an excuse in this, because they did not see those sensory miracles, given that they were disbelievers; their vision was limited to those who believed in his message (ﷺ).

Thus we know that the Messenger (ﷺ) was not deprived of cosmic miracles, those that happen once and then end, and which are a proof against those who witness them. They came to confirm the faith of the oppressed few. When they saw water gushing between his fingers while they were shaken by persecution, their attachment to the Messenger (ﷺ) increased. But the disbelievers did not see those miracles.

They should have been content with the miracle of which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Qur'an is sufficient for me" (القرآن كافيني). The Qur'an is a miracle of the same kind as that in which you excelled, O Arabs. Muhammad is a messenger from among yourselves; he did not come from a tribe other than your tribe, and his tongue is your tongue. You know that he did not sit with a teacher, nor is it known that he delivered a sermon among you before, nor did he compose poetry, nor is he known to have been one of the orators of the Arabs. Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, sent down the word upon his tongue:

﴿Say: "If Allah had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you. I have lived among you a lifetime before it. Will you not then reason?"﴾ (Surah Yunus) That is: I lived among you and did not speak with eloquence, nor did I compete in the markets of poetry. You should have believed that it is a saying from One who is All-Wise, All-Knowing. But some of them said: "He was concealing his talent and postponed revealing it." To these we say: Can an orphan who lost his father while still in his mother's womb, then lost his mother while still young, and whose grandfather also died while he was young, and who saw the great men around him perishing in no order of death, dying without illness or apparent cause, be the kind of man who could feel safe about himself, living to the age of forty in order to announce his talent?

Furthermore, who said that genius waits until forty to appear? All of us know that geniuses appear at the end of the second decade and the beginning of the third decade. Despite your not acknowledging the miracle of the Qur'an, here is the Truth, glory be to Him, making on your tongues what you concealed in your hearts, and the people see it in His firm Book:

﴿And they said, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man from one of the two cities?"﴾ (Surah al-Zukhruf) Thus you acknowledged the greatness of the Qur'an, and you tried to dispute the value of the one upon whom the Qur'an was sent down. He, glory be to Him, says here, in the verse on which we are reflecting:

﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?"﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd)

Then why did you say and acknowledge that He has a Lord? Should you not have acknowledged his message and declared your faith in him and in the message? It has already been said by them: "The Lord of Muhammad has forsaken him." This saying means that they acknowledged that he has a Lord, so why did they acknowledge Him in hardship and deny Him in ease?

If they ask you for a miracle other than the Qur'an, know, O Muhammad, that your Lord is the One who sends miracles, and He determines the miracle for each messenger according to what the people to whom the messenger is sent excel in. You, O Muhammad, are only a warner, that is, one who warns: ﴿You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd). Every people has a guide who guides them with signs suited to that people. The Children of Israel excelled in magic, so the miracle of Musa came in the kind of thing in which they excelled. The people of 'Isa excelled in medicine, so the miracle of 'Isa was of the type in which they excelled.

Thus we see that every people has a guide, and with him a miracle suited to his people. For this reason Allah answered them with a silencing reply when they said:

﴿"We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth, or you have a garden of palm trees and grapes and make rivers gush forth within it abundantly, or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces as you claim, or you bring Allah and the angels before us, or you have a house of gold, or you ascend into the sky. And we will not believe in your ascending until you bring down to us a book we can read."﴾ (Surah al-Isra')

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Say: "Glory be to my Lord! Am I anything but a human messenger?" And what prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them was only that they said, "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?" Say: "If there were angels walking calmly on the earth, We would have sent down to them from the sky an angel as a messenger."﴾ (Surah al-Isra')

The reply comes from the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿And We did not refrain from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them...﴾ (Surah al-Isra'). That is: a people before you asked for the signs they wanted, and Allah sent them, yet they disbelieved, because disbelief clothes the disbeliever in the garment of obstinacy, since the disbeliever is determined to disbelieve.

What is the occasion in which the Truth says that?

The Truth, glory be to Him, willed to affirm the matter that for every people there is a guide, that His Messenger (ﷺ) is a warner, and that their demand for miraculous signs stems from their desire to thwart the Messenger (ﷺ). Had the Messenger brought them a sign of what they asked for, they would have persisted in disbelief. He, glory be to Him, knows what they will do, for He knows what is more hidden than that; He knows, for example, what every female carries, what the wombs diminish, and what they increase.

We know that every female, when God wills that she conceive, carries the fetus in her womb, because the womb is the place where the fetus settles in the mother's belly. And His saying, exalted be He: ﴿And what the wombs diminish and what they increase﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd) means: what is lessened and what is lost of the miscarried fetus in any abortion, or what is reduced of births by death. Thus the wombs "diminished" (ghāḍat), that is, the offspring came forth before their creation was complete, such as when a child is lacking an eye or a finger; or the creation carries an excess that differs from what we are accustomed to in natural creation, such as an extra finger or being born with two heads.

Or the increase may be in number, that is, a woman gives birth to twins or more, or the increase may relate to the duration of the pregnancy.

Thus we know that He, glory be to Him, knows what the wombs diminish, that is, what they lessen in ordinary formation or increase, or the consideration may be of time: such as when an abortion occurs with the fetus at a day, a month, or two months old, and then up to six months; at that point it is not called an abortion but a birth.

There are those born after six months of pregnancy, or after seven months, or eight months; and the birth may extend to two years according to Abu Hanifa, to four years according to al-Shafi'i, or to five years according to Imam Malik, since the duration of pregnancy may decrease or increase.

It is said that al-Dahhak was born after two years in his mother's womb, and Hirm ibn Hayyan was born after four years; his mother's family kept observing the enlargement of her belly and the absence of her monthly bleeding throughout that period; then she bore our companion. For this reason they named him "Hirm," meaning he was old while still in the womb.

Thus we understand the meaning of "diminish" as lessening or increasing, whether in the form of creation or in the duration of time. The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And with Him everything is by measure﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd).

The measure is the quantity or the quality, in time or in place, or in gifts and qualifications. The Truth, glory be to Him, enumerated the five keys of the unseen when He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs...﴾ (Surat Luqman).

Some have tried to raise an objection here, attributing it to civilization and scientific progress. This progress is subject to probability, and whatever is subject to probability is invalidated as proof; this concerns knowing the sex of the fetus before birth, whether it is male or female. They overlooked that science has not known whether a person will be tall or short, intelligent or dull, wretched or happy; this has baffled physicians and researchers until today and beyond. Then if you ask how the doctor knows that?

He knows this matter after conception occurs, by taking a sample of the fluid surrounding the fetus and then analyzing it. But God knows without taking a sample, and it is He who said to one of His servants:

﴿O Zechariah, indeed We give you good news of a boy whose name is Yahya...﴾ (Surat Maryam). Thus we know that God's knowledge does not await a sample or an experiment; His knowledge is eternal, free from deficiency, and He knows what is in the wombs in whatever form it is, or its color, or its sex, or its intelligence, or its happiness or wretchedness, or its number.

He, glory be to Him, willed to manifest the absoluteness of His power in the conception of Zechariah's wife of Yahya, peace be upon him; He who created Adam without father or mother, then created Eve from a father without a mother, created Jesus from a mother without a father, and created all of us from a father and a mother. When the absoluteness of power wills, He says: ﴿Be, and it is﴾ (Surat Ya-Sin).

The example, as I said, is in Zechariah's entering the sanctuary to Mary, peace be upon her; he found with her provision, so he asked her: ﴿Where did this come to you?﴾ (Surat Al 'Imran).

She said: ﴿It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account﴾ (Surat Al 'Imran).

Zechariah knew that God provides for whom He wills without account; but this knowledge was on the periphery of his awareness, and Mary's words summoned it to the center of his awareness, so Zechariah knows with certainty that God alone provides without account. As soon as this statement moves that faith-truth from the edge of awareness to its center, Zechariah calls upon his Lord in that very place to grant him a child, and the Truth gives him the good news of a son.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 13, verse 9:

When Zakariyya (Zechariah) remembers that he has reached an advanced old age, and that his wife is barren, the Truth, glory be to Him, reminds him that giving a child is an easy matter for Him, glory be to Him: ﴿He said: "So it is. Your Lord says: 'It is easy for Me, and I created you before, when you were nothing.'"﴾ (Surah Maryam).

And of everything He has a measure (bi-miqdar). Nothing is ever hidden from Him, and what will happen to any human being in the future after he is born is unseen (ghayb); but the One who has full knowledge of it is Allah alone. It is as if there is a miniature "model" that Allah knows first; and even if a person comes to know it at the end of his life, he would find it matching what Allah willed and knew beforehand. Nothing resists Him, glory be to Him; for everything with Him is by measure.

He is the Knower of the unseen and the seen; He knows what is hidden behind the veil of the past or the future, and everything that is absent from man, and He knows, all the more, what man witnesses. So His knowledge is not limited to the unseen, leaving the seen without His knowledge. Rather, He knows the unseen and He knows the seen: ﴿The Knower of the unseen and the seen, the Great, the Exalted.﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 13:9).

Al-Kabir (the Great) is one of the Most Beautiful Names of Allah. Some have asked: why is "al-Akbar" (the Greatest) not among the Most Beautiful Names of Allah, while we only have the saying "Allahu akbar" in the rites of prayer?

I say: because the opposite of "al-kabir" is "al-saghir" (the small), and everything in relation to its Originator is small. We say in the call to prayer "Allahu akbar" because it takes you out of your work, which He has entrusted to you, namely the building up of the universe, so that you may seek His help during your worship of Him and in applying His method; He then provides you with the strength by which you produce what you need in your life of food, clothing and covering of the private parts.

So, all work is required, even for the establishment of worship. Beware of saying: "God is great and the rest is small," for the rest contains matters that are great from the viewpoint that they are blessings from the Greatest Bestower; but Allah is greater than us. We say it when we are asked to leave our works in order to seek help through His worship, glory be to Him.

We know that work is required for building up the universe, and is required even for the establishment of worship. You would have no strength to worship your Lord if your Lord had not empowered you to worship Him. It is He who preserves your strength through food and drink, and you would not eat or drink if you did not plough, sow and make. All of that gives you the strength to pray, give zakat and perform Hajj; and whatever the obligation cannot be completed without is itself obligatory. I have previously said that when the Truth, glory be to Him, called us to the Friday prayer, He said: ﴿O you who believe! When the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, then hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trading. That is better for you, if you only knew.﴾ (Surah al-Jumu'ah, 62:9). Thus the Truth, glory be to Him, takes us out of our work to the prayer at its appointed time. Then the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him, comes: ﴿And when the prayer is ended, disperse in the land and seek of Allah's bounty, and remember Allah much that you may succeed.﴾ (Surah al-Jumu'ah, 62:10).

Thus, glory be to Him, He took us out of work, which is a great matter, to something greater, namely the performance of prayer. The words of the Truth, glory be to Him, describing Himself as (al-Mutaʿal) mean that He is transcendent in His essence, attributes and actions: no essence is like His essence, no attribute like His attributes, no act like His act, and all that belongs to Him is fitting to Him alone, and He is never at all similar to anything else.

Whenever you hear the word "sawa'" (equal), it refers to a number not less than two. We say "sawa' Zayd wa-'Amr" (Zayd and 'Amr are equal), or "sawa' Zayd wa-'Amr wa-Bakr wa-Khalid."
