What is meant here is that, since Allah, the Exalted, is the Knower of the unseen and the seen, any secret that exists must be known to Him, the Glorified. He, the Glorified, says:

﴿The Most Merciful is established on the Throne. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is beneath the soil. And if you speak aloud, indeed He knows the secret and what is even more hidden.﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha)

Is the secret what you entrust to another? If the secret is that, then "the more hidden" is what remains with you. And if the secret means what exists within you that you have not told anyone, then He, the Glorified, knows it before it becomes a secret.

The Glorified continues: ﴿And whoever hides himself by night and whoever goes forth in the day﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 10). Thus the Exalted has here encompassed all kinds of action. Action, as we know, is the occupation of the limbs with their objects: the action of the tongue is to speak and to taste, the action of the hands is to do, the action of the ear is to hear, and the action of the heart is intention. Action, as we know, is sometimes speech and sometimes deed.

Thus we find "speech" has taken up half of "action," because conveying from Allah is speech, and the action of the limbs is subject to what is said by the Exalted and Glorified.

Therefore the Exalted made clear to us that action is every deed connected with the limbs; He took speech as one portion by itself, and the deeds of the limbs took the other portion, because the action of the remaining limbs falls within the framework of what has been heard of Allah's method. That is why the verse we are contemplating gathers all action, of speech and of deed: ﴿Whether of you conceal speech or speak openly, and whoever hides himself by night and whoever goes forth in the day﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 10).

Whoever hides by night must be planning something, such as wanting to listen to whatever lies behind every movement, or to look at what he might observe. Likewise, whoever shows himself and appears in the day, Allah knows him. The disbelievers should have taken heed of a wondrous matter they used to conceal within themselves, at the moment Allah related it, saying: ﴿And they say within themselves, "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?"﴾ (Surah al-Mujadila, 8). How, then, did Allah know this, unless He knows the secret and what is even more hidden?

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 13, verse 11:

The word (lahu) ("for him" / "to his benefit") indicates benefit. When you say "lakа kadhā" ("for you is such-and-such") it is the opposite of saying "alayka kadhā" ("against you is such-and-such"). When the Glorified says: ﴿For him are angel-guardians (mu'aqqibāt)...﴾ [13:11], it is as if the guardians are for the benefit of the human being. Mu'aqqibāt is a feminine plural, and its singular is mu'aqqibah; that is, Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, has angels who take turns guarding and preserving the human being night and day from things that cannot be guarded against.

The example is those statistics that have emerged regarding people who are bitten by snakes: it has been established that they are not bitten while asleep, but rather while awake. That is, during the hours when they are in the cover of sleep, there is something that protects them; but when awake, a person may act with recklessness and heedlessness, and so the viper bites him.

We say in our popular proverbs: "The eye has a guard upon it." And we observe many events that seem strange to us, such as a child falling from a window of an upper floor and not being harmed at all, because Allah, the Exalted, willed that the guarding angels (al-mu'aqqibāt) protect him from harm, since the duty of the guardians is to protect the human being from every harm.

Thus we see that Allah, the Exalted, prepared the universe for the human being before creating him, in order that He might make him a khalīfah (vicegerent) in it: He prepared the heavens, He prepared the earth, He subjected the sun and the moon, He brought forth the fruits, and He made the night cover the day.

All of that He prepared for the khalīfah before the khalīfah existed. And He, the Glorified, is al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting Sustainer) over this khalīfah; so He also protects him after creation, and does not leave him to the components of his own self to defend himself in matters he cannot defend against; and Allah assigns the mu'aqqibāt angels to that task.

The meaning of the mu'aqqibāt may also refer to the angels who follow (yata'aqqabūn) the actions of the human being and write down his good deeds and write down his bad deeds; and they may perform both tasks together: guarding him and recording his deeds. So if they record good deeds for him, this is for his benefit.

Someone may say: "But they will record the bad deeds, and these are against the human being and not for him." I say: No. It is good that we understand well the higher purpose, and know that when a person knows that a bad deed will be reckoned against him, counted, and written down, and he will hold his book to read it, he will then distance himself from committing bad deeds.

Thus the matter is in his interest, like the student who sees the invigilator in the examination hall and does not hate him, because he protects his right to receive a correct grade, instead of cheating others and taking a greater opportunity than him in grade and success; moreover, all the students know that the presence of an alert invigilator is a motive for them to study.

Therefore I always say: Beware of disliking that you have enemies, because what deceives a person in his conduct is the hypocrisy of his companions toward him; but your enemy keeps his eyes upon you all the time, and therefore you are cautious not to fall into error. On this meaning the poet says:

My enemies have a favour upon me and a merit, for they are like medicine and cure for one who is chronically ill. They searched for my slip, so I avoided it; so my thanks is due to them for their benefit to me. May the Most Merciful never remove my enemies from me, for I have become free of what the Arabs call "ruin" (dhilla)…

So then: the recording of good and bad deeds is a matter for the benefit of the human being; and when they succeed one another over the human being, it is as if they form patrols to protect the individual. For this reason, we find the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: "Angels succeed one another among you by night and angels by day, and they gather at the Fajr prayer and the 'Asr prayer; then those who spent the night among you ascend to Him, and He asks them, while He knows best about you: 'How did you leave My servants?' They say: 'We came to them while they were praying, and we left them while they were praying.'" And it is as if the angels are patrols. And the Glorified says: ﴿Indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed﴾ [17:78], that is, the angels of the night witness, along with the angels of the day. The Hadith of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) takes note of the time-period of human activity: all of a person's movements and work take place from dawn until 'Asr; then a person generally rests after that, and then sleeps.

The mu'aqqibāt come from before and behind a person; and "from before him" is for observation. For this reason we find Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), during the Prophetic Migration, walking for some of the time in front of the Prophet (ﷺ), and walking the rest of the time behind the Prophet (ﷺ). Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) would go forward to watch: is there anyone observing the Messenger or not? Then he would fall back to sweep the whole area with his gaze to see: is there anyone tracking the two of them? Thus Abu Bakr was keen to protect the Messenger (ﷺ) from observation or ambush.

And the Glorified says: ﴿For him are mu'aqqibāt from before him and from behind him; they guard him by the command of Allah...﴾ [13:11].

The superficial reader says: those angels guard the human being from the matter intended for him by Allah.

We say: Allah did not send down the angels to oppose His decree; this guarding does not come from the person's own self for himself, nor from the angels against the decree of Allah. The meaning here is that the angels guard the human being only by the command of Allah. For this reason we find in the Qur'an the saying of the Glorified: ﴿Because of their sins they were drowned...﴾ [71:25], that is, because of their sin they were drowned. So beware of thinking that the angels guard the human being from the decree of Allah, for we know that when the Glorified intends a matter, there is none to repel it.

The Glorified continues: ﴿Indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves...﴾ [13:11]. He is the One who created the vast universe with all its kinds: inanimate, plant, animal, celestial spheres, and angels; and He made all of that subservient to the human being; then Allah, the Exalted, protects and preserves the human being by His Self-Subsistence. Someone may say: "Then why do afflictions befall some people, even though He has said that He protects them?"

We say: those afflictions occur only when humankind changes Allah's method; for the preservation stands as long as the method stands. Read the saying of the Glorified: ﴿And Allah presents an example: a town that was secure and tranquil, its provision coming to it in abundance from every place; but it denied the favours of Allah, so Allah made it taste the garment of hunger and fear for what they used to do﴾ [16:112].

Thus we know that the preservation of the human being, his protection, and his provision, from before he is born, all of this Allah will not withdraw as long as the human being walks upon the Straight Path; but if the human being deviates from the Straight Path, Allah draws his attention with some lessons and admonitions so that he returns to the Straight Path.

The change that Allah makes to people until they change what is in themselves includes secondary provisions; as for the primary provisions, He does not withhold them from them, such as the sun, the moon, the stars, and the air; and He did not prevent the earth from bringing forth water for them.

What befalls them is in things whose occurrence does not stop the universe from proceeding in its regular order, such as a calamity in wealth or a calamity in the self; and the universe remains on its regular course. For this reason we find one of the philosophers having said: "God does not change for your sake; rather, you must change for God's sake."

And the Glorified has already said: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor suffer﴾ [20:123].

And He, the Glorified, says: ﴿And whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed, for him is a constricted life...﴾ [20:124]. You see in our contemporary world affluent societies from whom we import the tools of modern civilization; yet they live in extreme psychological constriction. This proves that material wealth in money or the tools of civilization does not achieve for the human being psychological balance or happiness. What applies to them is what the "Prince of Poets" Ahmad Shawqi (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

"It is not the load that the back can bear; the load is only what the chest contains."

Material wealth may in the opinion of some be the dream, so the person inclines to the crooked path with what it contains of bribes and dishonesty; and despite the money this person may hoard, psychological or physical diseases consume him. Thus we find the Glorified, who changes and is not changed; He is the Changer, not the changed. The saying of the Glorified: ﴿Indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves...﴾ [13:11] clarifies for us that the actions of the limbs arise from a source, a self that moves the limbs; and when the self is sound, the limbs become upright; and when the self is corrupt, the limbs become crooked.

So Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, subjected all the limbs to the desires of the self. If the self opposes the method of Allah, the tongue is subject to it and does not utter tawhid despite its will, because the self that directs it opposes faith.

For example: those who attributed to the messengers whom Allah chose, and claimed that they were the sons of Allah, while He, the Glorified, is far above that. But if the self is faithful, it commands the tongue to say the word of tawhid, and it rejoices in that; yet in both states it does not disobey the self which Allah has subjected to it.

Thus the limbs are moved by the will of their owner, and the human will is released from the limbs only when Allah wills that on the Last Day, and at the true standing.

At that moment no one will be able to control his limbs, for the Dominion on that Day belongs to the One, the Irresistible; the individual's authority over his limbs falls away, and these limbs will testify against their owner for what they did while they were subdued to his will.

Thus we know that the change is entirely in the self that directs the limbs. The saying of the Glorified: ﴿Indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a people...﴾ [13:11] tells us that He does not intervene except when matters become grave, the whole society is corrupted, the self-reproaching soul disappears from this society, and those who are able to deter, even by word, disappear from it; at that point the Glorified intervenes.

When people change what is in themselves, and restore the proper direction of the will over the limbs, their deeds are set right; so beware of thinking that there is anything that can resist Allah. Therefore the Glorified continues in the same verse: ﴿And when Allah intends harm for a people, there is no repelling it...﴾ [13:11].

You must take both together: ﴿Indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves...﴾ [13:11] and ﴿And when Allah intends harm for a people, there is no repelling it...﴾ [13:11].

Then the Glorified says: ﴿And they will not have besides Him any protector﴾ [13:11]. Beware of understanding that there is an authority that prevents Allah from changing what He wills to change; and they will not find another tender breast to pat them if Allah intends evil for them. There is no other protector who takes them from Allah and takes charge of their affairs, bringing good and repelling evil. For this reason the Glorified says: ﴿And they will not have besides Him any protector﴾ [13:11].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 13, verse 12:

After that, the Truth, glory be to Him, speaks of a phenomenon in the universe that has two aspects and is received in two ways: one of them is welcome, and the other is alarming, whether in a single soul or in a single group.

We all know lightning, and we receive it with fear of what alarms us and with hope for what we love and desire. So when lightning comes, we fear the thunderbolts, because thunderbolts usually come after lightning, or the rain-bearing clouds come.

Thus fear and hope come from one phenomenon. Or: fear belongs to one people, while hope and desire belong to other people.

The example I always cite for this is the saying of one of the Arab warriors who described his sword as "an opening for his friends and a death for his enemies."

Another example I cite is what the emir of a town called "al-Shari'ah," which lies between al-Ta'if and Makkah, related to us. The emir of al-Shari'ah told us in the year 1953 about a righteous woman who memorizes the Qur'an; her name is "Aminah."

This woman had two daughters, who were married, and each husband took his wife to his place of residence. One of the two sons-in-law worked in farming, and the other worked in the craft of "al-Shirk" (making mats/nets for water-channels). Aminah said to her husband: "Will you not go and find out about the condition of the two daughters?" So the man went to learn of the condition of the two daughters. The first he met on his journey was his married daughter, the wife of the one who ploughs and sows. He said to her: "How are you, and how is your husband, and how is the world with you and your husband?"

She said: "Father, I am well with him, and he is well with me. As for the state of the world, pray to God for us that He send down rain, for we have ploughed the land and sown the seeds, and we are awaiting the irrigation of the sky."

The father raised his hands to the sky and said: "O God, I ask You for rain for her."

He went to the other daughter and said to her: "How are you? And how is your husband?"

She said: "Well. And I beg you, Father, to pray to God that He withhold the rain, for we have made the shirk (mats) from clay; if it rains, the shirk will be spoiled." So he prayed for her.

He returned to his wife, who had asked him about the condition of the two daughters. He appeared distressed and said: "It is a bad year for one of them," and he related to her the condition of the two daughters, adding: "It will be a burdensome year for one of them."

Aminah said to him: "If you had been patient, I would have told you that what you say may not come to pass, and He, glory be to Him, is able to do that."

He said to her: "By God, indeed, tell me how?" Aminah said: "Have you not read the saying of God:

﴿Have you not seen that Allah drives the clouds, then joins them together, then makes them into a heap, so you see the rain come out from their midst; and He sends down from the sky mountains [of clouds] wherein is hail, and He strikes therewith whom He wills and averts it from whom He wills...﴾ (Surah an-Nur, 24:43)."

The man prostrated to God in gratitude that He had granted him a wife who helped him in the matter of his religion, and he prayed: "O God, turn the rain away from the owner of the shirk, and pour the rain upon the owner of the tilled land." And so it was. This example clearly illustrates the meaning of fear and hope upon seeing the thunder:

﴿He it is who shows you the lightning, [causing] fear and hope...﴾ (Surah ar-Ra'd, 13:12).

Either the fear and hope come from a single soul, in that a person fears the thunderbolts and hopes for the descent of rain, or they come from two opposites: one benefits from this, and another is harmed by it. The Truth, glory be to Him, adds:

﴿And He produces the heavy clouds﴾ (Surah ar-Ra'd, 13:12).

We know that *as-sahab* is the accumulated cloud, and it is heavy when it is laden with water; this is the opposite of the light cloud that appears like tufts of cotton.

The Arabs say: "Do not be impatient with the buckets, for the slowest buckets to fill are the fullest, and the heaviest clouds in their movement are the most laden."

When the bucket is lowered into the well and you raise it, the full bucket is the one that burdens you when you pull it from the well; but the empty bucket is light at the moment you draw it out of the well. Likewise, heavy clouds move slowly because of the water they carry.

Previously, the Truth (may He be exalted) mentioned lightning, which is light; here He mentions thunder, which is sound. We know that the speed of light is greater than the speed of sound; for this reason He mentioned lightning first, and then mentioned thunder after that.

When one of the common people hears someone whose speech he dislikes, he says to him, "You heard thunder," meaning: he asks for him to hear the disturbing sound that tires whoever hears it. We should be mindful that the disturbing things in the universe, when they glorify their Lord, are never disturbing, and you should not think that they are a discordant note in the universe; rather, they are a note that blends with the rest of the tunes of the universe.

We understand that glorification belongs to the rational being capable of speech, but this is [true] of humans; for He who created all beings taught them how to communicate, just as He taught humans how to communicate with their own kind; and likewise He taught every species its language. We all read in the Qur'an what the ant said when she saw the armies of Solomon:

﴿Enter your dwellings, lest Solomon and his armies crush you, while they do not perceive.﴾ (Surah an-Naml) And Solomon, peace be upon him, heard it, because Allah had taught him the speech of those languages. We know that the Truth (may He be exalted) taught Solomon the speech of the birds. He, the Exalted, said:

﴿We have been taught the speech of the birds...﴾ (Surah an-Naml) Did Solomon, peace be upon him, not converse with the hoopoe and speak with it, after Solomon, by Allah's teaching him, deciphered the message of the hoopoe's report? The hoopoe said to Solomon:

﴿I have encompassed [knowledge] that you have not encompassed, and I have come to you from Sheba with certain news. Indeed, I found a woman ruling them, and she has been given of all things, and she has a great throne.﴾ (Surah an-Naml)

So, everything has a language by which it communicates to fulfil its needs, and whoever Allah bestows upon of the secrets of His creation hears these languages; the Truth (may He be exalted) bestowed this upon Solomon, so he understood the language of the birds and spoke with it to the hoopoe; and he said to it:

﴿Take this letter of mine and deliver it to them, then withdraw from them and see what they will return.﴾ (Surah an-Naml) Thus we have learned of the story of Solomon and Bilqis, and how Solomon understood the speech of the birds and spoke with it to the hoopoe. And thus we learn how a person learns many languages: when a person goes to another society and stays there for a period, he learns the language of that society, and a person can learn more than one language.

The Truth (may He be exalted) has presented the question of the existence of languages for beings in the story of the ant and the story of the hoopoe with Solomon; these are of the rank after humans. The Truth (may He be exalted) also presents the matter of every creature among His creatures having a language in His saying:

﴿And We subjected the mountains to glorify [Allah] with David, and the birds; and We were doing [that].﴾ (Surah al-Anbiya') It is as if the mountains understood David's glorification and echoed it after him. Also, the Truth (may He be exalted) says:

﴿Indeed, We subjected the mountains to glorify [Allah] with him, at evening and sunrise, and the birds assembled; all were turning back to Him.﴾ (Surah Sad)

Likewise, Allah addresses the earth and the heaven, saying:

﴿Then He said to it and to the earth, "Come both of you willingly or by compulsion."﴾ (Surah Fussilat)

So they comply with His command: ﴿They said, "We come willingly."﴾ (Surah Fussilat) Thus we know that every species has a language by which it communicates, and we notice that every kind of animal has a sound that differs from one kind to another, and scientists are now studying the language of fish and trying to compile a lexicon for it. So when you hear:

﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them exalt Him. And there is not a thing except that it exalts [Allah] by His praise...﴾ (Surah al-Isra') Understand that there is no creature except that it has a language, and it glorifies the Most Generous Creator with it. Then He, the Exalted, says:

﴿But you do not understand their glorification...﴾ (Surah al-Isra') just as an person ignorant of English does not understand the language of the English.

Some have said: the intended meaning here is the glorification of indication (tasbih al-dalalah) to the Creator, and He, glorified be He, has decreed that we cannot understand the glorification of indication.

But I say: contemporary science has reached the study of the languages of creatures and proved them; accordingly, the glorification of creatures is by speech and communication between a speaker and a listener, and moreover those creatures have emotions as well.

We see scientists in our age studying the emotions of trees toward the human who waters them. Here is an experiment describing scientists measuring the vibration of plants while they were being watered by a farmer responsible for them; then the man died; they measured the vibration of those plants and found it disturbed, as though those plants had grieved for the one who used to care for them. Thus scientists arrived at the knowledge that plants have emotions.

Allah, the Truth (may He be exalted), has also shown us that inanimate things have emotions too, as evidenced by His saying about the people of Pharaoh:

﴿So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them...﴾ (Surah ad-Dukhan) So the heaven and the earth were relieved at the departure of these evil ones from the earth; the heavens and the earth are bound together with the universe in a commitment by which they do not deviate from Allah's intentions, and when a disbeliever comes to create a discord in the universe through his disbelief, they rejoice at his disappearance and do not grieve for him.

Since the heaven and the earth do not weep for the disbeliever upon his departure, it must be that they rejoice at this departure, and it must be that they weep at the departure of the believer.

Hence we find the saying of Imam Ali, may Allah honour his face: "When the son of Adam dies, two places weep for him: a place in the heaven and a place on the earth. As for his place on the earth, it is the place of his prayer; and as for his place in the heaven, it is the ascent of his deeds." Thus we find that the meaning of the Truth's saying:

﴿And the thunder glorifies [Allah] with His praise...﴾ (Surah ar-Ra'd) i.e., the thunder declares Allah free of imperfection and glorifies the name of the Truth, blessed and exalted, with glorification accompanied by praise.

When we declare the Essence of Allah free from being like the rest of essences, and when we declare the acts of Allah free from being like the acts of others, glorified be He, and when we declare the attributes of Allah free from being like attributes, this must be accompanied by praise of Him, glorified be He, because He is exempt from all those changing attributes; and we must rejoice that He is exempt. He, exalted, says:

﴿And the thunder glorifies [Allah] with His praise, and the angels from fear of Him...﴾ (Surah ar-Ra'd) One may ask: how do the angels fear Allah, when they are those of whom the Truth, glorified be He, said:

﴿They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded.﴾ (Surah at-Tahrim)

I say: the angels fear Allah with the fear of awe and the fear of majesty. We see in our lives someone who loves his leader or commander, so his fear is reverence; how much more so, then, the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, whom His angels love and whose majesty and perfection they revere. It is true that the angels are subjugated, yet they fear their Lord above them.

When the angels hear the thunder, they do not fear for themselves, but they fear for the people, because they are guardians over them; the angels are aware of their mission as guardians over humans, and they fear that any matter might confuse them, and they seek forgiveness for those on the earth.

So His saying:

﴿And the thunder glorifies [Allah] with His praise, and the angels from fear of Him...﴾ (Surah ar-Ra'd) shows us that the angels fear for humans from the thunder; they are charged with protecting them, along with their fear of Allah in awe and reverence.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said in the noble hadith: "No day dawns upon the servants except that two angels descend, and one of them says: 'O Allah, give the one who spends a replacement,' and the other says: 'O Allah, give the one who withholds destruction.'" Someone may think this is a supplication against the one who withholds; but I say: why not take it as a supplication of goodness? The one who spends has received reward for the good deeds he performed; as for the one who withholds, when Allah tests him with the loss of some of his wealth and he endures patiently, he receives the reward of patience. He, glorified be He, continues in the same verse:

﴿And He sends the thunderbolts and strikes with them whom He wills, while they dispute about Allah, and He is mighty in plan.﴾ (Surah ar-Ra'd)

There must be a painful event in the universe to awaken these people from their heedlessness. Here is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): two of the great obstinate opponents, Arbad ibn Rabi'ah, brother of Labid ibn Rabi'ah, and Amir ibn at-Tufayl, came to him to dispute with him, aiming to stall and to search for a slip in what he says or a weakness in his knowledge. The example is what similar disputants said, which the noble Qur'an related:

﴿When we have died and become dust and bones, will we indeed be resurrected?﴾ (Surah al-Mu'minun) and likewise the hastening of some disputants for the punishment.

These two came and said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Is our Lord made of iron or of copper?" They said that because they were worshippers of idols made of stone, and what is stronger than stone is iron or copper. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) supplicated, and a thunderbolt descended and burned them.

The sending of thunderbolts here is a Qur'anic sign, and there must be a cosmic sign that confirms it; and that cosmic sign did occur. The Truth (may He be exalted) says:

﴿while they dispute about Allah...﴾ (Surah ar-Ra'd)

Disputing about Allah has many kinds: disputing about His Essence, disputing about His attributes, or disputing about good and evil. They also disputed about the sending down of a material sign upon him, for they were not content with the Qur'an as a sign, although the Qur'an is a miraculous sign and of the kind in which they excelled, namely language.

They also disputed about thunder, and said: thunder has no intellect to glorify; and the angels have no obligation, so how do they glorify?

But the Truth (may He be exalted) said: He is able to send thunderbolts and strike with them whom He wills; He brings good to whom He wills, and inflicts harm on whom He wills. Do they possess all the time for this dispute, after He created all this universe?

Do you have the time for all this contention, for the purpose of disputing and blameworthy obstinacy? Disputation in itself may be used well or misused; the Truth (may He be exalted) told us:

﴿And do not dispute with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is best...﴾ (Surah al-Ankabut)

He also said:

﴿Allah has already heard the statement of the woman who is pleading with you concerning her husband and complaining to Allah...﴾ (Surah al-Mujadilah)

This is a dispute whose purpose is to reach the truth. Allah concludes the verse of Surat ar-Ra'd with His saying:

﴿And He is mighty in plan.﴾ (Surah ar-Ra'd)

It is said: "Mahala fulan bi-fulan" meaning: he plotted against him secretly and schemed against him; and al-mihal is secret plotting and scheming. Those among humans who resort to it are the weak who cannot confront the opponent openly, so they plot against him in secret, hiding the means of harm.

This happens among humans with one another, because humans do not know the unseen; but when Allah plots, no one can match His plot, and He, glorified be He, says:

﴿Indeed, they are plotting a plot, and I am plotting a plot. So give time to the disbelievers; give them time, gently.﴾ (Surah at-Tariq) Because the plot of Allah has no overcomer, and it is a plot not exposed to anyone. Therefore He, exalted, says:

﴿And they plot, and Allah plots; and Allah is the best of plotters.﴾ (Surah al-Anfal) They wanted to plot against His Messenger (ﷺ) and wanted to kill him; they brought a young man from every tribe to hold a sword, so that his blood would be dispersed among the tribes, and they lay in ambush for him. But the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was accompanied by divine care, so he went out upon them, reciting the saying of the Exalted:

﴿And We covered them, so they do not see.﴾ (Surah Ya-Sin) Thus he made clear to them that they would never be able to repel the call of Islam, neither by open confrontation and public declaration, nor by plotting and secret ambush; even if you sought help from the jinn. A human may plot and confront, and when he fails he may try to seek help from a power of another kind that has authority like the authority of the jinn; yet even that did not succeed with him (ﷺ), for they tried sorcery, and Allah revealed to him in a dream the place where the sorcery was placed.

Some of his companions went to extract the sorcery from the place the Messenger of Allah had specified for them. Thus the Truth (may He be exalted) made clear to them that everything they do would never befall His Messenger (ﷺ); for He is:

﴿Dominant over His affair...﴾ (Surah Yusuf)

Thus Allah, the Truth, was and still is, and will remain until He inherits the earth and whoever is upon it; and He is mighty in plan.

And He, glorified is He, has called us to believe in one God, and this is a call to truth, while those who are worshipped besides Him are called upon as if they were a god that is not true. The pronoun here may refer to God, as if God has called His creation to the word of truth, which is "There is no god but Allah." He, glorified is He, has testified that there is no god but Him. The angels have testified by direct witnessing, and those possessing knowledge have testified by reasoned inference. That is the call of truth.

Or the pronoun may refer to "to Him" meaning the human being who calls to the truth. When a person supplicates, this indicates that a matter has gone beyond the scope of his means, and so he calls upon someone who will help him in this matter.

Supplication (du'a') is a form of request, but requests differ according to the one requesting and the one from whom the request is made. If the one requesting is lower in rank than the one from whom he requests, it is not called fi'l amr (the imperative verb) in grammatical analysis (i'rab, the study of case endings and sentence structure). An example is your saying, "O Lord, forgive me," which is not called fi'l amr but is called du'a'. Rather, it is called fi'l du'a' (the verb of supplication).

Thus we see that if the imperative is from the lower to the higher, we do not call it fi'l amr; rather we call it du'a'. The intelligent student of i'rab is the one who notices, during analysis, whether the request is from the lower to the higher; he does not say "fi'l amr" but says "fi'l du'a'," as in the servant's saying to God, "O Lord, forgive me." If the request is between equals, he says "iltimas" (request between equals). If the request has come from the higher to the lower, it is "fi'l amr."

When a person calls upon his Lord, this means that the servant's means have been exhausted, and he turns to the One who is above the universe and possesses all means. Therefore each of us calls upon God, because He, glorified is He, is able to fulfill the requests of His servants, and nothing overwhelms Him.

But if you call upon one who is not able, the supplication does not benefit the servant. They used to call upon idols, and idols neither harm nor benefit. The idol of these people cannot act by itself or for itself, for it was made of stone. Naturally, supplicating such idols accomplishes nothing, because they are unable to do anything.

Thus it becomes clear to us that the call of truth is to call upon the One who is able. As for those who call upon false deities, these will disappoint the one who calls upon them in his aim. Therefore the Truthful, glorified is He, says here: ﴿To Him is the call of truth; and those they invoke besides Him do not respond to them with anything.. (14)﴾ (Surat ar-Ra'd), because they possess nothing. The idol of these people does not hear, so how could it respond? Then the Truthful, glorified is He, strikes a comparison with a tangible thing that we all do, saying: ﴿They do not respond to them with anything, except like one who stretches out his hands toward the water so that it reaches his mouth, but it will not reach it.. (14)﴾ (Surat ar-Ra'd).

The thirsty person, as soon as he sees water, stretches his hand toward it to scoop some up; but his hand does not reach the water. This is the state of one who calls upon other than God: he asks one who is not able to fulfill his need. Thus is the supplication to other than God, and it is supplication in error and in futility.

Prostration, as we know it, is one of the movements of the prayer (ṣalāh), and prayer is the servant's standing before his Lord after He has called him. Prayer consists of words and actions that begin with the takbīr and end with the salām, with specific obligatory elements (farā'iḍ), recommended practices (sunan) and preferred acts (mustaḥabbāt).

Prostration (sujūd) is the movement that manifests complete submission to God. Prostration is the placing of the highest part of a person at the lowest level, which is the person's foot. We find the common people saying: "Do not raise your head over me," meaning: do not be arrogant toward me, because raising the head signifies haughtiness, while lowering it through bowing (rukū') or prostration (sujūd) is a display of submission. So when God says: ﴿And to God prostrate whoever is in the heavens and the earth…﴾ [13:15]

You must understand that this is what actually happens, and if your mind does not stretch to grasp prostration as it occurs from you, then let your assumption stretch to the understanding that it is the ultimate in submission and humility before God, the Commander.

You know that the whole universe is subjected to God's command and is at God's disposal, and the cosmos is submissive to Him, glory be to Him. If a human responds to God's command by believing in Him, this is good. If a human does not respond, as the disbeliever does, then upon him is the evil of his deeds.

If you were to examine the matter with precise understanding, you would find that the disbeliever only rebels by his will, which dominates his limbs; but the rest of his parts are subjected, and all of them perform their function by God's subjugation of them, and all of them execute the commands issued to them from God. Thus the disbeliever is rebellious with one part of himself and subjected with another part. When God makes him ill, can he disobey? Certainly not. When God wills to stop his heart, can he make his heart oppose God's will? Certainly not.

Therefore, the one who is accustomed to rebelling against God in worship, and is skilled in this rebellion, should try to rebel against God's wills in matters over which he has no choice, and he will meet with inability to do so.

He must know that he has rebelled in disbelief only by the choice that God has granted him to an extent; the proof is that ninety-nine percent of his capacities are governed by compulsion, and only one percent of his capacities are left to choice, and thus subjugation is confirmed.

The disbeliever's submission for the most part, and his rebellion in another part, is the ultimate greatness of God, for he does not dare to rebel with that which God has made subject to him. Someone might say: Why did God say here:

﴿And to God prostrate whoever is in the heavens and the earth…﴾ [13:15]

and not say: "what is in the heavens and what is in the earth"?

I say: since prostration is mentioned here, it is a proof of the height of intellect, and He, glory be to Him, has made prostration here a proof that all creatures comprehend the reality of divinity and worship the Truth, glory be to Him. Here He says: ﴿And to God prostrate whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly…﴾ [13:15]

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, teaches us that all creatures submit to God in prostration, whether the subjugated, or even the parts of the disbeliever that he uses by his will in disbelief in God; these parts prostrate to God. The Truth, glory be to Him, continues: ﴿and their shadows, morning and evening﴾ [13:15].

In our daily life we hear someone say: "So-and-so follows so-and-so like his shadow," meaning he never refuses him at all, and sticks to him as if he were the shadow; and we know that a person's shadow follows his movement.

Thus we know that the shadows themselves are submissive to God, because their owners are submissive to God; the shadow follows its movement. Beware of thinking that it is submissive to you; rather, it is submissive to God, glory be to Him.

Here He specifies this matter by "morning and evening." "Al-ghuduww" is the plural of "ghadāh," which is the beginning of the day, and "al-āṣāl" is the time span between the afternoon ('aṣr) and the sunset (maghrib).

When you measure your shadow in the morning you will find the shadow long, and the closer you get to the sun, the longer the shadow becomes; and as midday (zawāl) approaches, the shadow shortens until it disappears. The clearest sign of the shadow swaying with the movement of its owner is in the morning and after the afternoon.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 13, verse 16:

And "Qul" (say) is a command to the Messenger that he should say it to the disbelievers. And there are other verses in which He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And if you asked them, "Who created them?" they would surely say, "Allah." So how are they deluded?﴾ (Surah az-Zukhruf 43:87)

One may ask: why did the Truth, glory be to Him, give the answer here, and not leave it to come from them?

We say: the coming of the answer from the Truth here, concerning the One who created the heavens and the earth, is stronger than if the answer had come from them.

An example from our own lives, and to Allah belongs the highest similitude: you say to your young son, who is quarrelling with his older brother, "Who brought you the new outfit?" He becomes flustered with embarrassment, because he knows that the one who brought the new outfit is his older brother with whom he quarrelled. So you say: "Your older brother brought it to you, the one you quarrelled with."

Here, at the moment the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) says to them what Allah commanded him to say:

﴿Say, "Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?"﴾ (Surah ar-Ra'd 13:16)

then they will be perplexed; so He then confirms for them what Allah commanded him to say: ﴿Say, "Allah."﴾ (Surah ar-Ra'd 13:16)

The command of Allah to His Messenger (ﷺ) continues, and the Truth, glory be to Him, says to him: ﴿Say, "Have you then taken, besides Him, protectors who do not possess for themselves any benefit or harm?"﴾ (Surah ar-Ra'd 13:16). Thus the Messenger, by conveying the Truth, glory be to Him, reveals to them the extent of their ignorance, for they had already acknowledged that Allah is the Creator of the heavens and the earth, and not one of them dared to attribute the creation of the heavens and the earth to the idols.

Here the Messenger (ﷺ) makes clear to them what the Truth, glory be to Him, commanded to be made clear: Allah created the heavens and the earth; will you after that take besides Him protectors who possess for themselves no benefit or harm? The proof is that the idol of these people is not able to do anything for them. The Truth, glory be to Him, continues:

﴿Say, "Are the blind and the seeing equal? Or are the darknesses and the light equal? Or have they assigned to Allah partners who created like His creation, so that the creation became confused to them?"﴾ (Surah ar-Ra'd 13:16)

Naturally, the blind cannot be equal to the one who sees. When you see "am" (or), know that it is a transitional particle; thus the Truth denounces what they have done by questioning about it, because it is indeed a reprehensible thing:

﴿Or have they assigned to Allah partners who created like His creation, so that the creation became confused to them?﴾ (Surah ar-Ra'd 13:16). That is: if these partners had created anything like the creation of Allah, they would have had grounds to draw a comparison between the creation of Allah and the creation of these partners. But these partners who were made sharers with Allah in divinity cannot create anything; so how do they choose them as partners of Allah? Then the command comes from the Truth, glory be to Him:

﴿Say, "Allah is the Creator of everything, and He is the One, the Subduer."﴾ (Surah ar-Ra'd 13:16)

In another verse the Truth, glory be to Him, offers an explanation of that verse:

﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it...﴾ (Surah al-Hajj 22:73)

So these partners have not created anything, and no one can claim that these partners have any intention of creating. But the coming of "lan" (never) here confirms that even with their being alerted to that matter, they will be unable to do it, because negation of the future implies a challenge, despite their being multiple gods; and even if they gathered together, they would never create anything. The challenge continues in His words, glory be to Him: ﴿And if the fly should snatch away from them a thing, they could not recover it from it. Weak are the seeker and the sought.﴾ (Surah al-Hajj 22:73). That is: even if the fly were to take away with its slender leg something of what they possess, they could not retrieve it from it. Thus it becomes clear that the Truth, glory be to Him, alone is the Creator of everything; worship is due to Him alone, without partner; He, may He be exalted, is the one singled out in lordship and divinity; He is the Subduer, the Proud, and the One who always prevails over His command. How, then, could anyone besides Him be equal to Him? Therefore He has no partner whatsoever.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 13, verse 17:

He, glorified is He, sends down water from above, from the heavens. We know that water evaporates from the seas, the rivers, and the land in which springs gush forth, so that it gathers as clouds. Then the clouds pile up, one upon another, and pass through a cold region, and the rain falls. The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow according to their measure...﴾ [13:17].

The valley (wadi) is the low ground between two mountains. When rain falls on the mountains, it flows into the valleys, and every valley holds water in proportion to its extent. We should observe that the wisdom of God willed this, so that the water would not turn into a flood. Had the water increased in those valleys, the villages would have been drowned as a result, the crops would have been ruined, and the houses would have collapsed.

An example of this is the flooding of the Nile, when it came in an amount suited to the size of the riverbed. Such a measure of flooding was what made the people of Egypt happy. But when it increased, it became a danger that bore down upon the villages and destroyed them. Thus we find that among the mercy of the Truth, glorified is He, is that the water flows from the sky as rain in proportion to the extent of the valleys, except when He wills otherwise.

Here the Truth, glorified is He, wishes to give an example of what benefits people; therefore He brought the detail of water descending in proportion to the extent of the valleys. Whoever has seen the scene of rain falling in this measure can observe that the flow of the torrent sweeps away all the straw and filth; those extraneous things form a foam on the surface of the water that runs in the river, then the water rushes into the channel to push that foam aside, so that the water thereafter flows clear and sparkling.

﴿He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow according to their measure, and the torrent carries a swelling foam...﴾ [13:17]. This example is understood by the people of the desert, since it is a land of desert, mountains, and valleys. So what about an example suited to the people of the settled towns? The Truth, glorified is He, brings this suitable example for them, saying: ﴿And from that which they heat in the fire, seeking an ornament or goods, there is a foam like it...﴾ [13:17].

When you go to the workshop of a blacksmith or a goldsmith of gold and silver, you find him kindling the fire so that the metal turns into molten liquid, and the scum (zabad) floats on top of this liquid, namely the things that entered the metal and are not originally part of it; and the metal remains pure after that.

The craftsman places gold in the fire to purify it of impurities, then adds to it materials that strengthen its hardness, or moves it from a state of purity to a lesser degree of purity. The state of purity in gold is what we call "24 karat," and the lesser grade is gold of "21 karat," and less than that is gold of "18 karat." Pure gold is soft; therefore they add to it what increases its hardness, and the goldsmith makes from this gold the ornament.

This is the example suited to the people of the settled towns, when they make ornaments; and they also make other tools that they use, and that the people of the desert use with them, such as swords for example, which must be made of hardened iron; for every tool made from it has the hardness suited to it. If the blacksmith wishes to make a sword, he must choose for it a type of iron that suits the functions of the sword.

The foam on the water descending from the sky comes about as a result of the rain passing over the surface of the mountains as it falls, in addition to washing the bed of the river in which it descends; and this foam usually accumulates on the banks, so that the water remains clear thereafter.

When you look at the Nile, for example, you find impurities that have settled on both sides of the river and its banks; and likewise when you look at the waters of the sea, you find what the ship casts out, floating above the waves, so that the waves throw it onto the shore.

Thus God struck the example for the people of the desert and the people of the settled towns with what benefits them in their lives: whether an ornament they wear, or a tool with which they fight, or another tool they use in the various aspects of their livelihood. In all of this they resort to refining the metals from which they make those ornaments or tools of life, so that they extract the metals from the dross or the scum. And likewise the Truth, glorified is He, does: ﴿Thus God strikes the truth and falsehood; as for the foam, it passes away as refuse, but as for that which benefits people, it remains on the earth...﴾ [13:17].

When God strikes truth with falsehood, He extracts what benefits people and removes what harms them. His saying ﴿so it passes away as refuse...﴾ [13:17] means He drives it away; "jufa'" means "cast out," from the word "al-jufwa" (estrangement); and it is said: "So-and-so jafa so-and-so," meaning he distanced him from himself. The Truth, glorified is He, concludes the noble verse with His saying: ﴿Thus God strikes the parables﴾ [13:17].

He, glorified is He, willed to show us through tangible matters what equals immaterial matters, so that a person knows that injustice, when it spreads, rises high and obliterates the truth, is headed for extinction; its likeness is that of the foam.

Those who respond to the Lord, who created from nothing, provided for them the means of life, and preserved the species through marriage and multiplication; so when He calls them to something, let them know that what He asks of them completes their own benefit, for He is the One who originated everything for them from the beginning.

As for those who respond to Him, theirs is the best reward (al-husna). He, glory be to Him, made the world a field for the Hereafter. In this world you are left to your own capacity to take up the causes (al-asbab); but in the Hereafter you are left to the Causer (al-musabbib). In this world you sow, plough, water and harvest, and your life may vary in hardship and ease according to your ability to deal with causes.

So when you respond to God and follow His method, you move to another life in which you live with the Causer, not with causes. Thus, when a thing crosses your mind, you find it before you. For in the other life, God does not leave you to causes; rather you are left to the Essence of God Himself, and what is left to the Essence endures with the endurance of the Essence. This is why we find the Real, glory be to Him, saying: ﴿So as for those who believed in God and held fast to Him, He will admit them into mercy from Himself...﴾ [An-Nisa' 4:175].

Some exegetes say, "It is Paradise," and I say: this is an acceptable explanation, because Paradise is from the mercy of God; but Paradise endures by God's preserving it, whereas God's mercy endures by the endurance of God. Here the Real, glory be to Him, says: ﴿For those who responded to their Lord is the best reward...﴾ [Ar-Ra'd 13:18].

He, exalted, also says in another verse: ﴿For those who did good is the best reward and more...﴾ [Yunus 10:26].

Al-husna is the better matter. He, glory be to Him, created for you in this world the causes through which you toil; but in the Hereafter you live with everything you wish for without toil, and this is the good.

Suppose the world has advanced, and those who travel to the advanced countries and stay in luxurious hotels are told: "Press this button and coffee will come down for you," and "the other button brings you tea."

Everything you can obtain as soon as you ask for it from the restaurant, where others prepare it for you. But however much the world advances, it will never reach the point where what passes through your mind comes to you the moment you wish for it; this will happen only in the Hereafter.

The word "al-husna" is feminine and is the elative form (af'al tafdil); one says "hasanah wa husna." In the masculine one says "hasan wa ahsan." Its opposite, for those who do not respond, is well known. Here the Real, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And those who did not respond to Him, even if they had everything on earth and the like of it with it, they would surely ransom themselves with it...﴾ [Ar-Ra'd 13:18]

That is, they say: "Take all that I possess and free me," but it will not be accepted from him. The Real, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Those, for them is the evil of the reckoning, and their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place﴾ [Ar-Ra'd 13:18]. Because reckoning may result once in good and another time in evil; and the Real, glory be to Him, used the word:

﴿And wretched is the resting place﴾ [Ar-Ra'd 13:18] here, because one of these people, God forbid, will be unable to move at the moment he is placed in the Fire, just as a newborn infant cannot move in its cradle; and it is certain that Hellfire is a wretched resting place.

The believer is the one who knows that the Qur'an, which carries the method (al-manhaj), is what Allah, glorified is He, sent down upon His Messenger; and he cannot be compared with the disbeliever, who is described here by the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿Is one who is blind⁠﴾.

And here He used "knowledge" (ʿilm) and "blindness" (ʿamā); because the signs that point to His power are visible things. And the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Only those of understanding remember⁠﴾, meaning: those who possess minds capable of reflection (tadabbur), contemplation (tafakkur), and discernment (tamyīz).

Whoever among those of understanding (ulu al-albab) believes in God for a moment knows that he has entered into a covenant with God not to worship anyone other than Him; not to submit to anyone other than Him; not to draw near to anyone other than Him; and not to look to or expect anything from anyone other than Him. This is the first covenant of faith.

From this first doctrinal covenant branches out every covenant that is made, whether in relation to God or in relation to the creatures of God; for what arises from the covenant of God is like the covenant of God itself. So if you have believed in God, you believe in the method (manhaj) that He sent down upon His Messenger; and if you fulfil the method, you have fulfilled the first covenant. For this reason we find that all the important, prominent and strong obligations (taklifat) in the life of believers come from Almighty God in the form of the passive voice, what is called "al-bina' lil-majhul" (the passive construction), such as His saying:

﴿Fasting has been prescribed for you...﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 183)

And His saying:

﴿Retaliation has been prescribed for you concerning the slain...﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 178)

And His saying:

﴿Fighting has been prescribed for you, while it is hateful to you...﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 216)

Every obligation comes preceded by the word "kutiba" (has been prescribed), and the One who prescribes is God. He, glory be to Him, has not imposed obligations except upon those who believe in Him. So the moment you declare your faith in God is the moment you contract with God to carry out what He imposes on you. You are free to believe or not to believe; but at the moment you believe in God, you enter into commitment to what He imposes on you, and you have entered into writing the covenant of faith between you and God.

For this reason the Almighty said "kutiba" and did not say "kutibta" (I have prescribed); because the covenant between you and God requires that you enter as a partner in it, and He, glory be to Him, has not imposed obligations except on those who believe in Him. Here He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Those who fulfil the covenant of God and do not break the solemn pledge﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 20)

That is: the covenant of faith is confirmed by what you have taken upon yourself of commitment.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 13, verse 21:

The first thing Allah commanded to be joined is the bond of kinship (ṣilat al-raḥim); that is, that you join those whom lineage ties you to. The true believer, if he traces the lines of descent, will find that all believers enter into the bond of kinship, because all believers are interlinked kin. If you have ten believers whom you join by the bond of kinship, and every believer joins ten like you, consider the overlapping and orderliness of the circles: you will find that all believers are included in them.

For this reason we find that the Exalted says in the hadith qudsi:

"I am the Merciful. I created the womb (raḥim) and derived for it a name from My name. Whoever joins it, I join him; and whoever severs it, I sever him."

A story has also been related about Mu'awiya, may Allah be pleased with him: his chamberlain (ḥājib) came to announce that a man at the door was saying, "He is your brother, O Commander of the Faithful."

Mu'awiya's chamberlain must have known that Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan had no brothers, but he did not wish to intervene in what the man was saying. Mu'awiya said to his chamberlain: "Do you not know my brothers?" The chamberlain said: "This is what the man says." Mu'awiya permitted the man to enter and asked him: "Which of my brothers are you?" The man replied: "Your brother in Adam." Mu'awiya said: "A severed kinship; by Allah, I will be the first to join it."

Al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad met a group of people who had a need of him, and he said to them: "Where are you from?" They said: "From Khurasan." He said: "Fear Allah, and be wherever you wish."

Allah has commanded us to join first the family (ahl), then the relatives (aqārib), then the circles further and further away, then the neighbour. All of this is because He, Exalted, desires cohesion among creation, so that the beneficial reaches the non-beneficial, and the capable reaches the incapable. Thus your neighbour and your poor relative: if you join him, Allah joins you. For this reason, the Exalted commands His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and through him commands every believer with his message: ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any reward for it, except love for the near of kin.﴾ (Surah al-Shura: 23).

Some who heard this verse said: "The near of kin is your kin among your kin." Others said: "No, the near of kin is the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, because the Qur'an said of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him:

﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves﴾ (Surah al-Ahzab: 6). Thus the kinship of the Messenger is more deserving for every believer than his own particular kinship."

The Exalted's speech continues describing the people of understanding (ulu al-albab): ﴿And they fear their Lord and dread an evil reckoning﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd: 21). Fear (khashya) is of that which can afflict one with harm; for this reason the Truth here made the fear to be of Him, Exalted. That is, they fear Allah, their Owner, their Creator, and their Nourisher, with a fear of reverence and exaltation. He, Exalted, made the object of fear the evil punishment; and you say: "I feared Zayd," and you say: "I feared illness." There is something you fear, and there is something that befalls you that you fear.

The people of understanding fear the evil of the Truth's reckoning for them; this fear prompts them to join what He, Exalted, has commanded to be joined, and to keep away from anything that angers Him. We know that an evil reckoning occurs through close scrutiny and the servant's full exaction of all his rights; He, Exalted, is far above wronging anyone, but whoever is subjected to a searching reckoning is one who receives punishment. We seek refuge in Allah from that, for no one is able to bear the punishment of the Truth against him.

And we find this verse linked to what precedes it, the attributes of *ulu al-albab* (people of understanding) who remember and recognize the places of truth through their intellects, guided by evidence. They fulfill the covenant of faith simply by their belief in God in the fundamentals of the doctrine of divine oneness and in what the requirements of the law that this doctrine brings.

For this reason, He (glorified is He) made it a transaction, which He clarified in His saying, may He be exalted:

﴿Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties, [promising] that they will have Paradise. They fight in the way of God, so they kill and are killed. [That is] a true promise [binding] upon Him.﴾ (Surat al-Tawbah) (111)

This is a transaction of offer and acceptance, and the covenant is an offer and acceptance. It is a pact confirmed first by innate evidence (*fitrah*) and second by rational evidence.

In this verse, they are those who sought the face of their Lord through patience. Patience (*sabr*) is bearing the hardships that befall the human soul, which divert it from the composure of its uprightness, its bliss and its happiness. Everything that takes the human soul out of the harmony of its order needs patience.

Patience requires a patient person, who is the believing human, and it requires something to be patient about. What one is patient about in events may be within the self itself, such as when a person endures the hardship of obligation that says "do" and "do not do."

Obligation commands you to leave what you love, to carry out some of what is difficult for you, and to comply by staying away from what it forbids you. All of this requires the striving of the self and the patience of the self over the hardships of obligation. For this reason, the Truth (glorified is He) says, for example, about prayer: ﴿You are only a warner, and for every people is a guide.﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd) (45)[^1] This is the patience of the self over the self.

But there is another kind of patience: patience on your part toward something that happens from someone else, which takes you out of the uprightness of your soul and its happiness. This is divided into two types: a type in which you find an opponent (*gharim*) to you, and a type in which you find no opponent. The illness that takes a person out of the sphere of healthy uprightness and causes you pain has no opponent for you, but you find an opponent when a person attacks you, for example by beating you, and this one who attacks you is your opponent.

Every patience has a capacity of faith that bears it. Whoever endures something that has no opponent, his patience is somewhat reasonable, because there is no one to stir his feelings. But a person's patience over pain inflicted on him by someone he sees before him requires great strength of self-control, lest the person become agitated and think of revenge. For this reason, you find that the Truth distinguishes between the two matters: between something that has befallen you without an opponent in it, and something that has befallen you where you have an equal opponent. About patience where you have no opponent, He says: ﴿And be patient over what befalls you. Indeed, that is of the determination of matters.﴾ (Surat Luqman) (17) And about the patience in which you have an opponent, which requires the restraint of anger and the control of rage, He says: ﴿And whoever is patient and forgives, indeed that is of the determination of matters.﴾ (Surat al-Shura) (43).

When the Truth (glorified is He) wants you to be patient, He does not ask this of you alone, but He asks all those who face you to be patient over their harming you. So it is as if He asked you to be patient over the harm that comes to you from others, while you are one individual.

He also asked others to be patient over harming you. This is the summit of social security for the life of the human soul. So if He (glorified is He) has asked you to be patient over the one who harmed you, He has asked people all together to be patient over harming them.

Thus, if a hasty thing from the transgressors comes from you, and you err against another person and hurt him, you still have a store of other people's patience with you, because the Truth (glorified is He) asked the one opposite you to be patient with you and to pardon.

If you have an opponent, patience requires of you three stages. First, you are patient at the initial level by restraining yourself within, but the anger remains, even if you prevent the impulse of action from expressing this anger, so you do not strike and do not harm. This is called:

﴿Those who restrain [their] anger.﴾ (Surat Al 'Imran) (134) *Kazm* (restraint) is derived from the process of tying the waterskin in which we carry water. If we do not firmly tie it, the water spills out of it, and it is said "*kazama al-qirbah*," meaning he tied it securely.

Then the Truth (glorified is He) brings the second stage after restraining anger, saying: ﴿And those who pardon people.﴾ (Surat Al 'Imran) (134)

Here the more elevated matter appears, which is removing anger from the chest, then rising to the rank of the truthful (*siddiqin*). One does not look at the one whose anger he restrained only at first, but pardons him, and does not regard him with enmity, but with a believing outlook. The believing outlook is that whoever harms you is only transgressing against God's right in you. Thereby God places you on His side and at His flank. Thus you find that whoever wronged you and mistreated you has placed you in God's company and protection, and you must do good to him.

Patience has motives. There are those who are patient so that it will be said of them that they possess endurance and patience, and to show that they are above events. This is patience not seeking the face of God, but patience so that their enemies will not gloat over them.

And there is patience because one has realized through his reason that his distress will not benefit him. Had he been wise, he would have been patient for the face of God, because patience for the face of God lightens the decree of God.

Whoever is patient for the face of God knows that God has a wisdom higher than the matter over which he is patient. If he were given the choice between what should have happened and what actually happened, he would choose what happened.

The one who is patient for the face of God looks for wisdom in the decree that befell him, and says: "I praise You, my Lord, for all Your decree and Your beautiful power, with the praise of contentment with Your judgment, out of certainty in Your wisdom."

So whoever is patient over poverty and says to his self, "Be patient until God relieves it," and does not ask anyone, will find relief has come to him from God. Look at the poet when he says:

*If you wish to extract wealth, spending it,*
*Ask your soul to spend from the treasure of its patience.*
*If you do, you will be the rich one,*
*And if you refuse, [you will remain] in the hardship of the self's desires,*
*And a warning of the hour of ease.*

*So every withholder after it is excused.*

That is: if your self urges you to borrow money to spend on its desires, and you reject that urging, and ask your self to give you from the treasure of patience that you possess; if you do this, you will be the rich one, because you have prevailed over yourself.

The one who turns his attention to the event alone grows weary. But the one who turns his attention to the event linked with its origin from his Lord and says, "There must be a wisdom from God behind this," is the one who is patient seeking His face. God wants to single out whoever is patient seeking His face with a high station, because he knows that God has wisdom in what He causes of decrees. Then He (glorified is He) continues describing *ulu al-albab*:

﴿And they establish prayer and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and publicly.﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd) (22)

We have already mentioned many sayings about prayer, and that whoever performs it as it is meant to be performed knows that it is a manifestation between the servant and his Lord, and that the servant is a guest of his Lord.

When the creation is presented to its Creator five times a day, the creation must receive care and attention from the One who designed and created it. Just as God is unseen to you, so too the causes of your recovery from distresses are unseen to you. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) taught us this: "When a matter distressed him, he would stand to pray."

Among the greatness of faith is that God is the One who calls you to prayer, and He (glorified is He) does not withhold nearness from you at any time you wish. You are the one who determines when you stand before Him at any time, after you answer His call with the obligatory prayers, so that you may perform what you love of the voluntary prayers. He (glorified is He) does not end the audience with you as the great ones of this world do; rather, you are the one who ends the meeting whenever you wish.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) took his manners from the manners of his Lord and adopted the lofty character. When someone placed his hand in the hand of the Messenger (ﷺ), he would not withdraw his hand from the hand of the one greeting him, unless that person was the one who withdrew.

The saying of the Truth (glorified is He): ﴿And spend from what We have provided them...﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd) (22) means that you should not look at what is taken from you, but look at the fact that if you come to need something from others, it will be taken for you. This is effective social security. Whoever fears leaving dependents without ability, if this person lived in a believing society, he would find the saying of the Truth fulfilled: ﴿Let those fear [God] who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would be fearful for them. So let them fear God and speak words of appropriate justice.﴾ (Surat al-Nisa') (9) Thereby the orphan does not feel orphaned, no one fears for his dependents, and no one is angry at God's decree concerning him. He (glorified is He) sets the economic balance when He asks us to spend, and spending comes from surplus wealth or wealth that has reached the threshold (*nisab*). Therefore, you must make a beneficial movement for life, from which others benefit, so that you have wealth to spend from, and your movement must suffice you and suffice others.

There are those who spend from what God has provided them by taking for themselves what suffices them, and spending the rest for the face of God, because they are assured that they have a God who is able to provide for them, and what is guaranteed with God is more than what is in their hand. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) asked Abu Bakr about the spoils he had received and said to him, "What did you do with them, O Abu Bakr?" Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him and please him, replied, "I gave them all in charity." The Messenger said, "And what did you leave for them?" Abu Bakr said, "I left God and His Messenger."

The Messenger of God asked 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, "And what did you do, O 'Umar?" Ibn al-Khattab said, "I gave half of it in charity, and I kept the other half for God." It is as if he were saying to the Messenger, "If there is an expenditure that you want me to spend the remaining half on, then I will do it."

Thus we have seen one who spends from what God has provided, giving all of what God has provided him; he is Abu Bakr al-Siddiq. And we find one who spends from what God has provided and is ready to spend the rest if he sees that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) has an expenditure that requires spending. And we find among the guidance of Islam that whoever takes care of an orphan should be abstinent and not take anything from the orphan's wealth if the guardian of the orphan has wealth; and if the guardian is poor, he may eat in a reasonable manner.

One might ask: "Why do we bring a poor person to have guardianship over an orphan's wealth?"

I would say: So that society is not deprived of experience capable of care. The poor one who has experience comes, and eats in a reasonable manner. We observe that the Truth (glorified is He) said: ﴿And provide for them therein...﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd) (22)

He did not say "provide for them from it," meaning take the provision from the wealth, which they own by working with this wealth. Thus we understand how the believing human spends from what God has provided him. There is one who spends everything he has, because he is confident in his credit with his Lord; and there is one who spends part of what God has provided him, and generosity and bounty may move him so that he gives to everyone who asks him, and he may spend everything he has, like someone who sits at the threshing floor of wheat and wants to pay zakat on the day of harvest, so he gives to everyone who asks him until what he has is exhausted.

For this reason, we find the Truth (glorified is He) saying: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest, and do not be excessive. Indeed, He does not like the excessive.﴾ (Surat al-An'am) (141)

Here we find the Truth (glorified is He) describing these spenders in His way: ﴿And they establish prayer and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and publicly...﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd) (22)

Secret giving is voluntary charity (*sadaqah mandubah*), while spending publicly is open charity, because people may see you as wealthy or it may be rumored about you, and they do not see you paying zakat, so their tongues may speak evil of you. When they see you spending and giving charity, they know that you are fulfilling the right of God, and you encourage them to spend from what God has provided them.

Whether to give charity secretly or publicly is left to the judgment of the person. There are those who give charity to the state so that it may dispose of it, and then give to the poor secretly; this is spending both publicly and secretly. The Truth brought both secret and public giving because He does not want to withhold good from anyone for any reason.

Someone may say: "So-and-so gives charity for show."

I would say to whoever utters such a saying: Has the poor person not benefited from the charity? He benefits, and no one enters into intentions. He (glorified is He) continues:

﴿And they repel evil with good...﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd) (22)

*Al-darʼ* (repelling) is pushing away with force; that is, they repel evil with good forcefully. The first believing good is that you believe in God, and by that you

Therefore, the Last Abode that follows this world, for people of understanding (ulu al-albab), is the Gardens of Eden (jannat 'adn). "Adn" means permanent residence, so the Gardens of 'Adn are the Gardens of permanent residence, because this world is not a place of permanent residence. Every blessing in this world is either lost to you through death, or you are lost to it through the changes of life. As for the Gardens of 'Adn, they are an abode of permanent residence, since "'adn" implies lasting companionship with the gardens.

The "gardens" (jannat), as we understand them, are orchards containing trees and fruits, and everything that the souls desire. But note that these gardens are not themselves the dwellings; rather, within those gardens there is a dwelling, as the words of the True One, glorified is He, show: ﴿And good dwellings in Gardens of Eden...﴾ (Surah At-Tawbah, 72). So the gardens are the grounds, and within them are dwellings. In our worldly life we find villas in the midst of gardens, so what then of the good dwellings in the midst of the Gardens that Allah has promised?

It must be that the description given by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of Paradise applies to it, in the Hadith Qudsi from the Lord of Might, glorified is He: "I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived." Thus Allah, glorified is He, has explained the final abode; it is: ﴿Gardens of Eden, which they will enter, along with whoever was righteous among their fathers, spouses, and offspring...﴾ (Surah Ar-Ra'd, 23).

"Aba'" is the plural of "ab" (father), meaning that there enter with the people of understanding those among the fathers who were righteous and followed the method of Allah. If someone asks: where are the mothers?

I say: when we use the dual form for the two equals, we always give precedence to the masculine, and therefore "their fathers" (aba'uhum) means the father and the mother. Did not the True One say in Surah Yusuf: ﴿And he raised his parents upon the throne...﴾ (Surah Yusuf, 100).

These are the people of understanding who will enter Paradise, who have fulfilled the nine conditions we have discussed. So have the fathers, spouses, and children fulfilled the nine conditions?

We say: the True One, glorified and exalted is He, treats His creation in this world according to the affection present in the offspring. One of us loves his children, spouses, and parents; and as long as he loves them and they have become righteous, each according to his capacity, Allah, glorified is He, joins them to him. Therefore another verse comes in which the True One says:

﴿And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith - We will join with them their offspring, and We will not deprive them of anything of their deeds. Every person is held in pledge for what he has earned.﴾ (Surah At-Tur, 21).

Here the Qur'an addresses the rational matter of joining (al-ilhaq), meaning that a lesser one is joined to a complete one. Had the two been equal in deed, it would not be called joining. Every person receives his due. Allah, the True One, has stipulated only one condition for joining the offspring to the fathers, or the fathers to the offspring, in Paradise, and that is faith alone.

And what is clarified for us here is that the fathers were distinguished by a deed of faith, as evidenced by His words, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds...﴾ (Surah At-Tur, 21).
