He, glorified is He, did not take the deed of the father who worked and set it against the son who did not work, and blend the two to take an average; no, this is so that He does not wrong those among the fathers or the sons who worked.

Moreover, if that were to happen, the presence of fathers with sons in Paradise would not be considered joining, because joining requires that the right of each one who worked remain intact; then Allah, glorified is He, graciously bestows the act of joining afterward, on one condition only: that the person being joined is a believer. Thus we understand the words of the True One:

﴿And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith...﴾ (Surah At-Tur, 21).

That is: the offspring are believers, the spouses are believers, the family are believers, and the parents are believers. But the one who is joined to another is the one whom Allah honors with this joining, so that joy enters the heart of the believer when he sees his children with him in Paradise, as long as they are believers. This is the pinnacle of justice. Why? 

The example I give for this: suppose a father was keen to feed his family from lawful earnings; his children may live in hardship and want, while we find the children of the dishonest man living in comfort. Thus the children of the dishonest man, who eats and feeds his children from unlawful wealth, enjoy luxury, while the children of the trustworthy man, whom some consider rigid because he observes the right of Allah and refuses to eat what is unlawful, suffer.

Since his children who eat lawful food may suffer with him from lack of ease, Allah, glorified is He, joins them in Paradise to the bliss that the father enjoys, in which nothing escapes them and nothing escapes him.

Thereby the offspring are made happy, because they came from the loins of a believing man who spent his life on the right path, even though some people accused him in this world of being rigid. And one might say: is there not a contradiction between this joining and the words of the True One: ﴿No father will avail anything for his child, nor will a child avail anything for his father...﴾ (Surah Luqman, 33)?

I say: there is no contradiction, because we pray over the deceased a prayer that the Lawgiver prescribed, and its benefit is that mercy reaches the believing deceased; and faith is from his own deed.

Therefore, Allah, glorified is He, adds to his store of faith whatever mercy He wills, through the funeral prayer that the Muslims performed over him: ﴿Gardens of Eden, which they will enter, along with whoever was righteous among their fathers, spouses, and offspring, while the angels enter upon them from every gate﴾ (Surah Ar-Ra'd, 23).

The word "zawj" (spouse) means the woman whom a man marries, and also the man whom a woman marries. We commit a common error when we say "zawjah" (wife) for a woman; rather, the correct usage is to say "zawj" of a woman related to a man by the bond of marriage. And He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And his wives are their mothers...﴾ (Surah Al-Ahzab, 6).

Thus we know that the Gardens of 'Adn are a place where everything is ordered; and this place has multiple gates, which are the gates of acts of obedience that led to the best rewards. The gate of prayer is entered by some people; the gate of zakat is entered by some people; the gate of patience is entered by some people; and so the gates are many. They are either gates of acts of obedience or gates of rewards through which the good things enter: ﴿Every time they are provided with fruit therefrom, they say, "This is what we were provided with before..."﴾ (Surah Al-Baqarah, 25). So the gate remains open, and from it come fruits, produce, and blessings of every kind: at one time mango fruits come through one gate, and after that apple fruits come.

And these gates, as I have said, are either for rewards, or they are the gates of acts of obedience that led to the rewards; and the angels enter upon them from every gate. So what do the angels say?

Peace means the tranquility and contentment after which no changes come, because peace in this world may be disturbed by the changes of life. You, O believers, who have entered Paradise, are free of such changes.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said about the moments after the Reckoning: "Paradise forever, or the Fire forever."

For this reason He, glory be to Him, says of the bounties of Paradise: ﴿Neither cut off nor forbidden﴾ (Surah al-Waqi'ah 33).

The angels, as we know, are of two kinds. The first are the angels who are absorbed (al-muhayyamun), whom the remembrance of Allah, exalted is He, occupies so that they are diverted from anything else; they do not perceive us and do not know the story of creation, and they have no concern with all that happens. Nothing is in their minds but Allah, and they are the exalted angels (al-'Alun), whose mention came in the story of the prostration before Adam, when the Truth, glory be to Him, asked Satan: ﴿Have you grown arrogant, or were you of the exalted?﴾ (Surah Sad 75). That is, the "exalted" here are those whom the command of prostration did not include, who have no relation to creation, and whose whole task is only the remembrance of Allah.

As for the second kind, they are the angels who manage affairs (al-mudabbirat amran). We know that the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted is He, summoned Adam into existence together with his offspring, and prepared for him everything in existence before he came: the earth was created, the sky was raised, the firm mountains with their sustenance, the sun, the moon, the stars, the waters and the clouds. The angels who manage affairs are those who have a relation to the human being, the vicegerent, and they are those to whom the Truth, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Prostrate to Adam...﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah 34). They are the ones who take charge of the affairs of the human being in execution of the commands of the Truth, glory be to Him, to them. Among them are the guardians, concerning whom the Truth, glory be to Him, said: ﴿For him there are successive [angels] before him and behind him, guarding him by the command of Allah...﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd 11). That is, the command comes from Allah, glory be to Him. And when they finish their task as guardians—a watcher and a recorder over every person—there will be nothing left for them to record after the Reckoning and the determination of recompense. Here these angels will enter upon the people of Paradise to bring the gentle gifts and presents of Allah; they are charged with the human being, the vicegerent.

When He, glory be to Him, puts a word in the Qur'an in its rhetorical and grammatical position, it conveys the meaning He intended. An example is the word "salam" (peace). When the angels came as guests of Ibrahim: ﴿They said, "Peace." He said, "Peace..."﴾ (Surah Hud 69).

By analogy it should have been "salaman" (in the accusative), but this is a matter of faith, so He said: ﴿Salam...﴾ (Surah Hud 69).

So "salam" here came not in the accusative but in the nominative, because peace for the angels is a established fact for them; and thus Ibrahim greeted them with a greeting better than the greeting with which they had greeted him. For we say "salaman" (sending peace), which means we wish that the act should occur; but Ibrahim, peace be upon him, perceived that peace is a fixed matter for them.

So it is likewise here, when the angels enter upon the honored servants on their entry into Paradise, they say: ﴿Peace...﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd 24). It is in the nominative grammatically, because peace is a fixed and established matter in Paradise; they said this because they know that peace is established there, unchanging with the changes of affairs as in the affairs of this world.

Peace in Paradise is for these people because of their patience, as the Truth, glory be to Him, said on the tongues of the angels: ﴿Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured...﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd 24).

The patience came in the past tense, and it is a truthful form: they were patient in this world, and the time of patience ended with the ending of obligation.

They are here in a house of recompense, and therefore the expression in the past tense comes in its right place, because they were patient in the house of obligation over the hardships of obligation: they endured harm, and the decrees that the Truth, glory be to Him, carried out upon them. Thus is the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd 24) in its exact place. Likewise His saying about those who possess the nine qualities, who are in this world: ﴿And those who patiently seek the face of their Lord...﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd 22).

Patience is mentioned here in the past tense, although they are still in the house of obligation. What made this meaning broad is that everything commanded by Allah comes in the present tense, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who fulfill the covenant of Allah...﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd 20), a matter that needs constant renewal; and His saying: ﴿And do not break the covenant﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd 20); and His saying: ﴿And those who join what Allah has commanded to be joined...﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd 21); and "they fear" (wa-yakhshawna), "they dread" (wa-yakhafuna). Thus we see all these verbs come in the present tense, and then the form shifts to the past in His saying: ﴿And those who patiently endured...﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd 22).

Whoever reflects on all this knows that all these matters require patience, as if patience precedes all these things, and it is the common element in every covenant of the covenants before. The Truth, glory be to Him, expressed by the past tense for this subtle point when the angels' speech to them came while they were in Paradise.

Thus the word "patience" falls in its exact place, because the angels address them with this speech while they are in the abode of permanence, and because the Speaker is Allah; He clarifies to us the beauty of what these believers live in, in the Hereafter. The Truth, glory be to Him, concludes the noble verse with His saying: ﴿How excellent is the final home﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd 24).

We know that "'uqba" means that which comes at the end. When He, exalted is He, presents the matter of faith and the qualities of the believers who live by the values of faith, the purpose is that the soul should aspire to be among them, and the soul must recoil from the opposite side of them.

The example is the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss﴾ (Surah al-Infitar 13), and after it, its opposite: ﴿And indeed, the wicked will be in Hellfire﴾ (Surah al-Infitar 14).

When you compare that, if they were not righteous, they would be in Hellfire, here we know the measure of the blessing of the Truth's guidance to them, that they be among the people of faith. Thus we find ourselves before two matters: the removal of harm, and the attainment of benefit. For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, also says about the Fire: ﴿And there is not one of you but will pass over it; this is a decree binding of your Lord﴾ (Surah Maryam 71), meaning: all of us will see the Fire. And He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Then you will surely see it with the certainty of sight﴾ (Surah al-Takathur 7). This is so that every Muslim may know what the blessing of faith has done for him before entering Paradise; thus he knows that Allah removed from him a harm and bestowed upon him a benefit: He removed from him what would make him wretched, and gave him what would profit him. For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has attained success﴾ (Surah Al 'Imran 185). And since the Truth, glory be to Him, has described the people of understanding with the qualities mentioned before, He also makes clear to us the loss of those opposed to them.

Would someone ask: did these people believe, and was there between them and God a covenant which they broke? We say: it is valid that they believed and then disbelieved, or: the speech here refers to the eternal covenant of God.

He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves, "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we testify."﴾ (Surah al-A'raf, 172).

Here He, glorified is He, makes clear that those who break the covenant of God after its pledge and confirmation by the cosmic signs that point to the existence of the One Creator are: ﴿and who sever what God has commanded to be joined﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 25).

The counterpart to them are the people of understanding (ulu al-albab) who used to join what God commanded to be joined, while these disbelievers are the breakers of the covenant: ﴿and cause corruption in the earth﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 25). The Truth, glorified is He, did not state the counterpart to every action performed by the people of understanding. He did not say, "and they do not fear their Lord," because they do not believe in a god; and He did not say, "they do not fear the evil of the reckoning," because they do not believe in the Resurrection. Thus it becomes clear to us that everything in the Qur'an came in its measure and in its perfect place.

We know that corruption in the earth is taking the good out of its goodness. You have come to the universe, and it has been prepared to receive you with all the means of life: food, drink, and breath; and other sustenance; and the preservation of the species by His permitting us to marry, male and female.

Corruption in the universe is that you come to something good in its own nature and spoil it. We always say: if you do not know how to increase the good in goodness, leave it in its state; and listen to the words of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 36).

So in no matter what affair, do not look only at its immediate good; rather look at what the matter will lead to afterwards: does it harm or benefit? For delayed harm may creep in stealthily and slowly, so that you cannot ward it off afterwards. The Truth, glorified is He, says at the end of the verse we are reflecting upon:

﴿Those, for them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 25).

We notice that the expression here came with the lam, which indicates that the curse has embraced them the way love of wealth embraces kings: ﴿and for them is the evil abode﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 25), meaning its punishment, which is the Fire, and we seek refuge in God.

The expansion (al-basṭ) is the extension of a thing. The scholars have disputed at length over the definition of provision (al-rizq): is provision only what God has made lawful, or is provision everything from which a person benefits, whether lawful or unlawful?

Some scholars said: provision is only what is lawful. Others said: provision is everything from which a person benefits, whether lawful or unlawful, because if you say that provision is confined to the lawful alone, then from where does the one who disbelieves in God eat?

Or the Truth, glorified is He, addresses the obstinate, saying: ﴿Say: "Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth?..."﴾ (Surah Yunus, 31).

And He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm.﴾ (Surah al-Dhariyat, 58).

And He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And in the heaven is your provision and that which you are promised. So by the Lord of the heaven and the earth, indeed, it is the truth, just as [it is true] that you speak.﴾ (Surah al-Dhariyat, 22-23).

So provision is from God; and after that He commands, "Do this" and "Do not do that." The saying of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]...﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 26). That is, He, glorified is He, extends provision to whom He wills. ﴿...and restricts [it]...﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 26), from qadar: that is, in the case of His decreeing it for the one upon whom it is restricted; and this is the one to whom He gives according to his need, because qadar is the cutting of a thing to the measure of another thing, as when He gives to the poor and extends provision for him according to his need.

The Truth, glorified is He, has commanded us to give zakah to the poor, and the poor remains living in his poverty, because he lives on subsistence.

Or: "yaqdiru" means "yudayyiq" (restricts). Whenever this occurs, beware of thinking that restricting the poor is not in his interest, for abundant wealth may be a motive for sin, and from chastity is that he does not find [much].

Or: "yaqdiru" means "yudayyiq" in its absolute sense. He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Let the wealthy spend from his wealth, and he whose provision is restricted, let him spend from what Allah has given him. Allah does not burden a soul except [according to] what He has given it. Allah will bring about, after hardship, ease.﴾ (Surah al-Talaq, 7). And because Allah has given him, this means that He has extended to him according to His decree. He, glorified, continues: ﴿And they rejoice in the worldly life...﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 26). Naturally, one whose provision is abundant will rejoice in it; and the believer is the one who looks at provision and says: it is the adornment of the worldly life; but what is with Allah is better and more lasting. As for the people of disbelief, they said:

﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man of the two cities, great?﴾ (Surah al-Zukhruf, 31).

The Truth, glorified is He, responds to them: ﴿Is it they who would apportion the mercy of your Lord? We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the worldly life and raised some of them above others in degrees...﴾ (Surah al-Zukhruf, 32).

When you investigate the identity of this one for whom provision is extended and this one for whom it is restricted, you will not find stability in this matter, because circumstances may take from the rich and make him poor, and wealth may pass from the rich to the poor.

And He, glorified is He, has guaranteed lofty means of provision for each of the believer and the disbeliever, the obedient and the disobedient; and each of us has entered life to take in his hand from the gift of lordship. If one falls short, then this person has no cause except that he did not take up the means of lordship and benefit from them.

The disbeliever may take them and benefit from them. The Truth, glorified is He, is the One who said: ﴿Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his harvest; and whoever desires the harvest of this world, We give him from it, but he will have no share in the Hereafter.﴾ (Surah al-Shura, 20).

So there is no restriction except within the limits that Allah wills, such as when a person plows the land and exerts himself in irrigation and tilling, then a thunderbolt or hail accompanied by frost comes and consumes the crop and destroys it. In this there is a reminder to the person that He, glorified is He, has taken from this person his provision, which is a gift from Him, so that the person will not be tempted by the means, and his provision may come afterward from another place, and by another cause.

﴿Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it], and they rejoice in the worldly life...﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 26).

Joy in itself is not forbidden or prohibited, but what is prohibited is the joy of arrogance (al-baṭar), like the joy of Qarun:

﴿Indeed, Qarun was of the people of Musa, but he oppressed them. And We had given him of treasures whose keys would surely burden a company of strong men... when his people said to him, "Do not exult..."﴾ (Surah al-Qasas, 76).

And the Truth, glorified is He, has said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the exultant﴾ (Surah al-Qasas, 76).

This is the joy of arrogance which Allah does not love, because He, glorified is He, said in another place: ﴿Say: "In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy—in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate."﴾ (Surah Yunus, 58).

Here, in the verse about which we are reflecting, their joy is mentioned, and the cause of this joy, which is the worldly life; that is, it is a trivial cause for joy, because it may be taken from them and they may be taken from it. But joy in the Hereafter is different, and it is the true joy. Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, says of it: ﴿In that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate.﴾ (Surah Yunus, 58). And the Truth, glorified is He, sets before us the comparison of the joy of the worldly life with the Hereafter, saying: ﴿And the worldly life, in the Hereafter, is but a brief enjoyment.﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 26).

The "mata'" (provision/belongings) of a man is what he prepares and takes along for a short journey, like the small bag in which you put some clothes and items that belong to you for a short trip.

The intelligent person is the one who looks at the utmost that a human being can do in life: he may learn until he reaches the highest levels of knowledge, and strive on the earth as far as his effort reaches; then finally he dies.

The believer is the one who connects the work of his worldly life with the Hereafter, so as to reach true bliss; and the believer is the one who exerts effort to connect himself with the mercy of Allah, because it remains by the permanence of Allah, and because the true believer knows that every goal that has an end beyond it is not considered a goal.

Therefore the worldly life in itself is not fit to be the goal of the believer; rather the true goal is either Paradise forever, or Hellfire forever.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 13, verse 27:

We know that "lawla" (why not / if only not), when it is followed by a nominal sentence (jumla ismiyya), has a meaning that differs from its meaning when it is followed by a verbal sentence (jumla fi'liyya). When we say "lawla Zayd 'indaka la-zurtuka" (had it not been for Zayd being with you, I would have visited you), it means the prevention of one thing from occurring because of the existence of another. When we say "lawla tudhakkir durusak" (why do you not review your lessons), this means urging (hadd) toward the action. Almighty God says:

﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses for it? Since they did not bring the witnesses, they are with God the liars.﴾ (Surah al-Nur: 13). The sentence which "lawla" enters in this verse is a verbal sentence, and it is as if Almighty God is urging us here to turn our attention to the greatest sign that was sent down upon him, may God bless him and grant him peace, which is the Qur'an.

The unbelievers have questioned, falsely, about the coming of a sign; and their questioning came after the coming of the Qur'an, and this is a manifest lie, by which they contradict themselves. For they said: ﴿They said: "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man from the two cities?"﴾ (Surah al-Zukhruf: 31). By this they have acknowledged that the Qur'an reached the limit of inimitability (i'jaz), and they wished that it had been sent down upon one of the great men of the two cities, Mecca or al-Ta'if. And it is they who also said: ﴿They said: "O you to whom the Reminder has been sent down, you are truly possessed!"﴾ (Surah al-Hijr: 6).

Then they return here to deny acknowledging the Qur'an as a miracle, although it came from the kind of thing in which they excelled. They appreciate literature, they appreciate eloquence, and they appreciate rhetoric; and they hold markets to display their production in eloquence and poetry. They are a people whose ears are delighted by what the tongue utters.

But here they demand a cosmic sign (aya kawniyya) like that which was sent down upon the earlier messengers, peace be upon them, and they forgot that the lifespan of a cosmic sign is limited to the time of its occurrence; and whoever sees it is the one who believes it, or whoever is informed of it by a trustworthy source believes it.

But the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent to organize the movement of life in the world of people until the Hour comes; and if he had brought a cosmic sign, it would have been confined to its own time only.

For this reason, Almighty God willed to bring a miracle that remains until the Hour comes, in addition to the fact that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was granted sensory miracles: such as water gushing from between his fingers; a handful of food that satisfied an army; a cloud that shaded him; the trunk of a tree that yearned for him so that he could stand upon it and preach; and the lizard (dabb) came to him in submission.

All these are cosmic signs which are a proof for whoever sees them, and likewise the miracles of the earlier messengers. Had the Qur'an not related them to us, we would not have believed in them; and the cosmic signs that came with the messengers were merely a demonstration to those who lived in the times of the earlier messengers that these messengers were conveyors from God.

Almighty God explained this matter with regard to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when He said: ﴿And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the earlier ones denied them.﴾ (Surah al-Isra': 59). That is: the earlier messengers who came down among their peoples and were accompanied by cosmic signs were also confronted by deniers of those signs; and the people of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, also said: ﴿And they said: "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth, or you have a garden of palms and grapes and you cause rivers to gush forth within it abundantly, or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces as you claim, or you bring God and the angels as a guarantee."﴾ (Surah al-Isra': 90–92).

Almighty God says elsewhere: ﴿And even if We had sent down to them the angels, and the dead had spoken to them, and We had gathered against them everything before them, they would not have believed unless God willed; but most of them are ignorant.﴾ (Surah al-An'am: 111).

Thus Almighty God shows us that they are drowned in obstinacy and will not believe, and that their statements are merely pretexts by which they delay. And here, in the verse about which our reflections are, they say: ﴿Why was no sign sent down upon him from his Lord?﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd: 27).

Thus we find that they acknowledge that he has a Lord, although they had previously accused him of being a sorcerer, and that he was, God forbid, a liar. And when the revelation paused for him, they said: "The Lord of Muhammad has forsaken him." And Almighty God sent down the revelation: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still, your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you. And the Hereafter is better for you than the first. And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied.﴾ (Surah al-Duha: 1–5). That is, the revelation will continue; and thus God exposed their lie over the years of the Muhammadan mission.

Here they are demanding, obstinately, the sensory cosmic sign; and the word "aya" (sign), as we have known before, means either: a cosmic sign that draws attention to the existence of the Creator; or a verse of the Qur'an containing the detailing of rulings; and that is not the sign they were demanding; or: a miraculous sign that indicates the truthfulness of the message.

It is as if the demand for signs came only because they were not convinced by the Qur'anic sign; and this is evidence of their dullness in receiving the proofs of certainty concerning the truthfulness of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace; because the Qur'an came as a miracle, and it came as a method.

And the miracle, as we have explained, comes from the kind of thing in which the people excelled, and God does not bring a miracle to a people who did not excel in anything like it and were not skilled in it.

So those who practiced sorcery had a miracle brought with the messenger sent to them of the same kind; and those who knew medicine had a messenger come to them with a miracle from what they excelled in. And the miracle of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came from the kind of thing in which they excelled; in addition to the fact that the Qur'an is a miracle and a method at once, unlike the miracle of timing and confinement to a period of time.

Nevertheless, the unbelievers of Mecca were obstinate, and they were not content with the Qur'an as a miracle and signs guiding them to the right path; rather they proposed the sign themselves according to their whims; and therefore we find that they went astray. And Almighty God says after that: ﴿Say: "Indeed, God leads astray whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back in repentance."﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd: 27).

Here we pause, because some attempt to remove from man the responsibility of obligation (taklif), claiming that it is God who prevents these unbelievers from being guided. We say: if we survey the verses of the Qur'an, we will find the saying of Almighty God: ﴿And God does not guide the disbelieving people﴾ (Surah al-Baqara: 264); and we find the saying of Almighty God: ﴿Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ (Surah al-Ma'ida: 51); and Almighty God also says: ﴿And God does not guide the defiantly disobedient people﴾ (Surah al-Ma'ida: 108).

From all of that we understand that the earlier action from them is what causes Him, glory be to Him, not to guide them; because a person, as long as a higher judgment has come to him and he believes in the source of the judgment, then He who sent down this judgment gives the person help; but whoever denies the source of the higher judgment, then He, glory be to Him, leaves him without help.

As for whoever returns to God, He, glory be to Him, guides him, directs him, and assists him with all support. And the Truth continues with the tranquility that He, glory be to Him, grants to whoever turns to Him in repentance.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 13, verse 28:

The meaning of al-ițmi'nān (tranquillity) is the calm and settledness of the heart, and its ease and comfort in a creed that no longer surfaces in the intellect to be debated afresh.

We know that a human being has perceptive senses by which he receives sensible things, and he has an intellect (ʿaql) that takes these things, digests them after perceiving them, examines them carefully, feels out whether they are true or false, and extracts from all of that a clear proposition which he keeps in his heart so that it becomes a creed (ʿaqīdah), because it has reached the stage of emotion (wijdān) that loves to choose what is loved.

Thus a creed passes through several stages: first it is sensory perception; then the stage of intellectual reflection; then the stage of clarifying the truth; then settling in the heart so that it becomes a creed. For this reason the Exalted says:

﴿And their hearts are at rest..﴾ (28) (Surah al-Ra'd). The tranquillity of the heart is the result of faith in the creed. The heart may pass through some of the changing circumstances (aghyār) that shake faith, and we say to whoever is passing through those anxious thoughts (hawājis) of changing circumstances: you have not given Lordship (rubūbiyyah) its due, because you are the one to blame for anything that befalls you.

If you had received the decree (qadar) well in what befalls you of events, you would know your own shortcoming in whatever has a part of you in any incident that befalls you as a result of your action. As for what befalls you in which you have no part, this is from the matter of the decree which the Truth willed for you for a wisdom you may not know, and it is good for you.

So: receiving the decree, if it comes from outside the self, is for you, and if it comes from within the self, it is against you.

If you were to count what benefits you from the decree falling upon you, you would find it far more than what it has taken from you. The example is the young man who studied his lessons and prepared for the examination, but an illness overtook him before the examination and prevented him from sitting it.

This young man did what was incumbent upon him; and God willed that this decree descend upon him for some wisdom: for instance, that it keep away the envy of his neighbours, or the envy of those who dislike his mother or father, or that it protect him from conceit and temptation in that he relies on means rather than on the Causer of causes. Or the postponement of your desire before the requirement of God may be good.

Thus it is incumbent upon the believing person to be connected to the Highest Causer, and to rely upon Him alone, the Exalted; and to know that reliance upon God means that the limbs work while the hearts rely, for reliance (tawakkul) is an act of the heart, not an act of the outward forms. Let each of us be mindful that God may withdraw the means so that we are not deceived by them, and thereby your faith in Him is balanced, and the faith of others is balanced.

You may see a clever young man capable of comprehension, but who does not achieve the aggregate suitable for the faculty he desired; so he prostrates to God in thanks, accepting God's decree and destiny; and God guides him to another faculty, where he excels, so that he becomes one of the outstanding figures in the new field. For this reason the Truth says:

﴿Perhaps you dislike a thing and it is good for you, and perhaps you love a thing and it is bad for you; and God knows, and you do not know.﴾ (216) (Surah al-Baqarah). Thus we find that whoever accepts the decree of God concerning himself, and remembers that he has a Lord above all means, tranquillity will flood his heart before any event whatsoever. Thus the heart is at rest through the remembrance of God, and all means become insignificant, for if means fail, the Causer will not fail.

The Truth, the Exalted, has brought this verse in the context of His speaking about the doubt raised by the disbelievers. When the Muslims hear this doubt, some thoughts and questions may arise: why did the Messenger of God (ﷺ) not bring us a sensory miracle like the earlier messengers, to dispel this problem and end this obstinacy? But those thoughts do not strip the believers of their faith; therefore the Truth sends down His word which brings tranquillity:

﴿Those who believe, and whose hearts are at rest in the remembrance of God..﴾ (28) (Surah al-Ra'd). The word dhikr in the language has many meanings. Sometimes dhikr is used and intends the Book, that is the Qur'an:

﴿Indeed, We have sent down the Reminder, and indeed We are its guardians.﴾ (9) (Surah al-Hijr). Dhikr also comes meaning fame, renown and distinction. The Exalted says:

﴿And indeed it is a reminder for you and for your people, and you will be questioned.﴾ (44) (Surah al-Zukhruf), that is: it is a great honour for you in history, and likewise for your people, that the Qur'anic miracle comes in the kind of their language which they speak. Dhikr may also be used for admonition (iʿtibār). The Truth says:

﴿But You gave them and their fathers enjoyment until they forgot the remembrance, and they were a people ruined.﴾ (18) (Surah al-Furqan). That is: they forgot the lessons that befell the nations who lived before them; so God gave victory to the religion despite the obstinacy of these people. Dhikr may also be used for everything the Truth sends through the tongue of any messenger:

﴿So ask the people of the reminder, if you do not know.﴾ (43) (Surah al-Nahl). Dhikr may also be used for good bounty from God. And dhikr is used for constant remembrance of God; He, the Exalted, says:

﴿So remember Me, and I will remember you..﴾ (152) (Surah al-Baqarah), that is: remember Me with obedience, and I will remember you with good and manifestations (tajallī). If dhikr has these meanings, then we find tranquillity in each of them: dhikr in the sense of the Qur'an bequeaths tranquillity. The Truth says:

﴿O you who believe, remember God with much remembrance (41), and glorify Him morning and evening (42). He it is who sends blessings upon you, and His angels, to bring you out of darknesses into light; and He is ever merciful to the believers (43).﴾ (Surah al-Ahzab). Every verse that came from the Qur'an was reassuring the Messenger (ﷺ) that he was truthful in conveying from God; for the Muslims were a small, persecuted group, unable to protect themselves or their families. In this circumstance the Truth says:

﴿The multitude will be routed and will turn their backs.﴾ (45) (Surah al-Qamar).

ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him) asked: which multitude is this, when we cannot defend ourselves, and some of us have emigrated to Abyssinia out of fear of persecution?

But the Messenger of God (ﷺ) went out to Badr, and specified the places where the great leaders of disbelief among the chiefs of Quraysh would fall; he said: "This is the fall of so-and-so, and this is the fall of so-and-so"; and he even indicated the manner in which the chiefs of Quraysh would be killed, and recited the word of the Truth:

﴿We will brand him upon the snout.﴾ (16) (Surah al-Qalam). Afterwards they brought the head of the man about whom the Messenger of God had said that, and they found the blow had struck his nose. Who, then, controls the places of death?

This can only come from a God who is God; and it is He who informed Muhammad (ﷺ) of this news: ﴿The multitude will be routed and will turn their backs.﴾ (45) (Surah al-Qamar).

This statement reassured the people who followed the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who does not know the unseen, and does not know the manner in which any disbeliever or tyrant will die; and he (ﷺ) informed them of it while they were in the utmost weakness. This announcement is evidence that his account is strong with the Knower of the unseen.

So: the Truth's word ﴿Verily, by the remembrance of God hearts are at rest﴾ (28) (Surah al-Ra'd) means that hearts find rest through the Qur'an and what it contains of truthful reports, perfectly true, to confirm that Muhammad (ﷺ) is a conveyor from his Lord, and that the Qur'an is not from Muhammad (ﷺ) but is from God.

Thus the believers received Muhammad (ﷺ) and affirmed what he brought. Khadijah (may God be pleased with her and content her) had not heard the Qur'an; when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) told her of his fears that what came to him might be jinn, she said:

"Indeed you join the ties of kinship, bear the burdens of the weak, earn for the destitute, host the guest, and help in the calamities of truth. By God, God will never disgrace you."

And Abu Bakr (may God be pleased with him and content him) affirmed that Muhammad was a messenger from God as soon as he informed him of it.

Thus we find him (ﷺ) possessed of qualities; God had shaped for His Messenger morals that made those around him believe everything he said the moment he spoke.

We note that those who believed in his message (ﷺ) did not believe because the Qur'an had seized them; rather they believed because Muhammad (ﷺ) could not possibly deceive them with speech, and his conduct before the mission was itself a miracle, and it was this that led the first believers to affirm the Messenger of God (ﷺ). As for the disbelievers, the Qur'an seized them and won over their hearts, and they wished it had been sent down to someone other than Muhammad (ﷺ).

When the believers see that the Qur'an informs them of situations they are living through for which they know no explanation, and also informs them of events that will occur, and then they find the future has come as the Qur'an said, then it becomes certain to them that the Qur'an is not from Muhammad, but from the Lord of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Therefore, when the disbelievers raise their nonsense to cast doubt upon Muhammad (ﷺ), the Qur'an comes reassuring the believers, so the nonsense of the disbelievers does not affect them.

The believer remembers God through good things, and takes lessons from everything that passes him and from everything in the Book of God; when he reads the Qur'an his heart is at rest in the remembrance of God, because he has believed with true faith.

The believers have also perceived that the reports of the Prophet which he told them have gone beyond their narrow local surroundings to the wide world with its two wings: the eastern in Persia and the western in Rome.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) announced to them, for example, the news of the victory of the Romans over the Persians, when the Truth sent down His word:

﴿Alif, Lam, Mim (1). The Romans have been defeated (2) in the nearest land; but after their defeat they will overcome (3) within a few years. To God belongs the command, before and after; and on that day the believers will rejoice (4).﴾ (Surah al-Rum).

Show me what genius in the world could control the outcome of a battle between two forces struggling and fighting; and then determine who will win and who will be defeated after a period of time ranging from five to nine years?

Likewise, world events come which the Messenger of God (ﷺ) knew nothing of, and which agree with what came in the Qur'an.

All of that puts the believers in the Qur'an in a state of tranquillity that this Qur'an is true, and that it is from God; and this is confirmed by the Truth's word:

﴿Those who believe, and whose hearts are at rest in the remembrance of God. Verily, by the remembrance of God hearts are at rest.﴾ (28) (Surah al-Ra'd).

We know that the universe received the first human, Adam (peace be upon him), with full welcome, and everything of the foundations of life was made ready for him in it; and the human being came to live within the means of God, those means extended from the hand of God; so we take hold of them, and our lives advance in proportion to the effort we exert.

And as soon as we die, we reach a higher life, if our deeds are righteous and our faith in God is good; for after we lived in this world by the extended means of God, we live in the Hereafter with the Causer in His Paradise which He prepared for the godwary.

The word of the Truth: ﴿Verily, by the remembrance of God hearts are at rest.﴾ (28) (Surah al-Ra'd)

means that tranquillity encompasses all hearts; every person has a corner where his heart is agitated, and as soon as he remembers God he finds tranquillity and his heart is steadied. The orientalists have tried to make a fuss around the Exalted's word: ﴿Verily, by the remembrance of God hearts are at rest.﴾ (28) (Surah al-Ra'd).

They asked: how does the Qur'an say here that remembrance tranquillises the heart, while in another verse it says:

﴿The believers are only those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts tremble..﴾ (2) (Surah al-Anfal). Which of the two meanings is intended? Had the orientalists received the Qur'an with correct Arabic linguistic faculty, they would have known the difference between:

﴿Verily, by the remembrance of God hearts are at rest.﴾ (28) (Surah al-Ra'd)

and the Truth's word: ﴿The believers are only those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts tremble.﴾ (2) (Surah al-Anfal). The first is as if God is mentioned in front of people while the person is heedless of God; here the person becomes alert with trepidation.

Or: the Truth addresses all creation with what they have of instincts, emotions and spiritual states; there is no perfect person, and every person has a lapse, except whom God protects. When a person recalls his excess in some evil respect, he trembles; and when he recalls God's pardon, His repentance and His forgiveness, he is at rest.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 13, verse 29:

"Tuba" (ṭūbā) is from "the good thing" (al-shay' al-ṭayyib); that is, they will encounter a good thing in all its aspects: in form, color, taste, temperament, and desire. Whatever any one of them desires, he will find it good, as if the good matter were existing for them. The word of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿And a good return (ḥusn maʾāb)﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd 13:29), meaning: a good return for them to the One who created them first, sustained them through means, and then took them to live by the highest Cause, and by the possibility of "Be, and it is." Then the Truth, glory be to Him, wishes after that to clarify to His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he is a messenger among the messengers; and every messenger, to whatever nation he was sent, would bring with him a miracle of the kind in which his people excelled.

Allah, glory be to Him, sent Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with the miracle suited to his people. They excelled in eloquence, clear expression, and the craft of speech, and in composing long poems, the most famous of which are the Seven Odes (al-Mu'allaqat al-Sab'). They had literary markets such as the Market of ʿUkaz and the Market of Dhu al-Majaz. Therefore, his miracle, peace and blessings be upon him, came of the same kind as that in which they excelled, so that the proof and the challenge would reach them. Had the miracle been in a field in which they had not excelled, they would have said: "We have never dealt with a matter like this before; and had we dealt with it, we would have excelled in it."

Thus it becomes clear to us that sending a messenger with a miracle in a field in which his people excelled is a form of establishing the challenge and displaying the superiority of the miracle that the messenger brought. Thus we see that the sending of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with the Qur'an, even though it did not convince the disbelievers, was in accordance with the logic of revelation from heaven for all the messages.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 13, verse 30:

Just as Allah sent you to your community, He had previously sent messengers to the earlier nations, and He did not send with any of them a miracle that contradicted what their people excelled in, so that no one could say that the miracle which came with the Messenger dealt with a kind of thing they were not accustomed to. Had they been accustomed to it, the Messenger would not have surpassed them.

And the word of the Truth: ﴿Thus﴾ (Surah Ar-Ra'd), meaning: in this same manner as the earlier sending of messengers, your sending to your community has come, like those earlier nations. Here the Truth, glorified is He, brings the Name that they ought to have esteemed at its true worth, which is "al-Rahman" (the Most Merciful). He did not say, "while they disbelieve in Allah," but said: ﴿and they disbelieve in the Most Merciful... 30﴾ (Surah Ar-Ra'd).

Despite their disbelief, they live on the provision of Allah, al-Rahman, and everything around them, what sustains them, and what they enjoy of blessings, are gifts from Allah.

They do not perform any of the obligations of Allah. So it would have been fitting for them to mention Allah's favour upon them, and to believe in Him, because what the divinity requires is the performance of worship.

Here He, glorified is He, brings His name "al-Rahman," which implies the bestowing of goodness freely. It was incumbent upon them to esteem this goodness which He has given them, without any power or strength of their own. They should have taken heed and declared that they turn to Him, glorified is He, in worship, and carried out the duty of worship.

At the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, negotiations took place between the Muslims and the disbelievers of Quraysh, who had prevented the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from entering Makkah, yet they accepted a covenant with him. That was an acknowledgement by them of Muhammad ﷺ and his companions, who had become a force to make covenants with, one that gives and takes.

Hence we find Sayyidina Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) saying: "There was no victory in Islam greater than the victory of Hudaybiyyah."

At Hudaybiyyah, Quraysh began to acknowledge the Messenger of Allah and the community of Islam, and they agreed to a long truce during which Muhammad ﷺ and his companions were able to campaign against the tribes living around Quraysh, where a small expedition would go out with a preacher of the religion of Allah, and tribe after tribe would submit.

Thus Hudaybiyyah was the greatest victory in Islam: Quraysh was calmed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and those with him were free to call the tribes surrounding them to Islam. But people's perception did not extend to what lay between Muhammad and his Lord. The servants are always hasty, while Allah is not hasty with the haste of His servants, until matters reach what He wills.

When the moment of contracting the agreement between the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Quraysh at Hudaybiyyah arrived, and Ali ibn Abi Talib began writing the wording of the treaty, he wrote, "This is what Muhammad the Messenger of Allah has agreed to." Suhayl ibn 'Amr objected and said: "If I had testified that you are the Messenger of Allah, I would not have fought you. Rather, write: 'This is what Muhammad ibn Abdullah and Suhayl ibn 'Amr have agreed to.'"

The companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ insisted that the description of Muhammad as Messenger be written, but the Prophet ﷺ said: "By Allah, I am indeed the Messenger of Allah even if you deny me. Write: Muhammad ibn Abdullah." But Ali, may Allah ennoble his face, insisted on writing the description of Muhammad as Messenger of Allah; so the Truth, glorified is He, caused His Messenger ﷺ to speak, saying to Ali: "You will be asked for something like it, and you will accept it."

When Ali, may Allah ennoble his face, assumed the caliphate after Abu Bakr, 'Umar and 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with them all, and the battle took place between Ali and Mu'awiyah, then the two parties agreed on a covenant, and the scribe wrote: "This is what Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib has agreed to." 'Amr ibn al-'As, Mu'awiyah's envoy, said: "Write his name and his father's name; he is your amir, not our amir."

Here Ali, may Allah ennoble his face, recalled what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said: "You will be asked for something like it, and you will accept it." He accepted it and said: "Erase 'Amir al-Mu'minin' and write: 'This is what Ali ibn Abi Talib has agreed to.'"

The saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was fulfilled. Among the events that establish faith is the story of 'Ammar ibn Yasir, who was in the ranks of Ali, may Allah ennoble his face and be pleased with him, in the confrontation with Mu'awiyah. Mu'awiyah's soldiers killed him, and the Muslims cried out: "Woe to 'Ammar, the rebellious faction will kill him." Thus the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said.

By this the Muslims understood that the rebellious faction was Mu'awiyah's faction, and many Muslims who had been in Mu'awiyah's ranks moved over to the ranks of Ali ibn Abi Talib. 'Amr ibn al-'As went to Mu'awiyah and said: "A rumour has spread in the army; if it continues, no one will remain with us. We have killed 'Ammar ibn Yasir, and the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ have recalled his saying: 'Woe to 'Ammar, the rebellious faction will kill him,' and those fighting with us have understood that the rebellious faction is our faction."

Mu'awiyah had a certain cunning, so he said: "Go among the army and say: 'It was the one who brought him out who killed him,' meaning Ali." When this saying reached Ali, he said: "And who killed Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, when it was Muhammad ﷺ who brought him out to fight?"

﴿Thus We have sent you to a community before which other communities have passed... 30﴾ (Surah Ar-Ra'd).

This means only that the Truth has sent you, O Muhammad, with a miracle suited to what your people excel in, and seeking anything other than that is ignorance of the reality of the messages and obstinacy whose aim is to push them further away from faith. The word of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿and they disbelieve in the Most Merciful. Say: He is my Lord... 30﴾ (Surah Ar-Ra'd), meaning: when they openly declare disbelief, you confront them by declaring faith, and say: ﴿He is my Lord; there is no deity but Him... 30﴾ (Surah Ar-Ra'd).

The word "my Lord" harmonises with "al-Rahman," who bestows all blessings and who takes charge of my upbringing. Had He done nothing but create me, nurture me, and sustain me with life and its necessities, that alone would suffice for me to worship Him alone and not associate anyone with Him.

Had a person associated others with Allah, he would turn once to that god, once to another god, and a third time to a third god, and so on; but Allah, glorified is He, willed to relieve man of this scattering through the creed of Tawhid. The Qur'an comes also to reassure hearts, and to mention: ﴿Allah sets forth an example: a man in whom are partners disputing with one another, and a man belonging wholly to one man. Are they equal in comparison? Praise be to Allah, but most of them do not know. 29﴾ (Surah Az-Zumar).

Thus the Qur'an presents us with two images:

The first image: a man owned by several masters, who oppose one another.

The second image: another man, owned by one master.

Reason must recognise that a single master is better than multiple masters, because the plurality of masters is corruption and causes corruption. The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would both have been corrupted. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe. 22﴾ (Surah Al-Anbiya). The wise person surrenders himself only to one master whom he trusts to be faithful to him. In our lives we say: "I am content with what so-and-so rules; I have entrusted him with such-and-such." None of us surrenders himself except to one whom he sees as trustworthy in this religion, and he must be trustworthy and strong, and able to carry out what is required.

And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in the fierce battle with the chiefs of Quraysh, said: "Indeed I put my trust in Allah."

This is his testimony that he relied upon the Strong, the Trustworthy, the Wise. The Messenger did not say "I have relied upon Him" (tawakkaltu 'alayhi); rather he said: ﴿Upon Him I have relied... 30﴾ (Surah Ar-Ra'd). The difference between the two statements is great: when you say "upon Him I have relied," you restrict reliance to Him alone; but if you say "I have relied upon Him," you may add and coordinate others on whom you may rely. For this reason we say: ﴿You alone do we worship... 5﴾ (Surah Al-Fatihah).

We confine worship to Him and for Him alone, glorified is He, so it does not extend to anyone else; and if it were postponed, it would be permissible to coordinate another with Him. This is called "ism qasr" (the restrictive construction), meaning that worship is restricted to Him; and likewise reliance.

﴿Say: He is my Lord; there is no deity but Him; upon Him I have relied... 30﴾ (Surah Ar-Ra'd), meaning: I do not take my commands from anyone other than Him, and my return is to Him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 13, verse 31:

The wa and law (لو) here is a conditional particle (harf shart) which requires an answer (jawab al-shart). Al-Haqq, glory be to Him, has omitted the answer of the condition here, relying on the alertness of the listener. Although such a statement would be incomplete when we utter it ourselves, it is not so when it comes from the speech of Allah, glory be to Him; it is complete with respect to the One who speaks, and He has left it out because the listener of the Qur'an is alert and anticipates the meanings. Let him recall along with this verse the saying of al-Haqq:

﴿And if We had sent down to you a Book on paper, and they had touched it with their hands, those who disbelieved would have said, "This is not but obvious magic."﴾ (Surat al-An'am)

And likewise the saying of al-Haqq, glory be to Him:

﴿And even if We had sent down to them the angels and the dead had spoken to them and We had gathered before them every thing, they would not have believed unless Allah willed; but most of them are ignorant.﴾ (Surat al-An'am)

So, from all the counterparts of that verse about which we are presenting our reflections, we take the fitting answer of the condition from those verses. The meaning becomes: Even if a Qur'an had been made to move the mountains, or the earth had been cut apart by it, or the dead had been spoken to by it, they would still not have believed.

It is related that some of the polytheists of Quraysh, such as Abu Jahl and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah, sat behind the Ka'bah and sent to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Abdullah said to him: "If it pleases you that we follow you, then move for us the mountains of Makkah by the Qur'an, and remove them from us until the valley becomes spacious, for it is a narrow land; and make for us in it springs and rivers, so that we may plant and sow. You are not, as you claim, less esteemed before your Lord than Dawud, for whom the mountains were subjected to travel with him; and subject the wind to us so that we may ride it to Syria, dispatch our provisions and needs upon it, and return the same day. The wind was subjected to Sulayman ibn Dawud, and you are not less esteemed before your Lord than Sulayman. And revive for us the ancestor of your grandfather (Qusay), or whomever you wish of our dead, that we may ask him: Is what you say true or false? For Isa used to revive the dead, and you are not less esteemed before Allah than he." Then al-Haqq, glory be to Him, revealed this verse and what preceded it in refutation of them.

All these were matters with which they were pretending, in order to turn away from faith. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came with a miracle of the kind in which they excelled, and the Qur'an came carrying the method of heaven until the Hour comes.

They asked that the mountains of Makkah be moved away so that the valley would be wide, for them to plant and harvest; and they asked for the cutting of the earth, that is, the separating of one tract from another; and this would happen by digging channels of water. The disbelievers had said: ﴿We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush for us from the earth.﴾ (Surat al-Isra')

What is meant by cutting the earth according to their request is that the distance between one place and another be shortened, so that the traveler can rest every stretch. The traveler leaves one land with each of his steps and reaches another land, and each person crosses the earth according to his capacity and the means of transport he uses.

The affluent want the distance between one tract of land and another to be great, because they own the steeds with which they can cover the distance easily; as for one who has no mount, he loves the distances to be near so that he can rest.

We observe that this is the case in our present age: when luxury has increased, cars cover the distance from Cairo to Alexandria without stopping, unlike what used to happen formerly, when cars needed rest and so did their travelers, and they would stop midway.

Something similar happened in the kingdom of Sheba. Al-Haqq, glory be to Him, says:

﴿So they said, "Our Lord, lengthen the distances between our journeys," and they wronged themselves...﴾ (Surat Saba') That is: make the distance between one place and another far, so that the capable traveler may enjoy the pleasant scenery. We also notice the excess of the polytheists of Quraysh in seeking extraordinary miracles, in that they asked for the revival of the dead, in the saying of al-Haqq:

﴿Or the dead were spoken to by it...﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd)

Some of them asked for the reviving of Qusay ibn Kilab, the greatest ancestor of the Messenger of Allah and of Quraysh, so that they might ask him: Is what Muhammad brought true? But the Qur'an did not come for such matters; and even if it had come with them, they would not have believed. The task of the Qur'an is centred on its being a final method suitable for every age; and that is its miracle.

He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Rather, to Allah belongs the affair entirely...﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd)

The word "amr" (affair) indicates one thing, and the word "jami'an" (entirely) indicates a plurality. Thus we find that the multiplicity of messages and miracles indicates only that every command of those messages proceeds from al-Haqq, glory be to Him; and He is the One who chose each miracle to suit the people among whom the Messenger is sent.

He, glory be to Him, continues:

﴿Have not those who believed despaired that, if Allah willed, He would have guided mankind entirely?...﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd)

The word "yay'as" (despair) is said here to mean "ya'lam" (know); it is a usage in the dialect of Quraysh. That is: did not those who believed know that these disbelievers would not be guided, because Allah did not will their guidance? The believers wished that the chieftains of Quraysh would believe, so that the burden on the Muslim group would be lightened, and they would not be persecuted, nor be harassed in their sustenance or in their families.

Here al-Haqq, glory be to Him, makes clear that this matter is not tied to the desire of the believer regarding these people; rather, faith is a matter that requires a person to empty what is in his heart of belief, look at issues with detachment, and what he becomes convinced of, he enters into his heart.

Thereby the doctrinal vessel is filled with what is beneficial; so that no belief enters your heart and no other belief comes to expel the first, or divert your heart from what you believe. He, exalted, says:

﴿Allah has not made for a man two hearts within his chest...﴾ (Surat al-Ahzab) The heart's vessel is exactly like the material vessel; it never accepts that two substances interpenetrate within it. If one substance enters upon another, the stronger of the two expels the weaker from the heart.

An example of this: suppose we have a vessel filled to the brim, and one of us tries to put into it a small iron ball. Here he will find that water overflows from the edges of the vessel in an amount equal to the volume of the iron ball. This is what happens in the material vessel, and likewise the case is with the doctrinal vessel.

Therefore al-Haqq, glory be to Him, says in the sacred hadith:

"My love and the love of the world do not combine in a heart."

Thus we see that there is a space for meanings just as there is a space for matter. So if you truly want the correct doctrinal meanings to enter your heart, you must first expel the contradictory meanings from the space of the heart; then seek through evidence the suitability of either of the two meanings. Whatever you find strong in proof, sound in logic, and abundant in strength and argument, admit it into your heart.

The disbelievers did not do this; rather, they persisted in error, insisting on the corrupt belief they held. As for those among them who embraced Islam, they removed the old belief from their hearts, and did not cling to their former conviction; rather, they studied and compared, and so they hastened to Islam.

As for one whose heart is occupied with the former belief, and who wants to enter the Islamic belief into his heart, he has not succeeded in that, because his heart is occupied with the old belief.

And if you, O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), want these people to believe, that must depend on their own will, and they must remove the corrupt belief from their hearts, and seek the more correct and better of the two beliefs. Therefore al-Haqq, glory be to Him, teaches us how to reach the truths with ease, and He says to His Messenger (ﷺ):

﴿Say, "I only advise you of one thing: that you stand up for Allah, in pairs and individually, and then reflect: there is no madness in your companion..."﴾ (Surat Saba') That is: say, O Muhammad, to the one who disbelieves in you: I advise you with an admonition, and you do not admonish except one whom you love to be upon the truth. This explains the saying of al-Haqq, glory be to Him:

﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; it grieves him what you suffer; he is anxious over you; for the believers, he is kind and merciful.﴾ (Surat al-Tawbah)

Hence the Messenger (ﷺ) wants you to be believers; therefore he calls you to stand for Allah, not for the status of anyone other than Him; for the status of any being will vanish, however great this one may be. Do not say to yourself that the servants will be equal to you. Rather, stand for Allah either in pairs, meaning that you stand with another, or let others stand two by two, so that each of you debates with whoever sits with him; and let none of you be partisan to a prior opinion, but direct his whole thought, detached, to Allah.

Let each one ask himself: this Muhammad, his description is such-and-such, he has done such-and-such, and the Qur'an he brought says such-and-such; and one of you will find himself guided to the truth between himself and himself, and between himself and the one who sat with him to debate, and the two of them will review with him the history of Muhammad (ﷺ) and what he brought.

When two people debate, neither fears that the other will defeat him; but if a third joins them, each wants to be proud of his opinion, refuses to accept the opinion of another person, and fears being considered defeated in the debate, and refuses for himself the possibility that anyone might belittle him. Therefore al-Haqq, glory be to Him, said:

﴿...in pairs and individually, then reflect: there is no madness in your companion...﴾ (Surat Saba') "Al-jinnah" is the disorder of the mind; that is, one who has madness acts and behaves in ways that the intellect does not approve. Al-Haqq, glory be to Him, links intellect with character, saying:

﴿And indeed, you are of a great character.﴾ (Surat al-Qalam)

It is said: so-and-so is "ʿalā khuluq", that is, he possesses the qualities that set him on the path of virtues, such as truthfulness and trustworthiness; and these are qualities which the intellectual thought arranges according to their situations, and it is the one that distinguishes for us which situations require firmness, or gentleness, or wisdom; all these are matters that the intellect arranges.

Exalted character does not proceed from a madman, because he does not know how to choose between alternatives; therefore we do not hold him accountable, and Allah does not hold him accountable either.

When al-Haqq, glory be to Him, commands them to investigate whether Muhammad suffers from madness, then al-Haqq, glory be to Him, knows in advance that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), by their own testimony, possesses perfection of character; the proof being that the most important things they possessed they entrusted to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

And the proof is that when he (ﷺ) entered upon them while they were disputing about the matter of rebuilding the Ka'bah, they accepted him as arbiter. Therefore He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe. You are not, by the blessing of your Lord, a madman.﴾ (Surat al-Qalam)

Thus we have seen that these disbelievers would not have believed, and Allah would not have guided them, because they possessed not the least readiness for guidance; as if they had become addicted to disbelief, we seek refuge with Allah; and Allah has sealed their hearts, increasing them in disbelief; so what is in those hearts of disbelief does not leave them, and what is outside does not enter them.

Some of the Muslims thought that the disbelief of these people might distress the believers through increased hardship from the disbelievers against them. Therefore al-Haqq, glory be to Him, makes clear to the people of faith that His help is near, and He says, glory be to Him:

﴿And those who disbelieve will not cease to be struck by what they have done, a calamity, or it will descend near their home, until the promise of Allah comes. Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise.﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd) That is: be reassured, O people of faith; the state of the people of disbelief will not remain as it is; rather, calamities will strike them while they are in their places, and they will see with their own eyes how faith spreads in the places they dominate; the area of the land of faith expands, and the domain of the people of disbelief shrinks; then comes the help of Allah, and the help of Allah has come, and there remained in the Arabian Peninsula none but one who says: "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."

Thus the verse foretold the coming of hope after despair, so that despair would not remain in control of the movement of the Muslims and their souls. Al-Haqq, glory be to Him, responded to the supplication of His Messenger (ﷺ) when he prayed: "O Allah, make it upon them as the years of Yusuf." Their chieftains were killed one after another; but their obstinacy persisted, and the obstinacy reached the point that the two daughters of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were married to the two sons of Abu Lahab. When the Prophet (ﷺ) announced his message, Abu Lahab and his wife said: our sons must divorce Muhammad's daughters. When the first of them divorced the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) supplicated against the one who

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 13, verse 32:

It is said "hazi'a bi-fulan" (he mocked so-and-so), meaning he ridiculed him. As for "istuhzi'a bi-fulan," it means he asked another person to mock a specific individual, and the sin of that falls on him as well as on whoever he incited to ridicule this person. The words of the Truthful, glorified is He: ﴿And messengers before you were certainly mocked, but I gave respite to those who disbelieved; then I seized them, so how was My retribution?﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd, 13:32). That is: you are no novelty, O Muhammad, in that some of the disbelievers take this stance toward you. The model for this is al-Hakam, the father of Abu Marwan, who used to imitate the gait of the Prophet (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) walked as though he were descending a slope, and his gaze was always cast down to the ground.

The people were not accustomed to that humble gait; they walked with arrogance, swaggering and displaying their shoulders.

When al-Hakam imitated the Messenger of Allah, the Messenger (ﷺ) saw him with the light of insight, and said to him (ﷺ): "Be like this," so his gait became a permanent affliction, whereas the gait of the Messenger of Allah was a lowering of himself before his Lord and a humility on his part (ﷺ).

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) banished al-Hakam to al-Ta'if, and he took to tending sheep there. The Prophet (ﷺ) did not pardon him; nor did Abu Bakr during his caliphate, nor 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. But the one who pardoned him was 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, who was a relative of his.

'Uthman ibn 'Affan bore witness and said: "By Allah, I asked the Messenger of Allah about him, and he said to me: 'If you can pardon him, then pardon him.' And when I became responsible for the affairs of the Muslims, I pardoned him."

Later it happened that 'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan became ruler over the Muslims. His son al-Walid had horses that competed with the horses of the sons of Yazid ibn Mu'awiya. The sons of Yazid resorted to deceit and placed obstacles to hinder al-Walid's horses.

A dispute broke out between the two sides, and al-Walid insulted the sons of Yazid. The sons of Yazid went to 'Abd al-Malik to complain to him about his son. The one who complained could not speak Arabic without error. 'Abd al-Malik said to him: "Why do you not straighten your tongue from solecism?" The complainant replied sarcastically: "By Allah, I was impressed by al-Walid's eloquence." He meant that the condition of the tongue of Ibn 'Abd al-Malik is no different from the condition of the tongue of the one complaining; both do not speak fluently, and solecism is frequent in their speech of Arabic.

'Abd al-Malik said: "Do you reproach me with 'Abd Allah, my son, who does not speak Arabic without solecism? His brother Khalid does not commit solecism." And he followed this with his saying: "Be silent, O man, for you are neither in the caravan nor in the troop."

This is a proverb we use today, and it has come down to us through Quraysh, where authority had two sources: the caravan (al-'Ir), meaning the trade that came by the caravans from Syria, whose leader was Abu Sufyan; and the troop (al-Nafir), meaning the people who mobilized to rescue Abu Sufyan at the Battle of Badr, who were led by 'Utba. The son of Yazid then said: "And who has a better claim to the caravan and the troop than I?" He meant that he is the grandson of Abu Sufyan on his father's side and the grandson of 'Utba on his mother's side.

He added: "But if you had said 'small flocks' and 'little goats' and mentioned al-Ta'if, you would have been right. May Allah have mercy on 'Uthman, who pardoned your grandfather and brought him back from exile." We know that the Truthful, glorified and exalted is He, said to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿Indeed, We suffice you against the mockers﴾ (Surat al-Hijr, 15:95), and that whoever mocked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would meet a divine punishment. Here the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿And messengers before you were certainly mocked, but I gave respite to those who disbelieved; then I seized them, so how was My retribution?﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd, 13:32). So you, O Messenger of Allah, are no novelty among the messengers, and you have a model in the messengers. The Truthful, glorified is He, promises you here in His well-guarded Book: ﴿So I gave respite to those who disbelieved…﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd, 13:32). That is: I gave respite to those who disbelieved. Al-imla' (respite) in the sense of postponement does not mean abandoning punishment for the sin; rather, it is delaying punishment for a sin yet to come. The model is that you leave a wrongdoer who committed a lapse until he commits a second lapse, then a third, and then punishment descends upon him from where he does not expect it.

If this is what happens in the world of men, then what of the limitless might of the Truthful, glorified is He, who says: ﴿We will draw them gradually [to destruction] from where they do not know﴾ (Surat al-A'raf, 7:182)?

He, exalted is He, also says: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve think that Our giving them respite is good for them. We only give them respite that they may increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment﴾ (Surat Aal 'Imran, 3:178), exactly as one finds a person who sets a trap for his enemy. Here the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿And messengers before you were certainly mocked, but I gave respite to those who disbelieved; then I seized them, so how was My retribution?﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd, 13:32).

The word ﴿so how was My retribution?﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd, 13:32) shows that it was a severe punishment. Therefore the Truthful, glorified is He, says elsewhere:

﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed. And when they passed by them, they exchanged winks. And when they returned to their people, they returned jesting. And when they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are misguided." But they had not been sent as watchers over them. So today, those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers, on couches, observing. Have the disbelievers not been rewarded for what they used to do?﴾ (Surat al-Mutaffifin, 83:29-36).

So then: those who mocked the messengers will surely receive severe punishment.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 13, verse 33:

One might ask: Since He said ﴿Is then He who stands over every soul in what it has earned (as if they were equal to those who have no such standing)?﴾ [13:33], was it not necessary to bring the counterpart and say: "Like one who is not standing over every soul in what it has earned?"

To such a questioner we say: This is the greatness of the Qur'an, which leaves to the intellect what it can deduce (istinbat, derivation of meaning), and so it brings forth things that require reflection and deduction, so that a person realises that he is receiving the words of a wise Lord, and that it is incumbent upon him to probe into it.

Hence our master ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud said: "Stir up the Qur'an" (thawwiru al-Qur'an), meaning: stir it up, so that you may discover the treasures within it.

We know that the expression "qa'im ʿala al-amr" (standing over the affair) means that He is the One who manages and administers it, and nothing is hidden from Him. The Truth, glorified is He, has come here in the form of the participle of standing (qiyam), so that we know that the Truth, glorified is He, does not manage the affair from a state of sitting; rather He manages it while standing over it, so every matter is clear to Him and not hidden.

He, glorified is He, stands over every soul in what it has earned: if good, then good; and if evil, then evil. But you, O disbelievers and polytheists, do not possess for yourselves any harm or benefit. So can any intelligent person equate the One who stands over the affair of every soul with others who do not do so?

But there are those of whom the Truth, glorified is He, speaks in the same verse:

﴿And they have set up for Allah partners...﴾ [13:33], meaning: they have set up, for the One who stands over the affair of every soul, partners who cannot manage even their own affairs, and therefore cannot manage the affairs of others. Indeed, an idol of theirs may suffer a crack, and then someone comes to those who worship it to set it right, crying out that their god has cracked and needs two nails to fix it. So how do they equate that idol with Allah, whom nothing limits and whose power nothing restricts?

The saying of the Truth, glorified is He:

﴿And they have set up for Allah partners...﴾ [13:33]

is evidence for the omitted text: "like one who is not standing over every soul." He, glorified is He, is not like these powerless idols, because He stands over every soul: your soul, the souls of others, and the soul of every human who has lived or will live.

Hence He, glorified is He, says after this:
﴿Say: Name them. Or do you inform Him of what He does not know on earth, or of mere outward speech?﴾ [13:33]

Here the Truth, glorified is He, commands His Messenger to say to those who disbelieve in Allah: Name those whom you worship besides Allah; they are stones, and stones have no names. They have named the idols with names such as al-Lat, al-ʿUzza and Hubal, and these names added nothing to those idols; they cannot do anything. Had they been named, the naming would be attributed to ʿAmr ibn Luhayy, who brought them about; yet it is they who named them.

The true God is not named by anyone; rather He names Himself. But since the matter is falsehood upon falsehood, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asks them about the names of those deities. He says to them: Do you inform Allah, the Creator of the whole universe, of what He does not know in His universe, which He brought into existence from nothing?

He, glorified is He, knows all that He has created, while you worship only idols to which the description "mere outward speech" applies, that is, speech without meaning, because they gave names to things that have no inner reality and no power to act. They were content with the outward form, while the named thing does not exist.

The Truth, glorified is He, says:
