﴿Rather, the plotting of those who disbelieve has been made attractive to them, and they have been barred from the way...﴾ [13:33], meaning: they thought they were deceiving Allah, and they said that those idols are gods, and they are not. Then He, glorified is He, says:
﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾ [13:33], meaning: the punishment they suffer in the life of this world is to preserve the movement of society from corruption, and punishment must befall them in this worldly life; and because whoever has his punishment postponed to the Hereafter must first see in himself a sign of punishment before he receives his punishment in the Hereafter.

Thus: the punishment of this world is to protect the movement of life; and this is why we find laws enacted to be applied to the deviant; the wrongdoer fears that the eye will fall upon him, and if anyone sees him he reports him so that he may receive his punishment; and thereby the movement of life is kept upright.

Hence we find the Truth, glorified is He, saying in Surat al-Kahf:
﴿They ask you about Dhu al-Qarnayn. Say: I will recite to you a remembrance of him. Indeed, We established him on earth and gave him of every thing a means. So he followed a means until, when he reached the setting place of the sun, he found it setting in a spring of black mud, and found near it a people. We said: O Dhu al-Qarnayn, either you punish them, or you adopt among them goodness. He said: As for one who wrongs, we will punish him; then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a terrible punishment.﴾ [18:83-87]

meaning: he was given authority to establish the affair among these people, and he established it on the basis of reward and punishment; whoever does good has a good recompense, and whoever does evil receives punishment. Thus we find the punishment of this world necessary for the safety of the movement of life from the oppression of those who do not believe in Allah.

Surah 13, verse 34 (ar-Ra'd) is the text under discussion. Here is the translation of the commentary passage:

For these polytheists who do not believe in the Hereafter there is a punishment in this world, through killing, captivity, calamities and disasters over which they have no power, and above that, for them is a punishment in the Hereafter more severe than the punishment of this world. So there is none for them to protect them, nor anyone who could place between them and the punishment of Allah a shield or a safeguard.

The primary source who promised the God-conscious (al-muttaqun) Paradise here is Allah, and the messengers (peace be upon them) conveyed this promise, and the scholars who convey from the messengers followed them. When you look at a verb that is common among a number of sources, you can seek out the primary source. An example is the saying of the Truthful, glorified is He: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death..﴾ [42] (Surat al-Zumar), and He says in another place in the Qur'an: ﴿Say: The Angel of Death who has been entrusted with you will take you (tawaffa) ..﴾ [11] (Surat al-Sajdah).

Thus the taking (tawaffi) has been attributed to Allah, and attributed to the Angel of Death. The Angel of Death has taken on the responsibility of taking souls, since the Truth (al-Haqq) assigned him that task; attributing it to the Angel of Death is a kind of clarification of the party to whom the Truth, glorified is He, has entrusted the execution of the task. And at times the Truth, glorified is He, mentions the original source that issues the command to the Angel of Death to carry out his task. Here in this noble verse we find the saying of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿The God-conscious were promised..﴾ [35] (Surat al-Ra'd).

The verb is in the passive form (mabni lima lam yusamma fa'iluh, the passive voice, i.e. the agent is not named); the promise comes from Him, glorified is He. We know that the Messenger (ﷺ) also made promises. Indeed, the report of the Pledge of al-'Aqabah has reached us: when he took the pledge from the Ansar, they said to him: "Take for yourself," so he took for himself what he wanted. Then they said to him: "And what shall we receive if we fulfil this?" He said to them: "For you is Paradise."

He (ﷺ) said that because the deed they performed is not repaid by anything except Paradise. It is reasonable that any one of those who attended al-'Aqabah might die after the covenant of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); so if he had promised them worldly enjoyments, which some might take afterwards, then whoever died before this would not attain any of what the Messenger promised those who made the covenant with him. Therefore he gave them what does not run out, which is the promise of Paradise.

And the Truth, glorified is He, here in the verse we are contemplating says: ﴿The likeness (mathal) of Paradise..﴾ [35] (Surat al-Ra'd). That is: He only strikes the likeness for us; because the words we address one another with were set for meanings we know. If in Paradise there are things no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and that have not occurred to any human heart, then it is possible to say that we have no words that convey the meaning of what is there; so Allah strikes likenesses for us with what we see of pleasures, but He removes from them what is turbid and clouded.

Thus we know there is a difference between "the likeness of Paradise" and "Paradise". The likeness gives me an image I hear about a reality I do not know; because the meaning of representation (tamthil) is to attach the unknown to the known in order to take judgment from it, just as you say to a friend: "Do you know so-and-so?" and he says: "No." So you say to him: "He resembles so-and-so whom you know."

You do this in order to liken the unknown to the known, so that the image comes to the mind of your listener. The Messenger (ﷺ) says, explaining what the Qur'an stated in summary: ﴿And therein is whatever the souls desire and that which delights the eyes..﴾ [71] (Surat al-Zukhruf).

And he (ﷺ) adds: "Therein is what no eye has seen, nor ear has heard, nor has occurred to the heart of a human being."

When you examine this noble prophetic saying you find a complete ascent (taraqqi): his saying "what no ear has heard" comes because he knows that what the eye perceives is limited compared with what the ear hears; because the ear hears what the eye does not perceive; it hears what others see in addition to what you see.

The ear hears the near and hears the distant, conveys its sound, brings it to mind, and then distinguishes it, unlike the eye, which is limited in distance according to the strength of sight; and with all this, the bliss of Paradise is above all this above. Then comes the greater ascent in his saying: "nor has occurred to the heart of a human being." Thoughts are wider than the power of the ear and the power of the eye; thoughts imagine things that may not exist.

Thus we see the inability of language to contain words that express what exists in Paradise, and none of us knows what the things in Paradise are, since none of us has seen Paradise.

And since the Messenger (ﷺ) said: "Therein is what no eye has seen, nor ear has heard, nor has occurred to the heart of a human being,"

then we must know the extent of language's inability to express what is in Paradise. So when Allah wants to express what is in it, He clarifies for us by likeness, not by description, because He knows that our language sets words for what exists in our lives, and there are no words in our language that convey the meanings of what is in Paradise. Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, said to us:

﴿The likeness of Paradise which the God-conscious were promised: therein are rivers of water unaltered, and rivers of milk whose taste does not change, and rivers of wine, a delight to the drinkers, and rivers of clarified honey..﴾ [15] (Surat Muhammad).

Although the Truth, glorified is He, strikes a likeness, He has purified the likeness of the flaws we know in this world. Water, when it flows, is sweet, clear and pure; but if it stagnates it becomes foul and stale. Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, clarifies for us that the water in Paradise is not foul; rather, it is rivers from which whatever would cloud it has been removed.

Likewise the likeness of rivers of milk whose taste does not change. Milk, as we know, is the food of the nomads: they milk the livestock and keep their milk in waterskins for a long time, so the taste of the milk changes; therefore the likeness is struck for them with the existence of rivers of milk whose taste does not change.

Also the likeness is struck with the existence of rivers of clarified honey. Honey, as we know, originally came from bees that used to dwell in the mountains before they were domesticated and placed in apiaries in gardens. The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, is the One who said: ﴿And your Lord inspired the bee: take for yourselves dwellings in the mountains, and in trees, and in what they build..﴾ [68] (Surat al-Nahl).

When entomologists researched the history of the bee, they found that the oldest honey in the world is that which existed in mountain caves; after it in age comes the honey that came from beehives, those hives which bees built after being domesticated; and after that comes the honey for which we ourselves set up apiaries.

They distinguished old honey from medium and new by burning some of each kind of honey, whereupon carbon resulted from the burning; and from this element they discovered the age of each of the three kinds.

The Truth, glorified is He, clarifies that in Paradise there are rivers of clarified honey, and thereby presents to us the best of what we loved of worldly honey, but without anything that clouds it.

He, glorified is He, also clarifies that in Paradise there are rivers of wine, but it is a wine that differs from the wine of this world; it does not affect the organic structure of the intellect, whereas the wine of this world has nothing delightful for its drinkers, because it is of alcohol that burns and stings the mouth. Therefore you find one who drinks it pouring it into his mouth so that it passes quickly and he does not feel its sting in his mouth, and it goes straight to his stomach and inflames it.

The situation differs if the drink is juice of mango, orange or sugarcane, where the soul finds the taste of those fruits pleasant; you find the one who drinks them taking his time to hold their effect in his mouth. The Truth, glorified is He, says about the wine of Paradise's rivers: ﴿No headache comes from it..﴾ [47] (Surat al-Saffat). That is: He, glorified is He, negates from the wine of Paradise's rivers all the turbid things found in the wine of this world.

So: when you hear, for example, about Paradise, know that it is an approximate likeness, because the reality cannot come, since there is no word that expresses it; it does not exist among us; and He, glorified is He, addresses us only with what we know of language; therefore He brings us the likeness struck, so that we take from it an approximate image.

Here in the verse we are contemplating, the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿The likeness of Paradise which the God-conscious were promised: beneath it rivers flow..﴾ [35] (Surat al-Ra'd)

We know that the lifeblood of the Arabs at the time the Qur'an was revealed was water; did they not ask the Messenger to cause rivers to gush forth for them? We find the Truth, glorified is He, has expressed the rivers of Paradise in the Qur'anic wording in two different forms:

The first: ﴿beneath it rivers flow..﴾ [35] (Surat al-Ra'd)

as He said in the verse we are contemplating. And at another time He, glorified is He, says:

﴿beneath which rivers flow..﴾ [100] (Surat al-Tawbah)

The difference between the two expressions is the encompassing of perfection in the text, meaning that:

﴿from beneath it rivers flow..﴾ [35] (Surat al-Ra'd)

makes clear that the sources of those rivers come from directly beneath that Paradise; so the water in those rivers never diminishes.

It is said that the difference between the rivers of this world and the rivers of Paradise is that the rivers of this world are cracks in the earth with banks that contain them; whereas the rivers of the Hereafter flow over the earth without banks to restrain them. We find that the rivers of wine also flow over the earth, and do not mix with the rivers of water, and likewise the rivers of milk, and all of that is by the craftsmanship of a wise, capable Lord. As for His saying:

﴿beneath which rivers flow..﴾ [100] (Surat al-Tawbah), that is: their sources are not directly beneath them; rather they come without lack from a direction you do not know; and He is capable of all things. He, glorified is He, continues, saying of that Paradise: ﴿Its food is perpetual..﴾ [35] (Surat al-Ra'd). Food (akl) is what is eaten, and He, glorified is He, is the One who said: ﴿It gives its food every season by the permission of its Lord..﴾ [25] (Surat Ibrahim).

His saying: ﴿Its food is perpetual..﴾ [35] (Surat al-Ra'd) means: it does not cease. We know that when a person eats, he does so in order to satisfy his hunger; and after he is satisfied, he may ask for the food to be removed from before him, until he becomes hungry again and asks for food anew.

Among those who love food in our worldly life, you see one of them saying: "I feel some discomfort because I am full," as he is in a struggle between a soul that craves and a belly that is never satisfied, as though he wanted to continue eating food all the time.

The saying of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿Its food is perpetual..﴾ [35] (Surat al-Ra'd)

preoccupied the Romans, who were masters of a great empire that Islam shook with its nascent civilisation. Their emperor sent someone to ask one of the caliphs to send a man capable of explaining the saying of the Truth: ﴿Its food is perpetual..﴾ [35] (Surat al-Ra'd). So he sent them one of the scholars, and they asked him: "Your Qur'an says that the food of Paradise is perpetual; and you and we know that everything that is taken from has to diminish; so how can the food of Paradise be perpetual?"

The scholar said to them: "Bring a lamp." They brought him a lamp and he lit it before them. He said to each of them: "Let each of you bring his lamp." Each of them brought his lamp. He said to them: "Let each of you light his lamp." Then he asked them: "Has the lighting of your lamps diminished this lamp at all?" They said: "No, nothing." He said to them: "Thus Allah has struck the likeness with the food of Paradise."

Naturally, they should have noticed that the lamp depends for its burning on the oil stored in it and is replenished from it, whereas the provision of Paradise is from Allah.

Some said: "Do we defecate in Paradise?" One of those who knew replied: "No." He asked: "Then where do the remains of the food of Paradise go?"

The knower of Allah said: "Just as the remains of what a child feeds on in his mother's womb go; where this surplus is burned up in the placenta of the child; and the child in his mother's womb grows continuously, relying on nourishment that reaches him from his mother through the umbilical cord."

All these matters are approximations that let us cross the gap between what we witness in our daily lives and what Allah has prepared for the God-conscious, He who is the Sustainer over every matter. The Truth, glorified is He, has said: ﴿Its food is perpetual and its shade..﴾ [35] (Surat al-Ra'd).

That is: the food is present and does not end, and likewise the shade. Shade is the screening of the light from a place, or the screening of a place from the light; and no one knows whether there will be a sun there or not; and the human mind is incapable of imagining that; it is the act of Allah, and He, glorified is He, is capable of all things.

He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever; for them therein are purified spouses, and We will admit them to deep, dense shade.﴾ [57] (Surat al-Nisa')

And He, glorified is He, said:

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 13, verse 36:

We know that Islam was preceded by two religions: the religion of the Christians, the people of Jesus (peace be upon him), and before it the religion of the Jews, the people of Moses (peace be upon him). Each of these two religions has a scripture: the Gospel is the book of Christianity, and the Torah is the book of Judaism. The Qur'an is the book of God, the muhaymin (the one that guards and preserves what came before) and the seal (the final one), the book of Islam. There are also other heavenly scriptures, such as the scrolls of Abraham, the Psalms of David, and others.

It was incumbent upon those to whom the Torah and the Gospel were revealed to continue in faith, supported by the help of heaven and the good that comes down from it to the earth. God had already taken a covenant from their prophets to this effect, and He, exalted is He, said:

﴿And when God took the covenant of the prophets: "Whatever I have given you of Scripture and wisdom, and then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and you must help him." He said: "Do you affirm and accept My covenant on this condition?" They said: "We affirm it." He said: "Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses."﴾ (Surah Aal 'Imran, 81)

Thus we know that the Truth, glorified is He, willed that every earlier religion should receive the one that follows it with belief in it. In every earlier religion, the texts affirmed the necessity of believing in the messenger who was to come, so that there would be no contest between the abrogating religions and the abrogated religions.

It is among the essential contents of any earlier religion that it awaits the religion that follows it; when the new religion comes, it receives it as a branch and a completion, and does not receive it as a religion opposed to the earlier one.

If Islam is the religion with which the procession of messengers is sealed, then the religions before it must have given good tidings of it, and every believer in the earlier religions is enjoined to believe in it. The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿He has prescribed for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah, and that which We have revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus: that you should establish the religion and not be divided therein.﴾ (Surah ash-Shura, 13)

The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And those to whom We have given the Scripture rejoice in what has been sent down to you…﴾ (Surah ar-Ra'd, 36). That is: the people of the Torah and the Gospel rejoice in what has come, O Muhammad, of the Qur'an. A person does not rejoice in anything unless it fulfils for him a goal that makes him happy, and that goal must be publicized and known. They rejoiced in what was sent down to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), because it fulfilled for them what had been foretold of him in their books.

This means that their books had been true, and whoever brings the final message is true, and it was incumbent upon them to be the first to hasten to believe in him. For joy is the expressive or dispositional act arising from the states of love, and a person rejoices only at the attainment of a good matter that he had been awaiting. Therefore they should have rushed to believe in the new religion and declared their faith in it, as Ka'b al-Ahbar, 'Abdullah ibn Salam, and Salman al-Farisi did, the last of whom traversed most of the lands seeking the true religion.

These are merely examples of those who wished to express their joy and to receive the help of heaven through the coming of the final Prophet, Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah (peace be upon him). They declared allegiance to the new Messenger as the earlier heavenly scriptures had announced his coming. Then others stood in hostility toward those who did not rejoice at the arrival of the Messenger, and then they altered what had come in their heavenly scriptures out of greed for temporal power.

Those who believed in the message of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) came to know that those who denied the prophethood of Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah had deceived themselves and others, and had brought things that were not present in their scriptures sent down to their messengers, such as their claim that God has sons, and He is exalted above that:

﴿And those to whom We have given the Scripture rejoice in what has been sent down to you, but among the factions are those who deny part of it. Say: "I have only been commanded to worship God and not to associate anything with Him. To Him I call, and to Him is my return."﴾ (Surah ar-Ra'd, 36)

That is justice from the Qur'an, because the Qur'an did not deny the earlier heavenly scriptures in their foundations; rather, it denied the distortion in the beliefs, and denied the positions of those who distorted and falsely claimed that God has offspring.

This distortion did not make the Qur'an deny everything that came in the scriptures prior to the Qur'an; rather, it denied only the distortion.

The Qur'an affirmed what belongs to God and what belongs to the Messenger, and denied the distortion by which they sought temporal power, the claim of sanctity, trading in indulgence certificates and selling Paradise, accepting confessions, and other things that no heavenly scripture had sent down.

When Islam came to forbid all that, they defended their authority, by which they trade in matters of religion, and that authority is not part of religion.

Consider the words of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿Say: "I have only been commanded to worship God and not to associate anything with Him…"﴾ (Surah ar-Ra'd, 36). This saying is evidence that those who altered the heavenly scriptures, or who denied the oneness of God, were addressed with this detailed statement: ﴿I have only been commanded to worship God…﴾ (Surah ar-Ra'd, 36). That is: he affirms that there is a religion that has been chosen for him by a Lord; Muhammad did not choose something that pleased him to worship, but he is, as a messenger from God, honored to belong to what he was commanded from heaven, and he associates no one with Him. We find the Messenger (peace be upon him) zealous regarding what concerns his Lord, while he may be lenient regarding what concerns his own person.

For this reason, some atheists said to him: "We believe in God, in heaven, in revelation and in everything, but we do not believe in you." The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) did not become angry. Had he been bringing his own self or egotism into the matter, he would have been angry, but he was not angry.

The proof of this is that his rejoicing (peace be upon him) was with the Byzantines, who believed in a heavenly scripture, against the polytheists who did not believe in a heavenly religion, namely the Persians. He (peace be upon him) grieved when the Byzantines were defeated, and then the Truth's word came down to him with the news of the coming victory within a few years, as consolation to him (peace be upon him):

﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The Byzantines have been defeated in the nearest land, but after their defeat they will overcome within a few years. To God belongs the command, before and after. On that day the believers will rejoice in God's help; He helps whom He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ (Surah ar-Rum, 1–5)

These people were closer to the heart of the Messenger of God than others, because they followed a heavenly religion; and when he sees the scent of one who does good, he prefers him over the one who does evil. He seeks victory for them, and God gives him good tidings of their victory within a few years, and they carry the scent of goodness, although they did not believe in the Messenger of God (peace be upon him). The meaning of: ﴿Say: "I have only been commanded to worship God and not to associate anything with Him…"﴾ (Surah ar-Ra'd, 36) is that I will worship God alone, and I will not give anything equal standing with His worship; and he calls to worship Him alone, because he knows that he will return to Him, just as every human being will return to Him. No one escapes from his Lord and Creator, and every person must prepare his provision for this return.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 13, verse 37:

The intended meaning of "kadhalika" (thus) is a reference to the sending of the earlier Messengers with miracles that God, glory be to Him, willed, and which no one proposed. And His saying: ﴿We have sent it down...﴾ [13:37]

When we hear it, we perceive that there is a lofty station from which something descends to a lower station, and such a thing is well known in sensible matters, and it is also well known in matters of meaning.

Indeed, this thing may not have reached the heavens, but may be on the earth, and yet the Truthful One, glory be to Him, says of it: ﴿And We sent down iron, wherein is great might and benefits for mankind﴾ [57:25]. It is a sending down, because it is a matter of the arrangement of the heavens, even if it is on the earth. And: ﴿Thus We have sent it down as an Arabic judgment﴾ [13:37].

"Hukm" (judgment) is the meaning, and the intended "sending down" here is the Qur'an, and it is a Book; and the Book is form and meaning. God, glory be to Him, willed here to use the intensive form of the attribute, so that the attribute comes as though it were the essence itself; that is, He sent down the Qur'an as a judgment. This means that the Qur'an in its very essence is judgment.

When you describe a judge who rules with perfect justice, you do not say "a just judge" (qadi 'adil) but rather "a judge of justice" (qadi 'adl), meaning as if justice had taken bodily form in the judge, and as if his whole constitution were justice. The Truthful One, glory be to Him, here makes clear that the Qur'an is the just judgment, and describes it as: ﴿an Arabic judgment﴾ [13:37], because the tongue with which the Messenger addresses the people who receive with their ears what he says to them must be Arabic. Therefore He says in another verse: ﴿And indeed it is a reminder for you and your people, and you will be questioned﴾ [43:44], that is: it is a great honour for you and your people that the Qur'an was sent down in the language of the Arabs.

The Qur'an has preserved for us the Arabic language sound and pure, whereas we find that all the languages of the world have first branched into dialects, then each dialect became independent and turned into a language, such as the Latin language from which most of the contemporary European languages emerged: English, French and Italian. We found that those languages split into independent languages, and each of them came to have different rules.

Indeed, the English language, for example, has become "British English" spoken by the people of Britain, and "American English" spoken by the people of the United States.

If we were to leave the language of communication among us as Muslims and Arabs in favour of the colloquial speech prevalent in our various countries, some of us would not understand one another, and the basis of our mutual understanding when we speak is the standard language (al-fusha). Our evidence is what we have seen in our Arab Maghrib: we find a person raised on the French language, or one whose language is a mixture of various Berber dialects, French and remnants of Arabic. If you speak to him in colloquial language he understands nothing from you, but if you speak with him in the Arabic language he responds and answers, because his nature receives the standard language with understanding and comprehension.

Thus we have seen how the noble Qur'an has preserved the Arabic language and the Arabic tongue. Among the meanings of the Truthful One's saying: ﴿an Arabic judgment﴾ [13:37] is that the one who protects and safeguards this Arabic tongue is the noble Qur'an. He continues, glory be to Him, saying:

﴿And if you were to follow their desires after the knowledge that has come to you, you would have against God no protector nor defender﴾ [13:37]. This is an address from Him, glory be to Him, to His Messenger (ﷺ), in which the Truthful One reveals to His Messenger (ﷺ) the harms and gravity of following desires; and it is an address which indicates that the religion revealed to Moses and then Jesus, the two who preceded the Messenger of God, no longer remained as it was in the time of those two previous Messengers; rather desire entered into it, and the religion no longer remained firm as it had been sent down from heaven. Therefore He, glory be to Him, says in another verse:

﴿And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth would have been corrupted﴾ [23:71].

That is because, if He, glory be to Him, had followed their desires, the order of the universe would have been lost. Did they not say to the Messenger of God (ﷺ): ﴿Or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you claim﴾ [17:92]?

And if the Truthful One had responded to this call, for example, would the heavens not have been corrupted?

So, after the Qur'an has come down from heaven as judgment, knowledge and a method that is easy for them to understand, because it is in their language, and it carries the complete method until the Hour comes, and in it is the guidance to happiness in this world and the Hereafter.

Therefore no one has the right to follow his own desire, for desire, as we know, differs from one person to another, and the address directed to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) contains within it an address to his Ummah (ﷺ).

Whoever does that, then he will have, apart from God, no protector to support or help him, or to shield him from the punishment of the Truthful One: wretchedness in this world, and being cast into Hellfire in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 13, verse 38:

And you, O Muhammad, are not a novelty among the Messengers in the matter of marriage and having offspring. This also carries the response to those who said: ﴿What is this Messenger that he eats food and walks in the markets?﴾ (Surah al-Furqan, 25:7)

And among them were those who said: "What is this Messenger that he marries women? Would it not have been more fitting for him to devote himself to his call?" Those who said this did not survey the procession of the Messengers, for had they done so, they would have found that most of the Messengers married and had children.

When the Messenger's life is close, as a clear example, to the lives of the people to whom he was sent, so that he may be an exemplar (uswah) for them, then the exemplary character is achieved through a comparable kind of human being. And when the Messenger's life is like the life of other human beings in its general framework, as a father and a husband, the exemplary character is clear to people. We know that there was a man who came to the Messenger of Allah seeking permission to devote himself entirely to worship through: fasting, prayer, and abstaining from women. The Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade that, and said in a noble hadith: "Indeed, I am the most fearful of you of Allah and the most mindful of Him, but I fast and I break my fast, I pray and I sleep, and I marry women. Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me."

The Truthful One, glorified be He, continues: ﴿And it was not for any Messenger to bring a sign except by permission of Allah. For every term is a decree.﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 13:38) That is: it was not for anyone to propose to Allah the sign that would accompany any of the Messengers, and no Messenger had the right to choose the sign that accompanies him.

By this statement the Truthful One, glorified be He, settled the matter of the polytheists' demand for signs from the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace; for every Messenger came for his own time and his own people, and every miracle was by Allah's choice, and every Messenger carries out what Allah assigns to him. It is not for the Messenger to propose to Allah any sign, because the Most High Creator is the most knowing of what suits this environment through the tongue of this Messenger. And we take from His saying, the Truth:

﴿For every term is a decree.﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 13:38) that every message has its messenger, every message has its place, and every message has its miracle. If this is the case, then leave Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and what Allah has chosen for him, in the place Allah willed, and in the time, and in the miracle that accompanies him, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

But, is there a change after the Truthful One, glorified be He, says: ﴿For every term is a decree.﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 13:38)?

Erasure (al-mahw) is, as we know, removal, and affirmation (al-tathbit) means that the truth remains as He sees it fixed. Some people have mistakenly understood that every ruling in the Qur'an came to be affirmed and will remain so forever; but in application it became apparent that some rulings required changing, which God changes for a wisdom in it that is good for mankind.

We say: no, that did not happen. Rather, there were rulings that were stage-based (marhaliyya), having a specified duration. For this reason the word of the Truth, glorified is He, came: ﴿And with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾ [13:39]

(Surat al-Ra'd). That is: with Him is the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz), in which the rulings having a specified duration are determined; and as soon as one ends, another ruling descends in its place. In this sense we can say: there is no abrogation (naskh) of rulings at all, because every ruling is bound to a fixed time that does not shift from its time; since every ruling is limited to a set time, and as soon as the time ends, a new ruling begins.

I say this so that I may alert the scholars to the necessity of sitting together to study this, so that the scholars do not disagree over whether there is abrogation or not. I say: let us define abrogation (naskh) first, because some think that there is a ruling that was supposed to apply to all times, then another ruling came to replace it for a wisdom required by the benefit of mankind and what God intends by it.

No ruling ended another ruling and arose at the moment of ending; rather, all rulings were predestined from eternity. Accordingly, there is no abrogation of any ruling; but there are rulings whose time, which God determined for them, comes to an end, and a ruling whose determination preceded from eternity comes to be followed by people. Since this is the case, there is no abrogation. Let us look at the word of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿Whatever sign We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring one better than it or similar to it...﴾ [2:106] (Surat al-Baqara).

It is clear from the explicit wording and the implicit meaning of the verse that when a ruling is abrogated, God brings one like it or better than it. Therefore: there is no abrogation, but there are rulings that perform their task in a time, then a time comes that requires a ruling better than it or similar to it in ruling, yet which accords with the unrestricted benefits (al-masalih al-mursala) together with the intention of God.

One may say: since He brings something better than the abrogated or postponed verse, that is better; but why does He bring the similar?

I answer: because if something better than it comes to you, you may accept it readily; but when we move to something similar to what the verse brought, this is the touchstone of faith (mahakk al-iman).

The similar was the orientation in prayer toward Bayt al-Maqdis at the beginning of the call; then came the command to change the qibla to the Ka'ba. There is no hardship in this; but here the adherence of faith to the obligation is tested, and here is submission to the ruling that God sends down, which is a ruling predestined from eternity; and in this is a test of faith's certainty in the management of the direction of the One who governs this course.

Likewise in the Hajj: the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to kiss the Black Stone; then he stones the stone that symbolizes Iblis. We do this following the example of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace; both are stones, but we comply with his command, may God bless him and grant him peace. So kissing the Black Stone and stoning the stone that points to the symbolism of Iblis—all of this is a response to the command of the Commander.

When the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿God erases what He wills and affirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾ [13:39] (Surat al-Ra'd), He means that He, glorified is He, ends the period of the former ruling whose term ends in the Mother of the Book, that is the Preserved Tablet; then the new ruling comes.

An example: the ruling on wine (khamr). The Truth, glorified is He, first treated it in a way that accords with the capacity of society; the first requirement was the establishment of belief (tathbit al-aqida); then the rulings came after that.

There is a difference between belief, which is the foundation, and the rulings, which carry the manner of doctrinal commitment; the ruling in matters of belief was binding and continuous.

As for rulings such as the ruling on wine, its prohibition was gradual in a way that suits people's familiarity and habituation; so the Truth, glorified is He, shortened the period of keeping company with wine; then came the prohibition and the command to avoid it and not to approach it. The parallel in our lives: we find someone who wants to give up smoking, who widens the time gap between one cigarette and another until he quits gently and removes it from his life entirely.

We find the Qur'an saying about wine: ﴿And from the fruits of the date palms and grapes you take intoxicant and good provision...﴾ [16:67] (Surat al-Nahl).

Here God bestows favour upon them with what He has provided for them; but people of discernment (ahl al-dhawq) notice that He did not describe wine as good provision, whereas He described the date and grape as good provision, because a person consumes them without corrupting them. Thus people of discernment notice that wine may afterward receive a ruling; then the Truth, glorified is He, sends down an admonition saying:

﴿They ask you about wine and gambling. Say: In them is great sin and benefits for people, but their sin is greater than their benefit...﴾ [2:219] (Surat al-Baqara).

Thus God clarified that the inclination of wine and gambling toward sin is greater than their inclination toward benefit. Then came after that His word with a preliminary ruling: ﴿Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you say...﴾ [4:43] (Surat al-Nisa').

This means that intervals between drinking wine should lengthen, so that no one drinks wine all day and part of the night; in this is training in turning away from wine. Then comes the complete prohibition of wine in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, intoxicants, gambling, idols and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful﴾ [5:90] (Surat al-Ma'ida).

Thus the ruling on the prohibition of wine took its gradual course suited to people's customs, and the prohibition of wine was accomplished gently and in stages.

Thus we understand abrogation as the ending in time of the former ruling and the beginning of the new ruling; this means that the first ruling had not been applicable to all time and then we removed it and brought another ruling; rather, the timing of the first ruling, predestined from eternity, had ended, and the new ruling began.

Thus there is no room for disagreement about the meaning of abrogation, since the Truth, glorified is He, referred erasure and affirmation to the Mother of the Book; in it is determined the appointed time of each ruling and its timing, and the time of the arrival of the ruling that follows it.

Since every matter is decreed from eternity, those who say that *al-bada'* (change of divine decision) is impermissible for God should note that this erasure and affirmation is not *bada'*; for *bada'* means that you do something, then it appears to you that it is corrupt, so you change it. The Truth, glorified is He, has not had the corruption of any ruling or verse become apparent to Him; rather, He decreed everything from eternity in the Mother of the Book, and made for each ruling an appointed time, a beginning and an end. The meaning of the word of the Truth, glorified is He, ﴿God erases what He wills and affirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾ [13:39] (Surat al-Ra'd) may be extended to include the abrogation of one message by another message; so He has erased something and affirmed something else, and every matter in which there is change for the better admits of erasure and affirmation, and it is from the presence of the Watcher, the Ready: ﴿Not a word does he utter but that with him is a watcher, ready﴾ [50:18] (Surat Qaf), that is: He is capable of commanding the Ready Watcher to record the obligations and prohibitions, and to leave aside permissible matters, and He is capable of erasing whatever sins He wills, and affirming whatever repentance He wills.

The Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 13, verse 40:

This verse defines the task of the Messenger (ﷺ), which is to convey the method of God. Whoever wills may believe, and whoever wills may disbelieve. However, the word of the Truth, glorified is He, concerning His Messenger (ﷺ) is:

﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is what you suffer; he is concerned over you and to the believers is kind and merciful.﴾ (Surah At-Tawbah, 128)

This statement made his concern tied to the guidance of all his people, and he hoped that all of them would be guided. Therefore, the Truth, glorified is He, says to His Messenger in another place:

﴿Then perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over them if they do not believe in this narration.﴾ (Surah Al-Kahf, 6)

That is: you are not responsible for their faith, and you should not grieve if they do not join the procession of faith. All that is upon you is to call them and convey to them the necessity of faith. The Truth, glorified is He, is the One who will hold them accountable, either in this world through destruction and humiliation, or in the Hereafter by their facing the punishment of the Fire.

When the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And whether We show you part of what We promise them or We take you [in death], your duty is only to convey, and upon Us is the reckoning.﴾ (Surah Ar-Ra'd, 40)

We know that every call to good grows greater day by day, and calls to evil fade day by day. The one who calls to good loves and longs to see the fruits of his call ripen, but the matter in some calls to good may require a time that exceeds the lifespan of the caller.

Therefore, the Truth, glorified is He, says to His Messenger (ﷺ):

﴿And whether We show you part of what We promise them or We take you...﴾ (Surah Ar-Ra'd, 40). That is: plant the call, and leave the one who picks the fruit to what comes after that, while you devote yourself only to planting. You will find that good and fruits come when God wills, whether He wills that during your lifetime or after your death.

If you look at the calls that life receives, you will find that every call has supporters or advocates, and that those who carry these calls have hastened to seek the fruit, although if they had been patient, so that those who come after them could pick it, those calls would have succeeded.

We in the countryside see the farmer planting, and through his planting we know his intentions: Is he working for himself, or working for those who come after him?

The one who plants wheat harvests quickly, faster than the one who plants a date palm or a mango tree, since the palm or mango tree does not bear fruit except after many years, sometimes reaching seven years. This is planted so that it will yield for the one who comes what it yielded for him of gold.

We eat from the dates that others planted for us, who have passed away, but they thought about those who would come after them. The one who does this must have a sufficient amount of land that he plants, because the one who does not own a sufficient amount of land thinks only of those he supports and of himself alone. Therefore, he plants only according to what the land can give him now.

As for the one who owns a sufficient amount of land and a generous soul, he is the one who has placed in his heart the responsibility of caring for those who will come after him, and to repay the favor that those who preceded him bestowed upon him, by planting for others who will come after him.

The call of Muhammad (ﷺ) testified that he did not seek for himself a quick fruit. Rather, we find the call facing difficulties upon difficulties, and the Prophet (ﷺ) bearing what he bore of hardship, exhaustion and effort, after he openly proclaimed the call to his closest kinsmen.

Then the call kept spreading among some clans and branches until the stronghold of disbelief fell, and Makkah became the sacred House of God as God willed. The whole Peninsula submitted to the method of God. The Prophet (ﷺ) sent letters to kings and emperors,

and all of them contained his saying (ﷺ): "Embrace Islam and you will be safe."

These letters showed that the Islamic call is a call extending to all people, in fulfillment of what the Truth said to His Messenger (ﷺ): that he is "a messenger to all mankind."

He, exalted is He, said:

﴿And We have not sent you except comprehensively to mankind, as a bringer of good tidings and a warner...﴾ (Surah Saba', 28)

People understood the difference between his message (ﷺ) and all the messages before, for to the people of 'Ad He sent Hud (peace be upon him). The Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And to 'Ad [We sent] their brother Hud...﴾ (Surah Al-A'raf, 65)

And He said about the people of Madyan:

﴿And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb...﴾ (Surah Al-A'raf, 85)

And He said about the mission of Musa:

﴿And a messenger to the Children of Israel...﴾ (Surah Al-'Imran, 49)

Thus the Truth, glorified is He, defined the time and place of the people of every message that preceded the message of Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah (ﷺ).

But the matter differs when He, glorified is He, sent Muhammad (ﷺ) as a messenger to all people. He, glorified is He, knew from eternity that this is the final religion (al-din al-khatim). Therefore He sent the Messenger of God to the rulers of the world contemporary with him, inviting them to enter the final religion.

The Messenger (ﷺ) left this task to those who would succeed him. He (ﷺ) called the Arabian Peninsula under the banner of "There is no god but God, and Muhammad is the Messenger of God," after they had been many tribes.

Each tribe did not bind itself to worship the god of another tribe, and each tribe did not bind itself to the legislation of the other tribe. They were never united, nor did they settle except in some villages, because most of them were nomadic Bedouins, each one carrying his tent on the back of his camel, moving in search of pasture (al-kala') and water for his sheep and livestock.

They had no national belonging, not to mention the tribes that fought among themselves in fierce feuds, and war between some tribes extended to forty years at some times.

The Prophet (ﷺ) was able to employ what they had of training, equipment and gear for the support of the religion of God. When he prepared for the military campaigns (ghazawat) or chose for the expeditions (sara'ya), he would find the fighters in full readiness. When he called them to war, he did not need to give them training, for all of them were already trained in fighting.

Thus the tribes became one nation after Muhammad, Messenger of God (ﷺ), united them in the unity of doctrinal completeness under the banner of Islam. This nation, the unlettered nation (al-ummah al-ummiyyah), concerning which the Truth, glorified is He, said:

﴿It is He who has sent among the unlettered a Messenger from among themselves...﴾ (Surah Al-Jumu'ah, 2)

This unlettered condition was an honour for them, lest it be said that they were a people who made a leap in civilization from a civilized nation. And this unlettered condition was striking, because the legislation that came to that nation stood before other nations, even to our time, in astonishment and appreciation.

The Truth, glorified is He, willed that this nation carry the message of heaven to the whole earth, after the Truth, glorified is He, had sent down:

﴿This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favour upon you and have approved for you Islam as a religion...﴾ (Surah Al-Ma'idah, 3)

Some people understood that the Messenger (ﷺ) was announcing his own death to his nation. After his departure (ﷺ) to the Highest Companion (al-Rafiq al-A'la), his companions spread the final religion throughout the entire world, and within half a century Islam had two wings: one wing in the East and one wing in the West. They defeated the two greatest contemporary empires: the empire of Persia with its civilization, and the empire of the Romans.

The lands were snatching Islam as a way of life. This happened after Islam fought the two empires at the same time, and people turned to Islam to verify its miracle, which they had felt in the character of those who heard the Qur'an and carried its message, and then in their discovery of the justice of the Qur'an in managing the movement of life.

Thus they discovered that the miracle of Islam is rational, and that its Messenger (ﷺ) is the final Messenger, who did not come to them with a sensory miracle. If the Qur'an was a miracle in language for the people among whom the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was sent, then the Qur'an for those who did not know the language of the Qur'an was a miracle in the justice and the values emanating from it.

People were rushing to Islam with the thrust of the believers and the pull of non-believers, when they saw that there is no difference between the leader and the least individual under its banner, and when they felt its justice and equality among human beings. Islam was not a miracle only for its own people, but for the whole world, and the saying of the Truth, glorified is He, is always realized:

﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth.﴾ (Surah Fussilat, 53)

We find a great thinker from the contemporary West declaring his Islam, although he had not read the Qur'an, but had only looked at the principles that Islam legislated, and how they carry solutions to what the successive civilizations and the people of laws in every land on earth had failed to achieve.

He knows that those laws came to a Messenger who belongs to a nation that excelled only in eloquence and literature, and that those laws provide solutions to problems that the whole world suffers from.

We saw how a man searched for the greatest hundred persons in human history, and how he made Muhammad (ﷺ) first among them. This researcher had not read the Qur'an, but he studied the effects of applying the Qur'an, and after he was attracted to the Qur'anic method, he found himself admiring the Qur'anic text.

An example: the study by Germans of the process of sensory perception: how a person feels pain, and how a person touches with his skin a smooth texture and is pleased by it, then touches something rough and is hurt by it.

The Germans continued studying this for years, in order to know the locus of sensation and its position in the human being, whether it is in the brain or elsewhere, until they concluded that the locus of sensation in every human being is in the skin, and that there are cells spread directly under the skin. The evidence is that when we insert a needle into a person's body, he feels pain only in the area of its entry, and nothing more. This drew the attention of one of the scientists, who said: "The Qur'an spoke of this when it said:"

﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins that they may taste the punishment. Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted in Might and Wise.﴾ (Surah An-Nisa', 56)

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on surah 13, verse 41:

The word "yarawa" (see) here means "ya'lamu" (know), but the verse did not say "ya'lamu," because knowledge may be knowledge of the unseen. "Yarawa" indicates that they have known what the verse reports as direct, witnessed knowledge and clear sight, not merely knowledge with the eye as a place-marker.

When the word of the Truth, glorified is He, reports a matter that happened in the past or will happen in the future, and we find in it the verb of seeing, this means that we must believe in it with the faith of one who witnesses it, because His word, glorified is He, is more certain than sight, and His knowledge is more certain than your eyes. The Truth, glorified is He, had already said to His Messenger: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?﴾ (Surah al-Fil, 105:1).

We know that the Prophet (ﷺ) was born in the Year of the Elephant, and it is not possible that he saw what happened to the companions of the elephant. Yet he affirmed what the true Word brought, as if it were a witnessed vision. The Truth, glorified is He, also said: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord extends the shadow? Had He willed, He would have made it still...﴾ (Surah al-Furqan, 25:45).

When the Qur'an speaks of an unseen matter, it uses the verb "yara" (see), such as the word of the Truth: ﴿If only you could see when the criminals hang their heads before their Lord...﴾ (Surah al-Sajdah, 32:12).

When the Qur'an speaks of a matter contemporary [to its audience], it says: ﴿Do they not see...﴾ (Surah al-Anbiya', 21:44).

And here the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Have they not seen that We come to the land, reducing it from its extremities...﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 13:41). This is speech addressed to those present and contemporary with them.

The definiteness of "al-ard" (the earth) here makes it unspecified, because when we wish to know "the earth," thought may turn to the ground on which we stand, and in the broader sense thought turns to the terrestrial globe on which all humankind live.

The earth may be attributed to a particular place in which some event occurred, such as the word of the Truth, glorified is He, about Qarun: ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home...﴾ (Surah al-Qasas, 28:81).

And the Truth, glorified is He, says about the whole earth: ﴿Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession in the land...﴾ (Surah al-Nur, 24:55).

Naturally, they will not take all the earth, but they will have authority over it. He, glorified is He, also says: ﴿So leave her to eat in Allah's earth...﴾ (Surah al-A'raf, 7:73).

Thus we understand that the word "al-ard" when applied to a place with a specific event refers to that place, but when used absolutely it means the whole earth, such as the word of the Truth: ﴿And the earth — He laid it out for the creatures﴾ (Surah al-Rahman, 55:10).

And like His word, exalted is He, to the Children of Israel: ﴿And after him We said to the Children of Israel: Dwell in the land...﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 17:104).

Although He said to them in another verse: ﴿Enter the Holy Land...﴾ (Surah al-Ma'idah, 5:21).

For this reason the Truth said in another place: ﴿And We divided them in the land into communities...﴾ (Surah al-A'raf, 7:168). That is: We made each fragment, with whatever cohesion it has, scattered apart from the other fragment. This is the condition of the Jews in the world: they live in special quarters in every country of the world, and so they have not melted into any society.

His word here: ﴿Have they not seen that We come to the land, reducing it from its extremities...﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 13:41) is addressed to the Quraysh. Authority had been theirs, and its seat was Makkah. Afterward they found that the situation changed from one day to the next: every day a tribe went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Madinah to declare its Islam and pledge allegiance to him. Thus the domain of unbelief diminished before their eyes, until they themselves declared their entry into Islam.

Thus the Truth, glorified is He, willed that the land of unbelief diminish and the land of faith increase, and they saw this with their own eyes, yet they did not take a lesson from what they saw before them: that the call was advancing and would never retreat, since land increases only through a person of authority established in it.

When the one of authority diminishes from the camp of unbelief by his position, he increases the expanse of faith, until there came what the Truth, glorified is He, spoke of: ﴿When the help of Allah and the victory come, and you see people entering the religion of Allah in multitudes, then glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness; indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance.﴾ (Surah al-Nasr, 110:1–3).

There are people sincerely devoted to the religion of Allah who try to demonstrate that the religion of Allah contains things indicating meanings not yet discovered. For example, immediately after humans ascended to the moon, they said: Allah clarified this when He said: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass. You will not pass except with authority...﴾ (Surah al-Rahman, 55:33).

They said: this is the authority of knowledge. But what do they say about His word after it: ﴿There will be sent against you a flame of fire and brass, and you will not be victorious﴾ (Surah al-Rahman, 55:35)?

Does that mean He permitted ascent by the authority of knowledge, as you claim?

To these people we say: we thank you for your attempt to link scientific phenomena with what came in the Qur'an. But where is the moon in relation to "the regions of the heavens and the earth"? It appears as an extremely small place in this vast universe. Where is it in relation to the star called Sirius, or to the cluster of bodies called the Chained Woman (Andromeda)? Indeed, where is it in relation to the galaxies that fill space?

When you look at the stars above you, you find that between you and them is a hundred light-years. If you intend to link the authority of knowledge with the Qur'an, you must take precaution, because if you were passing through by the authority of knowledge, the Truth, glorified is He, would not have said after it: ﴿There will be sent against you a flame of fire and brass...﴾ (Surah al-Rahman, 55:35).

If you ask: what is the benefit of the verse that relates this authority? It came because the Messenger had informed the people that he ascended to the heavens and was taken up, that is, he ascended and was taken up by the authority of Allah. And here the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Have they not seen that We come to the land, reducing it from its extremities...﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 13:41).

The word "atraf" (extremities) shows us that everything has a length and breadth by which its area is determined, and likewise it has a height by which its volume is determined. We know that any length has two ends, and if the thing is in the shape of a plane figure, its extremities correspond to the number of its sides. Since the Truth, glorified is He, says here: ﴿from its extremities﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 13:41), that is, from every point on the circumference of the circle is considered an extremity. This means that He, glorified is He, willed that the land of the disbelievers be constricted and that the land of the believers be widened from every direction surrounding the camp of unbelief. This statement indicates that it is a process newly occurring, and was not so before.

Then He, glorified is He, continues after that: ﴿Allah judges, and there is none to repel His judgment...﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 13:41). That is: the matter has been decided and its affair has ended. In our daily life we say: "This matter is finished, because the great leader has reviewed the ruling on it."

In the judiciary, we find that a verdict is issued by the court of first instance, then an appeal comes to confirm or reject the verdict, and it is not said that the appeal has "reviewed" the first verdict; rather it is said that it ruled such-and-such, either confirming or rejecting. How then about the judgment of One who does not forget and from whom nothing is hidden, and before whose judgment no one can review? The example of this is what the Truth, glorified is He, says about Solomon and David, peace be upon them: ﴿And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the field, when the sheep of a people grazed in it, and We were witness to their judgment. So We gave understanding of it to Solomon, and to each We gave judgment and knowledge...﴾ (Surah al-Anbiya', 21:78–79).

The origin of the story is that a dispute arose over sheep owned by one man, which trespassed into the cultivated field of another man. They brought the case to David, peace be upon him. David said: the owner of the sheep must hand them over to the owner of the field.

Our master Solomon, peace be upon him, was sitting listening to the discussion and said: No, rather the owner of the sheep must surrender his sheep to the owner of the land for a period of time, during which he takes their milk and benefits from them, until the owner of the sheep plants for him the same as what the sheep ate from his land.

The Truth, glorified is He, said: ﴿So We gave understanding of it to Solomon...﴾ (Surah al-Anbiya', 21:79).

This is the appeal. An appeal does not mean that a judge impugns the first judge; rather it seeks the essence of justice. Perhaps if the case were returned to the same first judge, he would issue the same ruling that the appeal issued after he explored all the circumstances surrounding it.

Here the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Allah judges...﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 13:41).

At the moment Allah issues a judgment, no appeal will come against it, and this is the meaning of His word: ﴿...there is none to repel His judgment﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 13:41).

This wise statement carries a foretelling of what the judiciary indicated by establishing the appeal: no one reviews the judgment of Allah, because the reviewer is presumed to be more alert than the one reviewed, and to have the capacity to notice what the first judge did not notice. There is no Sustainer (al-Qayyum) except Allah, and no one can know everything except Him, glorified is He. The affliction of every judgment is its execution. In our daily reality we find that whoever obtains a judgment suffers hardship in order to enforce it, because the one who issues the judgment differs from the one who enforces it: this one follows one authority, that one follows another. But the judgment issued by Allah is executed by His power, glorified is He, and there is no power at all besides Him. For this reason the word of the Truth comes: ﴿...and He is swift in reckoning﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 13:41). It is as if Allah, through this statement, alerts us that judgment with justice requires swift execution. We see in our daily life how one who holds a just right is worn down; if we executed judgments quickly, tranquility would prevail in the hearts of the members of society.

We find that the spread of tribal fanaticism in taking blood revenge arises only from delay in hearing cases, since hearing and judging a case takes years, which makes resentment grow. But if the judgment were executed immediately upon knowing the killer, while the outrage at the brutality of the crime was still fresh, blood feuds would not increase and souls would be calmed.

Here the Truth (al-Haqq), glory be to Him, informs His Messenger. Anyone who hears this message and surveys the procession of the earlier messages will find that every nation to which a messenger was sent schemed against him and plotted to nullify his claim, yet no scheme or plot that any nation devised was of any benefit to it, for all the messages were victorious.

Glory be to Him who said: ﴿God has decreed: "I shall surely prevail, I and My messengers."﴾ (Surah al-Mujadila, 21)

And He who said: ﴿And Our word has already preceded to Our servants, the messengers. Indeed, they would be the ones given victory. And indeed, Our soldiers – they will be the predominant.﴾ (Surah al-Saffat, 171–173)

When the Truth (al-Haqq), glory be to Him, states a ruling in the Qur'an, and He is the One who preserved this Qur'an, then no cosmic event will come to abrogate the Qur'anic ruling.

If you survey the processions of all the messengers, you will find this matter clear, just as Allah, glory be to Him, has affirmed it in the preserved Qur'an. He preserved it only because He is certain that cosmic events cannot transgress it.

Indeed, every nation schemed against its messenger, but to the Truth (al-Haqq), glory be to Him, belongs all scheming, and Allah's scheme is better for mankind than the schemes of all those nations. His scheme, glory be to Him, is the dominant one. If that happened with the earlier messengers, before you, O Messenger of Allah, then your situation must be different, because you were sent to all people, and no prophet will come after you.

All these matters were reassuring him, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, that his victory and the victory of his call are inevitable. He, glory be to Him, encompasses every scheme that any being may devise, and He, exalted and majestic, is able to nullify all of it.

He, glory be to Him, continues in the same verse: ﴿He knows what every soul earns, and the disbelievers will know to whom will be the final attainment of the [Home of the Hereafter].﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 42)

The Truth (al-Haqq), glory be to Him, knows what is hidden from eyes in the depths of creation, good or evil. He protects whomever He wills of His servants from the schemes of schemers, and He sends punishment upon the people of evil scheming against the messengers and the believers.

The disbelievers will surely know that their destiny is Hell, and how evil is the abode they will enter on the Last Day, in addition to the victory of His Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, in this world and their humiliation therein. Thus they will have received disgrace as their recompense in this world, and they will increase in knowledge of the reality of the punishment they will meet in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 13, verse 43:

We understand from the phrase ﴿You are not a messenger﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 13:43) that the disbelievers stop at rejecting the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him; as if all their hope is to deny that he is a messenger whom the Truth, glorified is He, has chosen for the final message. The proof is that they said:

﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man from one of the two cities?﴾ (Surah al-Zukhruf, 43:31)

And after that they said:

﴿O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down on us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment﴾ (Surah al-Anfal, 8:32)

That is, the idea of sending a messenger is acceptable to them, and what is unacceptable to them is the person of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, commands His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him: ﴿Say, "Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you, and [so is] whoever has knowledge of the Book"﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 13:43).

The witness, as we know, is one who confirms the ruling of the truth. When a matter arises in our worldly life on which we need a judgment, we bring the disputed matter before the judge, and he says: "Bring the witnesses."

The judge questions the witnesses in order to rule in light of the testimony. How much more so when the witness here is Allah, glorified is He? But then, will Allah bear witness, and to whom will He give His testimony, when they do not affirm the word of Allah that was sent down to His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him?

We say: Allah, glorified is He, sent him with the miracle that indicates the truth of his message in conveying from Allah, and a miracle is a breaking of the laws of the cosmos. Allah, glorified is He, made it a message in the hand of His Messenger and on his tongue; this means that He, glorified is He, has testified to his truthfulness.

A miracle is an extraordinary matter that Allah causes to appear at the hand of one whom He has declared to be His messenger, and it stands in the place of the statement: "My servant has spoken truly concerning what he conveyed from Me."

The intended meaning of a miracle is not the particular sense but its general sense. The example in the prominent miracles is clear: here is the fire into which they threw Abraham, peace be upon him. Had the aim been to save him from the fire, there would have been a thousand ways and means to do so, such as that the world should rain down, or that they should be unable to seize him. But the Truth, glorified is He, shows them afterward, after they had seized him, after they had bound him with chains, after they had thrown him into the fire, His command that the fire become coolness and safety for him, so that it does not burn him: ﴿We said, "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham"﴾ (Surah al-Anbiya', 21:69).

Thus the Truth, glorified is He, changed the law and broke it, so that the truthfulness of Abraham in what he conveys from Allah would become clear to them; for the breaking of the laws by the Truth, glorified is He, is the proof of the soundness of his message. And since the Truth, glorified is He, has said here, in the verse concerning which we are reflecting:

﴿And those who disbelieve say, "You are not a messenger." Say, "Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you"﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 13:43).

The testimony of the Truth, glorified is He, to His Messenger concerning the truthfulness of his conveying from Him is embodied in the fact that he, peace and blessings be upon him, grew up among them and spent forty years before he uttered a single letter carrying his message, or a sermon, or a poem; and the brilliance of genius cannot be delayed until forty.

The Truth, glorified is He, willed that the Qur'an should flow on the tongue of His Messenger at this age, so that Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, would convey it to all people; and this in itself is a testimony from Allah. He, glorified is He, adds here:

﴿and whoever has knowledge of the Book﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 13:43).

By "the Book" here is meant the Qur'an; whoever reads the Qur'an with care can see its inimitability in it; and whoever reflects on the meanings in it and examines its style finds in it a testimony to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. Or the intended meaning of His true words ﴿and whoever has knowledge of the Book﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 13:43) may be: those who know the report of the coming of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, from the Torah and the Gospel; because the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and his description are mentioned in those earlier books preceding the Qur'an, to the extent that 'Abdullah ibn Salam, who had been one of the rabbis of the Jews, said: "I recognized Muhammad when I saw him, as I recognize my own son, and my recognition of Muhammad is even stronger."

Therefore he went to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, my soul has inclined toward Islam, but the Jews are a people of slander; if I announce my Islam, they will revile me, curse me, and attribute to me qualities that are not in me. I want you to ask them about me first." So the Messenger of Allah sent for their chiefs and the great men among them; and they imagined that Muhammad might soften and give up his call. They came, and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to them: "What do you say about Ibn Salam?" They began to heap praise upon him and spoke the finest words about him.

Then Ibn Salam said: "Now, before you, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." They began to revile Ibn Salam; so Ibn Salam said to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him: "Did I not tell you that the Jews are a people of slander?"

We know that those among the People of the Book who rejoiced at what the Truth, glorified is He, sent down as revelation to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, were forty men from the Christians of Najran, thirty-two from Abyssinia, and eight from Yemen.

We know that those who denied the call of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used to forbid one another from listening to the Qur'an; and the Qur'an reports this about them when they said:

﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and talk over it loudly, that perhaps you may overcome﴾ (Surah Fussilat, 41:26).

This means they were certain that hearing the Qur'an affects the soul by awakening the fitrah, which yearns toward belief in it. As for those who have knowledge of the earlier books preceding the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, they know the report of his mission and his descriptions from their books.

The Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Those to whom We have given the Book recognize him as they recognize their own sons﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 2:146).

And He also says:

﴿So when there came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it; so the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 2:89).
